name: rp_pair_zscore_VNQ_IEF_120_2p0_4p0
rationale: Structural, not a track-record claim -- I assert nothing about how VNQ, IEF, listed real estate or any live strategy has recently performed. THE MECHANISM: a mean-reversion primitive needs a TETHER between its two legs and an identifiable economic agent who closes the gap; most UNIVERSE pairs have the first at best. This one has both, and both are measured in primary data rather than asserted. (1) THE TETHER IS THE DISCOUNT RATE. A listed REIT is a claim on property cash flows discounted at the 10-year Treasury yield plus a cap-rate spread, and IEF is a direct instrument on that same 10-year point. Nareit's own Q1 2026 data confirms the linkage is live rather than notional: the REIT IMPLIED cap rate is 5.89%, 169bp above the 10-year Treasury, and Nareit states explicitly that the REIT implied cap rate 'has reacted meaningfully to changes in the 10-year Treasury yield' while the private NCREIF ODCE APPRAISAL cap rate (4.44%, only 24bp over the 10-year) has not, having sat essentially unmoved at its year-end-2021 level for three years. So the log spread log(VNQ)-log(IEF) is, structurally, the listed property risk premium: the two legs share one dominant driver, and what is left over is the cap-rate spread. (2) THE AGENT WHO CLOSES THE GAP IS A TAKE-PRIVATE BUYER, not an abstract 'it should revert'. US REITs above $200M market cap closed Q1 2026 at a median 19.3% discount to consensus NAV; S&P Global counts four US REIT M&A deals totalling $16.77bn announced through 2026-04-15, three of them privatizations of public equity REITs, and ALL FOUR targeted companies trading at a significant discount to NAV, at 20-40% premiums to the unaffected share price. That is a real, capitalized bid that appears when listed pricing detaches from the private mark -- the closest thing this UNIVERSE offers to a mechanical restoring force behind a relative-value spread. THE SINGLE BIGGEST WEAKNESS, STATED FIRST RATHER THAN BURIED: the restoring force runs on a MULTI-QUARTER clock and this primitive cannot wait for it. Nareit puts the current public-private valuation divergence at 17 quarters and still open; an M&A process takes quarters to announce and close. pair_zscore normalizes against a trailing window capped at 120 trading days (~6 months), so what is actually under test is short-horizon reversion around a ROLLING mean, NOT convergence of the structural gap itself -- and a 17-quarter-old gap is precisely the kind that a rolling mean absorbs into its own baseline instead of trading against. If the only real reversion here lives at a horizon longer than the primitive can see, this should and will die on gate 1, and that is the honest prior going in. SECOND WEAKNESS: VNQ is equity and IEF is not, so the spread carries an unhedged equity-beta residual that no 1:1 log spread removes (this primitive fits no hedge ratio, unlike family N's regressed beta). A broad equity drawdown widens the spread with no REIT-specific dislocation behind it, and March 2020 -- listed REITs sold off hard while Treasuries rallied -- is the worst single realization available in the OOS window. It is exactly the realization that should kill this if the spread is really a levered equity bet wearing a relative-value label. THIRD, AGAINST MY OWN THESIS: the dislocation on offer has been SHRINKING, not widening -- the same median NAV discount was 8.7% by mid-2026 against 19.3% at Q1. A smaller gap means less for the mechanism to close, which is a reason to expect failure, not a caveat appended to a bullish case. I propose it anyway because waiting for a wider gap would be timing, and pre-registration is what stops that from being decided after the fact. DISTINCT FROM WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: no graveyard.csv row uses VNQ/IEF, and family N's six pre-registered cointegration pairs (GLD/SLV, TLT/IEF, EFA/EEM, SPY/QQQ, USO/DBC, LQD/HYG) do not include it -- so unlike most remaining pair candidates in this UNIVERSE, this one is not contraindicated by an already-failed ADF test. rp_static_spread_carry_VNQ_IEF_a touches the same two tickers under a DIFFERENT primitive and a different hypothesis -- a persistent premium in the spread's DRIFT versus reversion around its mean -- with its own name and its own separate verdict, the same distinction this ledger already drew between rp_static_spread_carry_LQD_IEF_a and rp_pair_zscore_LQD_IEF_120_2p0_4p0; neither borrows the other's evidence. PARAMETER CHOICES, each tied to the mechanism rather than tuned: z_window=120 is the LONGEST window the primitive offers, chosen because the dislocation is driven by quarterly NAV marks and multi-quarter deal processes -- a shorter window would normalize away the very deviation being traded. z_entry=2.0 / z_stop=4.0 are this lab's OWN already-pre-registered pair thresholds (family N, from Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst 2006's canonical 2-sigma construction), deliberately reused rather than searched over. freq=W because the signal's state changes on a ~6-month normalization against a multi-quarter mechanism: rebalancing daily would pay turnover the hypothesis never earns, and gate 1's null is duty-cycle-matched, so the candidate is charged for exactly that. BREADTH: pair_zscore is tied for least-proposed in this ledger (7 of 46 prior rows, against static_spread_carry's 10), and this is its first use of the real_estate asset class.

S&P Global Market Intelligence, 'US REIT M&A activity ramp-up extends into early months of 2026' (2026-04, spglobal.com) -- four US REIT M&A deals totalling $16.77bn announced through 2026-04-15, three of them privatizations of public equity REITs, all four targets trading at a significant discount to NAV; median NAV discount for US REITs above $200M market cap 19.3% at Q1 2026, narrowing to 8.7% by mid-2026; recent take-privates struck at 20-40% premiums to unaffected share prices. Family N's pre-registered pairs and Engle-Granger results (STRATEGIES.md) confirm VNQ/IEF is not among the six pairs already ADF-tested and dropped. name: rp_single_asset_trend_DBC_126
rationale: The broad commodity complex is currently in a deep low-inventory state, which is the precondition the theory of storage says makes a signed directional position on a commodity index economically different from a coin flip. The 2026 Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz disruption took an estimated ~5.5 mb/d of Middle East crude production offline on average during July 2026 -- more than 5% of global consumption -- and crude and refined-product curves returned to extreme backwardation after fighting resumed 2026-07-08; the Bloomberg Commodity Index's index-weighted implied carry was reported at +13% as of 2026-03-31 against a firmly negative -1.3% median since May 2011, and the broader complex (copper, platinum) is running physical deficits with global stockpiles and spare capacity eroding. Two mechanical consequences follow, neither of which is a claim about any strategy's recent performance: (1) when inventories fall far enough that convenience yield exceeds storage plus financing, curves invert and a long futures position earns a positive roll return instead of paying contango drag; (2) the same depleted buffer stocks are what normally damp a spot shock, so with them gone price moves propagate rather than being absorbed -- i.e. the sign of a trailing return carries more information about the next period in a low-inventory regime than in a well-supplied one. DBC is a futures-holding ETF whose Optimum Yield roll targets backwardated contracts, so both effects land directly in the price series engine.py loads, making this testable with spot ETF closes alone. A 126-day (~6 month) lookback matches the horizon over which inventory cycles resolve and spans the disruption regime that began in late February 2026; monthly rebalancing keeps turnover low for a slow-moving structural state. Distinct from the already-tested rp_single_asset_trend_USO_126 (single front-month WTI, no cross-commodity inventory channel) and from the DBC legs inside rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_TLT_DBC_252_60 and _VNQ_DBC_189_63, which use different lookbacks and are only ever held against an offsetting leg. Stated honestly against this lab's own record: every trend primitive tested here is DEAD, and backwardation can collapse back to contango quickly -- the pre-registered claim is narrowly that the inventory/roll channel is a structural reason a broad-commodity trend sign might carry information a pure price-trend does not, and the OOS gate decides.
citation: Mechanism: Gorton, Hayashi & Rouwenhorst (2013), 'The Fundamentals of Commodity Futures Returns', Review of Finance 17(1) -- inventories drive backwardation and the predictability of commodity futures returns (theory of storage, Kaldor/Working). Current conditions: CME Group, 'Implications of WTI Oil Futures In Backwardation Amid the Supply Crunch' and 'How Backwardation Generates Positive Roll Returns in Energy' (cmegroup.com/insights/economic-research/2026/) -- crude and refined-product curves in extreme backwardation since 2026-07-08, positive roll return to a rolled long position; S&P Global Market Intelligence, 'Commodity Price Watch: July 2026' -- ~5.5 mb/d of Middle East production offline on average in July 2026, >5% of global consumption, US-Iran MOU reopening Hormuz transit; Aberdeen Investments, 'Commodities June outlook: An illusion of abundance' (2026-06) -- global stockpiles declining and spare capacity eroding across oil and metals, disruptions absorbed via inventory drawdown; IBKR Campus, 'What does today's commodity market mean for broad allocations?' -- reports BCOM index-weighted implied carry of +13% at 2026-03-31 vs a -1.3% median since May 2011, and describes DBC's Optimum Yield roll methodology.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_20_4
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- and the honest reading of the mechanism's own literature argues the UNCONDITIONAL version of this trade should fail here, which is why that is stated up front rather than buried. THE MECHANISM. Cross-sectional short-horizon reversal is not a forecast of anything; it is the return to LIQUIDITY PROVISION. When non-informational order flow -- forced rebalancing, hedging demand, an outage-driven scramble for one asset -- displaces an asset's price relative to its peers, whoever takes the other side is paid a premium for absorbing it, and the premium is realised as the displacement decays. Nagel (2012, RFS 25(7)) establishes the two facts this proposal rests on: (a) reversal-strategy returns proxy for the returns to liquidity provision, and (b) that expected return is strongly TIME-VARYING and rises with market-wide volatility, as financially-constrained intermediaries withdraw liquidity supply and the price of supplying it goes up. Crucially, Nagel also finds that reversal formed from COARSE BASKETS (industry portfolios) does NOT earn high returns unconditionally, and only pays in high-volatility states. This lab's UNIVERSE is 15 broad ETFs -- coarser still than industry portfolios -- so the pre-registered expectation here is explicitly the conditional case, not the unconditional one. If the conditional premium is not large enough to survive DSR/CPCV over the full 2018+ OOS window, this dies, and that is the correct outcome. WHY THIS REGIME, NOW. The current setup is a supply-shock/dispersion regime, not a demand-cycle one: crude and refined products have returned to sharp backwardation on physical outages tied to Strait of Hormuz disruption (CME Group, 2026: WTI Jun-2026 at a $20.65 premium to Jun-2027), which is a scarcity-premium displacement concentrated in one asset class rather than a broad repricing. At the same time bond volatility is dormant (MOVE ~74.7) and HY OAS sits in its richest decile (~271-281bp) with the Fed easing -- so realised dispersion ACROSS asset classes is wide while dispersion WITHIN the rates complex is compressed. Multi-asset commentary going into 2026 (Vontobel, Goldman Sachs AM) frames rising cross-asset and cross-country dispersion driven by divergent fiscal policy and supply shocks as the defining feature of the regime. Dispersion is the raw material a cross-sectional rank needs: with near-zero dispersion, top-K and bottom-K are noise. WHY DOLLAR-NEUTRAL MATTERS HERE. Oxford Economics expects the stock-bond correlation to turn positive again in 2026 on supply shocks and activist fiscal policy, which impairs the channel the fair 60/40 benchmark relies on. A long-top-K/short-bottom-K book is dollar-neutral by construction and does not borrow that channel, so gate 3 (correlation to the benchmark) is a claim this shape can actually make. WHY THESE PARAMETERS, AND HOW IT DIFFERS FROM WHAT IS ALREADY IN THE LEDGER. lookback=20 is the FLOOR of the pre-registered range -- the closest this vocabulary gets to the roughly one-month horizon the reversal literature actually studies; anything longer is a valuation claim, not a liquidity-provision one. freq=D is the substantive choice and the first daily rebalance ever proposed for this primitive: the two prior reversal proposals in this ledger (rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_21_3 at M, rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_42_2 at W, neither of which has reached an OOS verdict) hold a position for a month or a week while the displacement they are formed on decays in days, so they cannot express this mechanism at all -- a monthly-rebalanced 21-day reversal is a different strategy from a daily-rebalanced 20-day one, not a neighbouring parameter. k=4 (long 4, short 4 of 15) is chosen for breadth: a liquidity premium is small per name, so it needs positions, and k=4 is the widest setting that still leaves a genuine middle of the ranking untraded. Note this is CROSS-SECTIONAL, distinct from the time-series str_reversal_* family (3d-23d) already dead in graveyard.csv, which reverses each asset against its OWN past rather than against its peers.
citation: Nagel, S. (2012), 'Evaporating Liquidity', Review of Financial Studies 25(7), 2005-2039 (https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/25/7/2005/1602153; NBER WP 17653) -- reversal returns as the return to liquidity provision, time-varying and predictable by volatility, and weak unconditionally for coarse baskets. Lehmann, B. (1990), 'Fads, Martingales, and Market Efficiency', QJE 105(1), for the original short-horizon cross-sectional reversal result. Current-regime facts: CME Group Economic Research (2026), 'Implications of WTI Oil Futures In Backwardation Amid the Supply Crunch' (https://www.cmegroup.com/insights/economic-research/2026/implications-of-wti-oil-futures-in-backwardation-amid-the-supply-crunch.html); Vontobel AM, '2026: Multi Asset Reloaded' and Goldman Sachs AM, 'Market Know-How 3Q 2026', on rising cross-asset/cross-country dispersion; Oxford Economics, 'Stock bond correlation will become positive again in 2026'.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_IEF_a
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- I assert nothing about how gold, Treasuries or any live strategy has recently performed, and the single strongest piece of evidence I found argues AGAINST this proposal, so it is stated first rather than buried. THE MECHANISM: official-sector reserve substitution. A central bank's FX reserve portfolio is a choice between a small number of substitutable stores of value, and the two largest are US Treasuries and gold. The World Gold Council's 2026 Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey (76 respondents, its largest ever) records that gold overtook US Treasuries by market value at end-2025 -- 27% of global official reserves versus 22% -- that central banks have bought an average of ~1,000t/yr over the past four years against a ~500t/yr average the preceding decade, that 89% expect global gold reserves to rise over the next 12 months, and that 74% expect LOWER US dollar holdings over the next five years. The stated motive has also changed in kind, not just degree: 84% now hold gold as a long-term store of value, while 'historical legacy' fell from 62% to 46% year over year. That is a price-INSENSITIVE, mandate-driven marginal buyer of one asset funded by a stated intent to underweight the other -- the shape static_spread_carry exists to express (an always-on structural risk-premium/flow bet, not a mean-reversion signal and not a trend forecast). WHY THE SHORT LEG IS IEF SPECIFICALLY, AND WHY IT IS NOT A LEVERED GOLD BET. Gold and nominal duration share one dominant driver: the real discount rate. Gold is effectively a zero-coupon perpetual real claim, so falling real yields lift it and lift IEF at the same time. Shorting the nominal-duration leg is therefore not decoration -- it removes the factor both assets already have in common and leaves gold's residual monetary/official-demand component, which is the only part the mechanism above actually speaks to. IEF rather than TLT because reserve portfolios are held for liquidity and are concentrated in the short-to-intermediate Treasury sector; the 20yr+ sector TLT tracks is dominated by pensions, insurers and leveraged accounts, not reserve managers, so IEF is the closest instrument in this UNIVERSE to the maturity bucket the substitution actually happens in. engine.py vol-targets each leg, so this is a relative claim between two vol-scaled sleeves, not an equal-notional bet dominated by gold's ~3x higher realised volatility. THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT AGAINST, FROM A PRIMARY SOURCE. IMF COFER for 2026Q1 shows the US dollar's share of allocated FX reserves ROSE to 57.13% from 56.42% in 2025Q4, with the IMF attributing roughly half of that increase to exchange-rate valuation effects -- and the IMF explicitly notes that gold overtaking Treasuries in 2025 was driven ALMOST ENTIRELY BY GOLD PRICE VALUATION EFFECTS, not by net selling of Treasuries. If the headline 27%-vs-22% crossover is mostly a price artefact of the very asset I am proposing to be long, then the crossover is a CONSEQUENCE of gold's repricing rather than evidence of a forward flow, and this spread is closer to an extrapolation of a past move than to harvesting a premium. That is the honest prior going in. THREE FURTHER WEAKNESSES. (1) MAGNITUDE ASYMMETRY: ~1,000t/yr is on the order of $100bn against a Treasury market measured in tens of trillions -- the flow is large relative to annual gold supply and negligible relative to the short leg's market, so the mechanism is lopsided and only one leg is really being pushed. (2) IT IS PUBLIC: a widely-published survey-documented flow is exactly the kind whose expected excess return should already be discounted into the level; static_spread_carry has no timing element whatsoever, so if the ratio already reflects a decade of this, forward return can be negative even while the flow continues exactly as described. (3) THIS LAB'S OWN RECORD: the one surviving carry-shaped strategy here (delta-neutral crypto funding) pays for bearing an identifiable, nameable tail risk. I cannot name the equivalent risk this spread is compensated for bearing, which makes it a relative-value directional view wearing a carry label -- a reason to expect DEAD, not a caveat appended to a bullish case. Gate 3 is a real hurdle regardless: gold's own 2012-2015 drawdown was roughly -45%, far worse than a 60/40's, and the short-IEF leg does not hedge that. DISTINCT FROM WHAT IS ALREADY IN THIS LEDGER. GLD/IEF appears under no primitive in pipeline_ideas.csv and no graveyard.csv row uses the pair. rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_UUP_a is gold versus the DOLLAR -- an FX-level claim about the currency itself -- whereas this is gold versus USD DURATION ASSETS, a reserve-composition claim with a different short leg and a different mechanism. rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_TLT_GLD_126_189 touches gold and Treasuries under a different primitive (two trend-following legs, no always-on position), at the long-bond maturity the substitution argument above specifically does NOT apply to; neither borrows the other's evidence. PARAMETERS. static_spread_carry has no fitted parameters by construction -- ticker_a=GLD as the accumulated asset, ticker_b=IEF as the diversified-away-from asset, long_leg='a' in the direction the documented flow runs, which is the only assignment the mechanism permits. freq=M because the state variable is a reserve-allocation decision reported and revised quarterly; a faster rebalance would pay turnover the hypothesis never earns, and gate 1's null is duty-cycle-matched so the candidate is charged for exactly that. BREADTH NOTE, STATED PLAINLY: static_spread_carry is the MOST-proposed primitive in this ledger (10 of 49 prior rows, against curve_carry's 7), so this proposal does not help vocabulary coverage. No primitive is heavily under-represented (the spread across all six is 7 to 10), curve_carry's only parameter is a lookback and 21/42/63/84/126/189/252 are already taken, and today's research pointed at an official-sector flow between two specific tickers rather than at the TLT/IEF curve -- so I chose merit over a one-count rebalance, per the stated preference-not-a-rule.
citation: World Gold Council, 'Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey 2026' (gold.org/goldhub/research/central-bank-gold-reserves-survey-2026), and WGC press release 'Central banks set to step up gold buying over the next year' -- 76 respondents (largest in the survey's nine-year history); gold surpassed US Treasuries by market value at end-2025 at 27% of global official reserves vs 22%; central banks bought an average of ~1,000t/yr over the past four years vs a ~500t/yr average the preceding decade; 89% expect global gold reserves to rise over the next 12 months; 74% expect lower US dollar holdings over the next five years; 84% cite long-term store of value as a reason to hold gold, with 'historical legacy' falling from 62% (2025) to 46% (2026). Reported via Kitco News, 'Record 45% of central banks plan to increase gold holdings, WGC survey finds' (2026-06-16). COUNTER-EVIDENCE, weighted deliberately: IMF COFER, 'Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves' data brief (data.imf.org) -- the US dollar share of allocated reserves ROSE to 57.13% in 2026Q1 from 56.42% in 2025Q4, with roughly half the increase attributable to exchange-rate valuation effects, and the IMF states that gold surpassing US Treasuries as a share of official reserves in 2025 was driven almost entirely by gold PRICE valuation effects and is not reflected in a declining COFER dollar share (COFER methodology revised from 2025Q3, unallocated reserves eliminated with revisions back to 2000Q1). Additional 2026 volume context: World Gold Council Gold Demand Trends Q2 2026 and CME Group, 'Precious Metals Outlook 2026' -- central bank purchases running at roughly 850t projected for 2026, with sustained multi-month official-sector accumulation. Mechanism (real-rate factor shared by gold and nominal duration, motivating the IEF short leg rather than an outright gold position): standard gold-as-zero-coupon-real-asset framing, e.g. Barro & Misra (2016), 'Gold Returns', Economic Journal 126(594).

name: rp_pair_zscore_HYG_IEF_120_1p75_5p0
rationale: HYG/IEF is the tradable form of the high-yield option-adjusted spread: HY OAS is quoted over Treasuries, so the HYG-vs-IEF log-spread proxies the credit risk premium itself more directly than HYG/LQD, which nets two credit instruments against each other. That premium is currently compressed to a structural extreme -- HY OAS ~271-281bp in early August 2026, the richest decile of its own history against a long-run median near 450bp, with IG at 81bp and bond volatility dormant (MOVE 74.7). This is a claim about the LEVEL of compensation for default risk, not about what has recently performed. pair_zscore is the conditional expression of it: flat near the mean, taking risk only when the spread is statistically extreme, unlike an always-on static_spread_carry which cannot express 'this premium is mispriced right now'. z_window=120 (top of range, ~6 months) because credit cycles mean-revert far more slowly than equity pairs and a short window would define 'unusual' against weeks of noise. z_entry=1.75 rather than higher because HY spread distributions are strongly right-skewed -- they spike wide and grind tight -- so the compressed side rarely reaches high z and a 2.0+ entry would leave a regime like today's untradeable. z_stop=5.0 for the same skew: HY OAS reached multiples of current levels in 2008 and 2020, so a tight stop exits at the crisis extreme rather than on genuine reversion failure. Identified decompression catalysts: energy is ~10% of the HY index with Brent near $91 on Middle East supply risk, and September brings the heaviest post-summer issuance calendar at minimal concessions. Prior is that this dies like everything else here (pairs/cointegration is already DEAD across six pre-registered pairs); the credit-premium-level pair has not been tested against the gates in this form.

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_QQQ_USO_200_40
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- nothing below asserts that trend-following, commodities, tech or any live strategy has recently performed well; every input is a statement about the current transmission structure between two shock channels. THE MECHANISM, NAMED SPECIFICALLY (required by this primitive, which will not accept 'these two happen to be uncorrelated'): the QQQ leg and the USO leg sit on opposite ends of ONE causal chain -- crude oil is the principal transmitter of inflation shocks into the 10-year real yield, and the 10-year real yield is the dominant valuation variable for the longest-duration equity claim in this UNIVERSE. QQQ's cash flows are the most distant of any UNIVERSE equity ETF, so its multiple is disproportionately a discounted-value function of the real rate; an energy-led inflation impulse raises breakevens and term premium, lifts the real discount rate, and de-rates exactly that multiple, while the same impulse is what a crude trend leg goes long into. Run the chain the other way and it still holds: a disinflationary crude decline lowers the real discount rate and re-rates QQQ upward while the crude trend leg is short. That is a directional, checkable transmission claim -- not a correlation search. WHY THE HEDGE LEG IS A COMMODITY AND NOT DURATION, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF PICKING THIS PAIR NOW. The textbook offset for an equity-duration shock is nominal duration (TLT/IEF), and that offset is structurally impaired in the current regime: Oxford Economics' 2026 work argues the stock-bond correlation returns to POSITIVE territory in 2026 and that the pre-Covid regime of weakly pro-cyclical inflation does not sustainably return, with continued supply shocks, geopolitical risk and more activist fiscal policy pushing term premia higher. When the correlation is positive, a rates leg does not offset an equity-duration shock -- it SHARES it, because both legs are then being driven by the same inflation/term-premium factor. So the hedge for long-duration equity has to come from the asset class that is the SOURCE of that factor rather than another victim of it. This is also why the pair is admissible under the primitive's asset-class rule for a real reason and not merely a bookkeeping one: QQQ resolves to equity, USO to commodity. WHY USO RATHER THAN DBC. DBC is a diversified basket whose energy exposure is diluted by metals and agriculture and whose optimised roll rule deliberately blunts the front of the curve; the inflation-transmission channel argued above is specifically CRUDE, so the pure front-month WTI instrument is the sharper expression of the stated mechanism, not a broader-is-better diversifier claim. A SECONDARY, PARTIAL AND DELIBERATELY NOT OVERSOLD POINT ON THE USO LEG. USO holds and rolls front-month WTI, so its price series -- which is what engine.load_prices() sees -- mechanically embeds roll yield. The WTI curve is currently backwardated (CME Group's 2026 'Implications of WTI Oil Futures In Backwardation Amid the Supply Crunch'; a gently backwardated Brent strip running from roughly USD 79/bbl for Oct-2026 down toward USD 69-70/bbl by 2029 as of early August 2026), which means a LONG USO position is roll-yield-supported while held. I am not counting this as carry, because this primitive takes both signs via sign(): the same structure that pays the long side charges the short side symmetrically. It is a reason the long half of the leg is cheaper to hold, not an edge. PARAMETERS AND WHY. lookback_a=200 for QQQ: the equity-duration re-rating this argument describes is a multi-quarter repricing of a discount rate, and ~200 trading days is the horizon over which the AI-capex investment cycle driving that duration actually turns (PIMCO, 'AI Financing Needs Do Not Override Cyclical Drivers of Yield', argues AI financing needs do not override the cyclical drivers of yields -- i.e. the rate channel stays the operative one). lookback_b=40 for USO: roughly two months, the horizon over which crude's inventory/term-structure state actually re-prices, and deliberately much shorter than the equity leg so the two legs are not the same trend measured twice -- which is also what should let them clear this primitive's calibration-window correlation cap on merit rather than by luck. freq=W: the faster leg is 40 days, so weekly rebalancing gives ~8 rebalances per lookback while paying far less turnover than daily, and gate 1's null is duty-cycle-matched so the candidate is charged for exactly the trading it does. name: rp_single_asset_trend_EFA_252
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM. Nothing below asserts that trend-following, international equity, or any live strategy has recently performed well; the inputs are official-sector reserve-composition data and the mechanical construction of the instrument. THE MECHANISM. EFA is an UNHEDGED USD share class over developed ex-North-America equities, so the price series engine.load_prices() actually sees decomposes into two additive return sources: the local-currency equity return, and a pure FX translation term (EUR/JPY/GBP/AUD vs USD). The hypothesis is specifically about the SECOND term. The dollar's share of allocated global FX reserves fell below 57% for the first time since 1995 -- 56.9% in Q3 2025, down from a 72% peak in 2001 -- and central banks have now bought more than 1,000 tonnes of gold in each of three consecutive years as the reallocation counterparty. That is an official-sector flow with two properties ordinary FX flow does not have: it is price-INSENSITIVE (a reserve manager rebalancing a mandated currency weight does not stop because the dollar got cheaper, which is what normally arbitrages a drift away) and it is administratively SLOW (reserve composition targets move on multi-quarter committee cycles and are reported quarterly through IMF COFER). A price-insensitive, slow, one-directional flow is the textbook generator of DRIFT rather than mean reversion. So the testable claim is that EFA's USD-denominated series carries a persistent additive component that a trend-sign signal can hold, and that this makes single-ticker trend behave differently on an unhedged foreign-currency claim than on the domestic assets where this lab has already killed it. WHY EFA AND NOT EEM. Both are unhedged, but EEM's currency basket is dominated by managed and partially-pegged regimes whose central banks actively suppress exactly the drift this argument depends on; EAFE's are freely floating majors, which are the currencies reserve managers actually hold, so the flow described above lands in EFA's FX term directly rather than being absorbed by an intervention desk. WHY NOT UUP DIRECTLY. UUP is the pure expression of the dollar leg and has already been proposed (rp_single_asset_trend_UUP_63, 2026-08-06). EFA is a deliberately different bet: it pairs the same FX drift with a positive-expected-return equity claim underneath it, so the signal is not asked to earn its keep from FX alone. PARAMETERS AND WHY. lookback=252 (top of the pre-registered range, ~12 months) because the flow's own clock is the binding constraint -- COFER is quarterly, the reserve-share decline being cited spans 2025 into 2026, and a shorter window would measure the equity leg's noise rather than the currency leg's drift. I am choosing this horizon from the mechanism's timescale, not shopping it. freq=M because a signal built from a multi-quarter structural flow has no business rebalancing faster than monthly; gate 1's null is duty-cycle-matched so the candidate is charged for exactly the trading it does, and monthly is where a 252-day signal's turnover is honest. THE HONEST CASE AGAINST, STATED IN FULL. (1) 252/monthly IS the canonical TSMOM specification this lab has already killed. tsmom_12m and tsmom_ensemble are both DEAD in graveyard.csv, engine.py pins LOOKBACK=252 with an explicit 'do NOT tune this', and seven of the eight prior single_asset_trend proposals are already DEAD (GLD 126, SLV 63, VNQ 126, EEM 189, USO 126, TLT 126, and DBC 126 pending). The ONLY genuinely new thing here is the unhedged-FX-composite channel; if that channel is not real, this is a restatement of a dead hypothesis on a fifteenth ticker and should die identically. My prior is DEAD. (2) THE MECHANISM IS SLOWER THAN THE OOS WINDOW CAN RESOLVE. Reserve share moved roughly 15 percentage points over 25 years; even if the drift is entirely real, its per-year contribution is small relative to EAFE equity volatility, so the FX term may simply be undetectable at the sample size gate 1 has -- an argument that the effect could be real AND the verdict correctly DEAD. (3) THE DRIFT IS NOT MONOTONIC. The dollar index strengthened over the twelve months into June 2026 on rate expectations even while reserve share kept falling, which is the direct counterexample: tactical FX and structural reserve diversification are different clocks, and a trend signal reads the tactical one. The cited sources make exactly this caveat themselves and I am not arguing past it. (4) A LONG-ONLY VERSION OF THIS IS ALREADY A SURVIVOR HERE. Diversified buy-and-hold is one of only two things alive in this lab and already owns international equity beta; for this candidate to add anything, the trend SIGN has to carry information beyond simply being long, which gate 2's diversification test is well placed to reject. DISTINCTNESS. EFA has never been proposed under single_asset_trend, appears in only 2 of the 52 prior pipeline_ideas.csv rows (both as a hedge leg), and no graveyard.csv row uses it. BREADTH NOTE, STATED PLAINLY. single_asset_trend stands at 8 of 52 prior rows against curve_carry's 7, so this does not improve primitive-level coverage by one count. curve_carry's sole parameter is a lookback and 21/42/63/84/126/189/252 are already taken (three already DEAD), leaving only gap-filling draws; today's research pointed at an FX/reserve-composition mechanism that curve_carry -- hard-wired to the FRED Treasury slope and the TLT/IEF pair -- cannot express at all. Per the stated preference-not-a-rule. Today's other three proposals used static_spread_carry, pair_zscore and asset_class_trend_hedge, so this is a fourth distinct primitive for the day.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_HYG_TLT_a
rationale: Structural, not a track-record claim -- I assert nothing about how high yield, long Treasuries or any live strategy has recently performed, and no timing view is expressed: static_spread_carry holds a FIXED, always-on position, so the hypothesis under test is only whether a persistent risk premium exists across the whole OOS window, never whether now is a good entry. THE PAIRING THIS LEDGER HAS NOT YET EXPRESSED. The eleven prior static_spread_carry proposals cover the term premium alone (TLT/IEF), the credit QUALITY-TIER differential (HYG/LQD), the investment-grade credit premium against duration-matched Treasuries (LQD/IEF), the property/cap-rate premium (VNQ/IEF, GLD/IEF), size (IWM/SPY), EM (EEM/EFA), the commodity front-of-curve roll (USO/DBC, SLV/USO), the metals split (SLV/GLD) and the official-sector reserve rotation (GLD/UUP). None of them pits the HIGH-YIELD credit premium directly against the LONG-END term premium. Long HYG / short TLT is the only pair this UNIVERSE can form that does, and no graveyard.csv row uses HYG at all (456 rows checked); family N's six pre-registered cointegration pairs (GLD/SLV, TLT/IEF, EFA/EEM, SPY/QQQ, USO/DBC, LQD/HYG) do not include it, so this candidate is not contraindicated by an already-failed ADF test. THE MECHANISM, and why the short leg is TLT rather than IEF. Both legs are compensation for bearing a different risk: HYG pays a spread over Treasuries for default, downgrade and illiquidity risk on ~3-year paper; TLT pays a term premium for bearing long-end duration. Shorting the Treasury leg strips out the risk-free rate common to both, so what is left is the DIFFERENCE of the two premia -- the honest question being 'does the high-yield credit premium exceed the long-end term premium unconditionally, 2018-present?' The long-end leg is the right one because the structural repricing my research turned up is concentrated there specifically, not in the belly: the ACM 10-year term premium (ACMTP10) stood at +0.51% in June 2026 after roughly five years near or below zero, and the driver named in the primary reporting is issuance composition rather than growth -- Treasury has run the bill share hot (the 4-week bill now averages ~$94bn per offering in 2026 against ~$47bn a decade ago), deferring the coupon supply that ultimately has to clear against a shrinking pool of duration buyers. The August 2026 quarterly refunding is $125bn ($58bn 3yr / $42bn 10yr / $25bn 30yr) refunding ~$96.3bn of maturing privately-held notes and bonds, i.e. ~$28.7bn of new cash raised from private investors in one refunding. That is a supply/demand imbalance in duration compensation, measurable and slow-moving, and TLT is this UNIVERSE's only instrument on it. THE SINGLE BIGGEST WEAKNESS, STATED FIRST RATHER THAN BURIED: on current pricing BOTH blades of this spread move against it. The premium it harvests is priced near the thinnest it has ever been -- ICE BofA US High Yield OAS (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2) was 271bp on 2026-08-06, roughly 30bp above the series' all-time low of ~241bp set in June 2007, a famously bad moment to have been long credit risk -- while the premium it PAYS AWAY on the short leg has moved the other way, from deeply negative to +0.51% and structurally rising on the issuance grounds above. So the ex-ante spread between the two premia is compressed from both ends simultaneously. This is a reason to expect the candidate to FAIL, and it is the honest prior going in. I propose it anyway because waiting for a wider spread would be timing, and this primitive cannot time -- a fixed always-on spread either earns an unconditional premium across 2018-present or it does not, and that is precisely the question worth one pre-registered test. SECOND WEAKNESS, and the structural one: the two legs are NOT independent bets. In a flight to quality, credit widens and long Treasuries rally, so both legs lose at once and the spread is effectively a levered short-crisis position rather than a hedged one. March 2020 is the worst single realization available in the OOS window -- HYG sold off hard while TLT rallied hard, and HYG additionally traded at a discount to NAV until the Fed's corporate-credit facilities were announced. 2018Q4 is a smaller version of the same shape. If the average premium does not survive those drawdowns net of costs, this should and will die on gate 3 or on gate 2's Calmar test. The favourable realization is 2022, when the long end fell far harder than credit widened -- I name it for symmetry, not as an expectation. THIRD, MECHANICAL HONESTY ABOUT WHAT THE POSITION ACTUALLY IS: this pair is deliberately NOT duration-neutral, unlike LQD/IEF. HYG's effective duration was 2.99 years at 2026-06-30 against this repo's own frozen TLT_DURATION=16.0 (src/tradefabe/pipeline.py), and engine.py vol-targets EACH leg to TARGET_VOL on a trailing window rather than holding fixed notionals, which scales the legs to comparable risk contribution but does not equalize DV01 -- TLT's higher volatility means it receives the smaller notional, leaving the position net SHORT duration and net LONG credit. That is the intended exposure, not a residual: being net short duration is how the position pays the term premium away, which is half the hypothesis. It also means the candidate carries an equity-like beta through HYG that no fixed-weight spread removes. CARRY, since this lab's one survivor is a carry book and the comparison should be made explicitly rather than implied: the running carry here is POSITIVE but is NOT a mechanically paid rate. HYG's yield to maturity was 9.75% on 2026-08-04 (30-day SEC yield 6.51% at 2026-06-30) against a long-end Treasury yield in the low-5s, so the gross accrual differential is real -- but high-yield spread income arrives net of realized defaults and downgrades that are small, lumpy, and correlated with exactly the episodes that hurt the position, and HYG charges 0.49%/yr against it. That is a materially weaker structural claim than crypto funding carry's mechanically-paid rate, and it should be read as a reason the candidate may deserve to die rather than as a caveat appended to a bullish case. PRIMITIVE-CHOICE HONESTY: static_spread_carry is the most-proposed primitive in this ledger (11 of 53 prior rows) so this is deliberately not a breadth pick, and I checked the under-used ones first. curve_carry is the least-proposed (7) but is fixed to TLT/IEF, reads no credit data at all, and its single parameter is already sampled at 21/42/63/84/126/189/252 across a (20,252) range -- an eighth lookback would be grid-filling, which is the factory's job, not this routine's. cross_sectional_rank (8) ranks the whole cross-asset UNIVERSE and cannot express a two-premium difference. The mechanism here is a fixed spread, so no under-used primitive can carry it. freq=M because the position is fixed: the only turnover is the monthly rebalance back to vol-target weights, and monthly is the lowest-turnover clock this primitive offers -- which matters directly, because gate 1's null is duty-cycle-matched and is charged the same trading costs the candidate is.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_momentum_105_1
rationale: PRIMITIVE CHOICE, and why not curve_carry. cross_sectional_rank has 8 of pipeline_ideas.csv's 54 prior proposals against static_spread_carry's 12, and its THREE-dimensional (metric x lookback x k) space is by far the least-covered per draw in the vocabulary. curve_carry is nominally the least-used (7) but is a ONE-parameter primitive whose pre-registered (20, 252) range has already been sampled at 21/42/63/84/126/189/252 across six separate term-premium rationales -- an eighth draw there fills a gap in an already-mined space rather than adding information, so the under-representation preference is better served here. STRUCTURAL SETUP -- about DISPERSION MAGNITUDE, and direction-free. This primitive's mechanism requires exactly one precondition to have anything to harvest: the trailing-return spread between the top-K and the bottom-K of the UNIVERSE must be wide enough that the long and short legs do not cancel. That precondition is currently at an extreme, and at the cross-ASSET level this 15-ETF universe actually ranks over, not merely inside equities. Through 2026-07-31 the broad commodity complex sits ~+39% YTD against US equities ~+10.5% and a bond complex far behind, with the commodity block itself internally split -- crude ~+87% YTD on the Strait of Hormuz blockage while GOLD LAGS on a firmer dollar. A ~29-point gap between the best and worst asset-class blocks, plus a split INSIDE the leading block, is the wide and non-degenerate rank ordering this primitive needs; in a compressed-dispersion regime the identical signal trades costs for noise. WHY THE ORDERING SHOULD PERSIST RATHER THAN CHURN -- the real hypothesis under test. The dominant driver is a PHYSICAL supply constraint (a blocked shipping lane), not a sentiment rotation. A constraint of that kind resolves on a logistics/geopolitical clock measured in quarters and re-prices the affected assets against everything else for as long as it binds, so the rank order it produces is slow-moving. That is a claim about the PERSISTENCE OF THE RANKING, not a forecast that any particular ticker keeps rising: both legs' membership and sign are computed mechanically from trailing returns and I assert no view on which assets occupy which end. PARAMETERS. metric=momentum because the persistence argument above IS a momentum claim and no other metric in the set expresses it -- the named mechanism is the reason, never any strategy's record. lookback=105 (~5 months) spans the 2026 shock without reaching back into the materially different 2025 regime, and is untested; the three prior momentum draws sit at 63/126/252, all monthly. k=1 is the point of this proposal and has NEVER been drawn (prior k values: 2, 3, 4): today's dispersion is concentrated at the EXTREMES rather than spread evenly across the 15 names -- one asset near +87%, another commodity lagging outright -- so a wide K dilutes the book into the thin middle of the ranking where the spread is smallest. k=1 is the configuration that actually harvests extreme dispersion, and it sits at the boundary of the pre-registered (1, 7) range. freq=W rather than the M every prior momentum draw used: a supply constraint can lift abruptly, and a monthly book stays stale for up to a month at exactly the point the rank order can turn over. HONEST LIMITATION, stated rather than papered over. The most-cited 2026 dispersion evidence -- S&P 500 cross-sectional volatility more than five standard deviations above its long-term average, 10 of 11 sectors below their long-run correlation averages -- is SINGLE-STOCK dispersion inside the equity block and does NOT transfer to a 15-ETF cross-asset universe; it is corroborating regime context only. The load-bearing fact here is the cross-ASSET return spread above. I make no claim about how any live strategy, fund or factor has recently performed. The hypothesis it tests is therefore narrow and checkable -- does the Treasury slope move in PERSISTENT regimes, or does it chop? Today's setup is the sharpest statement of that question the OOS window has offered, because the slope's two ends are now driven by two DIFFERENT forces on two DIFFERENT clocks, pulling in OPPOSITE directions. (a) THE LONG END IS STEEPENING on term-premium / inflation-risk compensation: the 10-year moved from under 4.40% in late June to 4.65% by 2026-08-10, and the reporting attributes it to investors repricing longer-run inflation risk and demanding more compensation for holding longer-term bonds -- a supply/credibility channel, not a growth channel. A short lookback measures the news clock and gets whipsawed by exactly this kind of eight-week round trip; a lookback long enough to span a full policy cycle measures the drift instead. 147 trading days is ~7 months, roughly five FOMC meetings -- the shortest horizon that contains a complete decision cycle rather than a single repricing episode. name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_USO_IEF_63_168
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM. Nothing below says that trend-following, commodity strategies, or any live fund has recently performed well. Every input is a physical quantity, a price level, a policy fact or a published correlation study -- never a strategy return. THE MECHANISM. asset_class_trend_hedge holds two INDEPENDENT trend legs, each long or short by the sign of its own trailing return, and the primitive's own requirement is that the two legs come from different asset classes AND that a specific mechanism, not a correlation search, explains why they offset. Mine: the two legs sit on OPPOSITE SIDES OF THE INFLATION AXIS, and their trends are set by two different physical/institutional clocks. Leg A (USO, commodity) is driven by barrels -- OPEC+ quota decisions and Middle East transit risk, which move on a meeting-and-headline clock of weeks to a quarter. Leg B (IEF, rates, 7-10y) is driven by the Fed's policy path, which moves on an FOMC/CPI clock of six-to-twelve months and only responds to oil with a long pass-through lag. The OFFSET claim is specifically this: whichever way the shock runs, the signed legs end up on opposite sides of it. In a SUPPLY/INFLATION shock, oil trends up and duration trends down, so the candidate is long USO and short IEF. In a GROWTH/DEMAND shock, oil trends down and duration rallies, so it flips to short USO and long IEF. Neither state is a levered bet on one factor; the pair is always straddling the inflation axis rather than doubling down on it. That is also why I expect the signals to decorrelate mechanically rather than merely economically -- the legs measure different clocks (63 vs 168 days) on different drivers, which is what a low trend-sign correlation IS. WHY NOW, AND WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE PARAMETER CHOICE. The current setup is the cleanest live statement of the two-clock structure the OOS window has offered. (a) The BARREL CLOCK is running fast and is supply-side, not demand-side: the market is short roughly 1.8 mb/d this quarter on the Iran/Strait of Hormuz disruption, with WTI near $84 on 2026-08-12 after closing at $82.13 on 2026-08-10, and prices re-rating on individual diplomatic setbacks -- a headline-driven, quarter-scale regime, which is what a 63-day lookback measures. (b) The POLICY CLOCK is running slow and in the opposite direction: the Fed held at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth consecutive meeting in July 2026 with THREE dissents preferring a 25bp increase, and a September HIKE is now the market-centered outcome, explicitly framed as a response to energy-driven inflation. A policy turn from cuts to hikes is a multi-meeting object; 168 trading days is ~8 months, ~6 FOMC meetings, the shortest horizon that contains a complete turn rather than one repricing. I am choosing both lookbacks from their mechanisms' timescales, not from a grid. (c) The regime this describes -- an energy-led inflation shock -- is exactly the one the stock-bond correlation literature identifies as the state where duration stops hedging and stocks and bonds fall together, i.e. where a rates leg is NOT interchangeable with an equity leg. That is the specific reason to pair a commodity leg with a RATES leg here rather than the equity/commodity pairings this ledger already holds. THE HONEST CASE AGAINST, STATED IN FULL. (1) MY PRIOR IS DEAD. Every predictive strategy this lab has tested is dead against pre-registered kill rules, and that includes the closest neighbours to this one: single_asset_trend on USO at 126 days and on TLT at 126 days are both already proposed here, and the two existing commodity-touching asset_class_trend_hedge draws (TLT/DBC 252/60, QQQ/USO 200/40) test the same family of claim. If trend on either leg is noise, combining two noisy legs produces a noisier candidate, not a better one. (2) USO IS NOT CLEAN OIL EXPOSURE. It holds front-month futures and pays the roll; across most of the 2018-2026 OOS window the curve was in contango, and the 2020 episode mangled the fund's structure outright. A long leg bleeds roll in contango even when spot oil is flat, and the current backwardation that would help it is a feature of TODAY, not of the window the verdict is computed on. This is the single most likely reason the candidate dies. (3) THE STRUCTURAL STORY IS ABOUT NOW; THE VERDICT IS ABOUT 2018-2026. One month of Hormuz risk premium cannot make a signal work across eight years. The research legitimately motivates WHICH pair and WHICH horizons to test and nothing more; it is not evidence the candidate passes. (4) THE DECORRELATION GUARD MAY REJECT IT, and I would rather say so than pretend otherwise. On 2007-2017 calibration data IEF's 168-day trend sign was positive through most of a secular bond bull market, which dampens its correlation with anything; but oil's two big crashes (2008, 2014-16) coincided with flight-to-quality bond rallies, which pushes the trend-sign correlation negative. If |corr| exceeds the 0.3 cap the screen should and will kill this, and that is the guard working, not a bug in the idea. (5) TWO LEGS, TWO CHANCES TO WHIPSAW. A sign-flip signal near a flat trend churns, and freq=W charges turnover on both legs; the duty-cycle-matched null prices exactly that trading. PRIMITIVE-CHOICE HONESTY. asset_class_trend_hedge stands at 9 of the 56 prior rows in this ledger, tied with pair_zscore, cross_sectional_rank and single_asset_trend, against 12 for static_spread_carry and 8 for curve_carry. curve_carry is nominally the least-used, but it was taken by the immediately preceding run (rp_curve_carry_147, 2026-08-13) and its one-dimensional (20, 252) space is now sampled at eight points, so a ninth draw would be gap-filling rather than exploration. The commodity-vs-rates corner of asset_class_trend_hedge is genuinely under-explored by contrast: its only prior rates-leg-plus-commodity draw is TLT/DBC, and TLT is a term-premium instrument against a broad commodity basket, whereas IEF is a policy-path instrument against a single, supply-shocked energy leg -- a different claim on both sides, not a reparametrization. This is today's FIRST proposal (slot 1 of 10; zero rows in this ledger carry a 2026-08-14 UTC date), so it is not steering around anything proposed earlier today. freq=W because the faster leg's driver updates on a headline/OPEC clock of weeks and the slower leg's on the FOMC calendar; daily rebalancing would pay costs for noise the 63-day signal cannot resolve. name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_252_3
rationale: Structural claim only -- I assert nothing about how any strategy, live or backtested, has recently performed, and no direction is forecast: cross_sectional_rank's positions are mechanical from the ranking, not chosen by me. THE MECHANISM, AND WHY IT NEEDS A PRECONDITION THIS LAB HAS NEVER HAD. Long-horizon cross-sectional reversal (De Bondt-Thaler overreaction -- the extremes of a multi-quarter ranking revert) is a different hypothesis in kind from the short-horizon reversal this lab has already killed many times over. EVERY reversal ever tested here is <= 40 trading days: str_reversal_3d/5d/10d/15d/20d plus ~36 str_reversal_gen_* factory draws, all DEAD, and the three prior pipeline cross-sectional reversal proposals at lookback 20, 21 and 42. Those all test a LIQUIDITY/microstructure mechanism -- fade the inventory move, collect the accommodation premium. A 252-day reversal tests an OVERREACTION mechanism, and overreaction requires something to have been overreacted TO: a large, identifiable, and physically TRANSITORY shock. Absent one, a long-horizon contrarian ranking is just short momentum, and cross-sectional momentum is already DEAD here. So the entire hypothesis rests on one checkable precondition -- does the last 12 months of cross-asset dispersion in this UNIVERSE have an identifiably transitory driver? WHY THAT PRECONDITION IS MET RIGHT NOW, SPECIFICALLY. 2026's dispersion across this universe is dominated by ONE nameable physical event rather than a diffuse set of independent drivers: the Strait of Hormuz disruption from roughly 2026-03-01. It moved every block at once and in opposite directions. Commodities: prompt WTI near $99/bbl in April with the curve in steep backwardation (M1-M2 ~$3.02/bbl, M1-M12 ~$15/bbl, Dec-2026 trading as much as $40 below the front). Inflation: headline CPI 3.8% y/y in April, highest since May 2023, on a ~17.9% energy surge. Rates: the Fed's response produced a bear FLATTENING, 2s10s compressing from its early-February 2026 wide to ~45bp while the 30y set cycle highs at 5.19-5.24%. That is the precondition being demonstrated, not asserted. AND THE SHOCK IS DOCUMENTED AS RETRACING PHYSICALLY -- in barrels and quotas, not in prices. EIA's August 2026 STEO expects most shut-in Middle East production back near pre-conflict levels in early 2027, with only ~0.6 mb/d of disruption persisting through end-2027. OPEC+ approved +188 kb/d for September at its 2026-08-02 meeting, COMPLETING the rollback of the 2023 voluntary cut tranche. WTI is $82.11 (2026-08-13) against April's ~$99 prompt; the strip is now described as only 'relatively shallow backwardation' out to the early 2030s; Cushing stocks are 27.52 Mbbl, the highest since August 2024. Headline CPI has printed 3.5% (June) then 3.4% (July), a second consecutive decline, with July PPI unchanged m/m. Gold traces the same arc from the other side: a record ~$5,600 in January 2026, then -14.1% in Q2 -- its worst quarter since 2013 -- then back to ~$4,360-4,500 in August. Every one of these is a statement about physical supply, a production quota, or an inflation print. None is a claim about any strategy's track record, which is the distinction DOCTRINE.md's pre-registration discipline exists to enforce. WHAT THE PRECONDITION DOES AND DOES NOT BUY. It makes the mechanism a LIVE hypothesis worth one pre-registered test. It does not make it likely, and the honest prior is against: 51 reversal rows in graveyard.csv are DEAD, cross-sectional momentum is DEAD, and every predictive strategy this lab has ever tested is DEAD. PARAMETERS, EACH TIED TO THE MECHANISM RATHER THAN SEARCHED. lookback=252 (~12 months) for two reasons that agree: it is the canonical long-horizon overreaction window, and it is the shortest setting in the pre-registered range that spans the WHOLE shock cycle instead of a piece of it -- the Hormuz closure is ~5.5 months back and gold's January peak ~7 months back, so any window below ~189 days would rank assets on the RETRACE alone and mechanically BUY the shock rather than fade it, inverting the intended sign. 252 is the top of the pre-registered range; it has been proposed here for momentum and for low_vol, never for reversal. k=3 of 15 keeps each side a genuine tail of the ranking. k=4 would tend to hold the entire commodity block (GLD/SLV/DBC/USO) against the entire rates block (TLT/IEF/LQD/HYG) and collapse into a static asset-class bet rather than a reversal -- and would additionally make this the near-exact sign flip of the already-proposed rp_cross_sectional_rank_momentum_252_4. freq=M because a 252-day ranking's membership changes a handful of times a year, and gate 1's null is duty-cycle-matched under DOCTRINE v1.5b, so a candidate rebalanced faster than its own signal moves is charged turnover the hypothesis never earns. SELF-CRITICISM, WORST FIRST. (1) rp_cross_sectional_rank_momentum_252_4 is already DEAD with OOS Sharpe 0.253, and this candidate is close to its sign flip at a different k. A near-sign-flip of a weak-positive DEAD strategy is NOT automatically alive -- both sides pay the same costs, so the usual outcome is that both die. That is the single best reason to expect this to fail. It borrows none of that row's evidence and costs its own pipeline-bucket n_tested draw regardless. (2) The mechanism's clock is the shock's PHYSICAL resolution, which EIA puts in early 2027 -- further out than a 252-day ranking holds a position, so the primitive may be measuring the beginning of a reversal rather than its completion. (3) DOCTRINE v1.9's prelim screen is calibration-only (2007-2017) and deliberately lenient, and that window contains the GFC commodity collapse and the 2014-2016 oil bust -- two large transitory-looking shocks -- so a PASS there would be weak evidence for a thesis about 2026 conditions and must not be read as support. Only the OOS gate decides. (4) A long-horizon reversal yields few genuinely independent observations per unit of backtest, which is exactly the setting where DSR/CPCV are least able to separate edge from luck. BREADTH NOTE (2026-08-14): cross_sectional_rank sits at 9 of the 57 prior rows in pipeline_ideas.csv, against static_spread_carry 12 and asset_class_trend_hedge 10 -- mid-pack, not the default reach. Within it, reversal is the least-used metric (3 of 9) and has never been proposed above 42 days, so this explores a genuinely unvisited corner of the fixed vocabulary rather than re-parameterizing a well-trodden one.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_IWM_168
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM. Nothing below asserts that trend-following, small-cap exposure, or any live strategy has recently performed well. Every input is a policy fact, a rate level, or a balance-sheet/maturity-schedule fact -- never a return. THE MECHANISM. Small-cap equity is the one equity exposure in this UNIVERSE whose earnings are mechanically levered to the front end of the curve, and the front end is now repricing HAWKISH for the first time in this cycle. (a) POLICY: the FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29 for a fifth consecutive meeting, but the vote was 9-3 with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissenting IN FAVOUR OF A 25bp HIKE -- the first time since September 2016 that three policymakers dissented with a unified direction. Futures now imply roughly a 65% chance of a September hike, and BofA's own Q2-2026 guidance is explicitly built on a forward curve containing one 25bp September hike, so the hike is in the curve, not a forecast of mine. The stated drivers are energy/supply-chain shocks tied to the Iran conflict and doubt about the Fed's inflation credibility -- a cost-push channel, not a demand channel. (b) TRANSMISSION: small caps carry far more floating-rate debt than large caps (roughly a third of Russell 2000 constituents; market commentary puts it at ~32% of R2K debt versus ~6% for the S&P 500), so a front-end move hits their interest expense directly rather than through a discount rate. SOFR sits near 4.3%; Fitch estimates each 25bp of SOFR adds ~$3.5bn of annual interest expense across the leveraged-loan universe. US speculative-grade borrowers must refinance ~$397bn in 2026 (about half floating-rate loans and revolvers), with small-cap-specific commentary putting the 2026 wall at ~$368bn refinancing near 6.5% against 1-2% legacy coupons, i.e. 150-200bp above the coupons being retired. WHY THIS IS A TREND HYPOTHESIS AND NOT A MEAN-REVERSION ONE -- the whole content of the primitive choice. The shock is already public, but it does NOT arrive at announcement: it lands borrower-by-borrower on each firm's own refinancing date and quarterly SOFR reset, and only becomes visible in reported interest expense at that firm's next earnings print. That is precisely Hong & Stein's (1999) gradual-information-diffusion condition -- a known fundamental impairment released on a mechanical calendar over several quarters -- which is the only respectable reason to expect a price series' own trailing sign to persist rather than revert. A pair or z-score primitive would assume the divergence closes; this thesis says it accretes on a refinancing schedule, so time-series trend is the right shape and mean-reversion is the wrong one. NOTE THE SIGN IS NOT ASSUMED: single_asset_trend is symmetric, so if the September hike does not land and the front end unwinds, the same signal takes the other side -- the claim under test is that the diffusion is SLOW, not that small caps fall. WHY lookback=168 (~8 months). The transmission clock is the quarterly SOFR reset plus the quarterly earnings disclosure that reveals it; 168 trading days spans roughly three such cycles, long enough for the accretion to accumulate across multiple reporting dates and long enough not to be whipsawed by a single FOMC headline (the September meeting itself), which a 20-60d lookback would chase. WHY freq=M: the underlying channel updates at quarterly earnings, so a monthly rebalance samples it several times over without paying daily turnover to track rate noise. NOVELTY: IWM has never been proposed for single_asset_trend by this pipeline (existing single_asset_trend proposals cover GLD, SLV, VNQ, UUP, EEM, USO, TLT, DBC, EFA), and no rp_single_asset_trend_IWM_* spec exists in pipeline_ideas.csv or graveyard.csv. PRIOR: family-level trend and cross-sectional momentum are DEAD in this lab; this proposal expects to fail the same gates and is offered because the mechanism is specific and checkable, not because trend deserves another look.

(secondary market commentary -- cited as reported, not as a primary source). name: rp_curve_carry_105
rationale: Every curve_carry proposal so far has varied only the slope-trend lookback (21/42/63/84/126/147/189/252) at W or M rebalance; the untested dimension is the REBALANCE FREQUENCY, and there is a mechanism-specific reason it should matter for this primitive in particular. curve_carry's DV01 weighting (k_tlt = IEF_DURATION/(TLT+IEF), k_ief = TLT_DURATION/(TLT+IEF)) makes the book level-neutral only at the instant it is rebalanced to those weights; between rebalances the realized weights drift with relative TLT/IEF price moves, and because TLT's duration (~16y) is roughly twice IEF's (~7.5y) that drift is asymmetric and systematically re-introduces net duration -- i.e. the exact level exposure the construction exists to cancel. Rebalance frequency is therefore the knob that decides how much of the primitive's own design assumption actually survives, and it has never been set to D. The current structural setup is where that matters most: the Fed's target range has sat at 4.25% with no cut delivered in 2026, so the 2y leg is policy-anchored and essentially ALL slope variation is coming from the long end -- the leg with the larger DV01 and larger price moves, hence the leg that drives hedge drift. In a front-end-driven slope regime (a cutting cycle) drift is second-order; in the present long-end/term-premium-driven regime it is not. The 2s10s is positive but narrow, well below the 100-150bp typical-expansion range, the 3m10y has flipped back to negative, and term premium is being pushed by Treasury supply and activist fiscal policy rather than by the expected short-rate path. lookback=105 (~5 months) is chosen to span the multi-month term-premium repricing impulses driving that (quarterly refunding/supply news) while excluding the 2025 easing cycle's front-end contribution, which no longer applies with the Fed on hold; stated honestly, 105 is an interpolation between the already-tested 84 and 126 -- the genuinely new axis in this spec is freq=D, not the lookback. Bearing daily turnover cost is the real risk, and it is priced by the doctrine's own frequency- and duty-cycle-matched null.
citation: Curve-slope decomposition and term-premium-driven steepening: Adrian, Crump & Moench (2013), 'Pricing the Term Structure with Linear Regressions', Journal of Financial Economics 110(1) (NY Fed ACM term premia). Current regime: Fed target range 4.25% with no 2026 cut delivered to date, 2s10s positive but narrow vs the 100-150bp expansion norm and 3m10y re-inverted, long-end-led steepening (wisdomtree.com/us/insights/blog/steeper-curves-ahead; centralbank.watch/tools/yield-curve/us-yield-curve/; 30y auction sizing/levels via newsquawk.com US Treasury auction previews, Aug 2026); term premia rising on supply shocks and activist fiscal policy rather than the expected short-rate path (Oxford Economics, 'Stock bond correlation will become positive again in 2026'). DV01/duration hedge-drift mechanics: standard fixed-income convention (duration-weighted curve trades must be re-struck as relative prices move); TLT ~16y and IEF ~7.5y effective durations are the frozen constants already pre-registered in tradefabe.pipeline.TLT_DURATION/IEF_DURATION.

name: rp_pair_zscore_EEM_EFA_84_2p0_4p5
rationale: EEM and EFA are the same trade in economic terms -- non-US equity beta funded and reported in dollars -- so their log-spread is close to a pure relative-valuation series rather than two independent risk assets, which is the precondition a z-score mean-reversion primitive needs. The current structural setup is a wedge in the CURRENCY-TRANSLATION term, not in fundamentals: the dollar's 2026 move has been concentrated against the developed-market currencies EFA actually holds (EUR/JPY/GBP -- DXY near the top of its 52-week range, then falling past 99.6 toward a two-month low after July retail sales dropped and both CPI and PPI softened), while the broad and emerging-market dollar indices have barely moved (EM index +0.06% over 30 days, -0.25% on the week) -- DXY excludes CNY and the other major EM currencies entirely. A dollar regime that repriced one leg's FX translation and left the other's flat pushes the EEM/EFA log-spread away from its mean for a reason unrelated to either region's earnings, and FX translation wedges are the component of a cross-region equity spread with the clearest reason to be mean-reverting. Reinforcing, not load-bearing: EM sits at ~14-15x forward earnings against ~24x for MSCI World, so there is no fundamental repricing story that would make a stretched spread the new level. z_window=84 (about four months) defines 'unusual' relative to the CURRENT dollar regime rather than averaging across the 2025 regime shift; z_entry=2.0 with z_stop=4.5 fades a genuine dislocation while exiting rather than doubling down if the spread keeps running, which is what a real regime break would look like. Weekly rebalance because an FX-translation wedge resolves over weeks -- daily would pay turnover for noise. Stated honestly: every predictive strategy this lab has tested is DEAD, cross-region mean reversion included, and a plausible mechanism is not evidence of an edge -- this is a candidate for the gate, not a claim it will pass.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_EFA_SPY_a
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM. Nothing below asserts that long-international / short-US has been working lately; every fact cited is a level or a composition fact about the two wrappers as they stand today. static_spread_carry wants a fixed, always-on long-short whose payoff is compensation for bearing something structural, not a timing signal -- so the question is whether EFA-minus-SPY is a paid-for-risk spread rather than a bet on a turning point. Three features of the CURRENT composition of the two indices make that case. (1) Starting-yield differential. MSCI EAFE trades at a forward P/E near 16x against roughly 22x for the S&P 500 -- a ~6-turn gap, i.e. a forward earnings yield near 6.3% versus ~4.5%. A static long-EFA / short-SPY position is mechanically long ~180bp of starting earnings yield. That is arithmetic on today's multiples, not a claim about realized returns. (2) Concentration risk sitting entirely on the short leg. S&P 500 top-10 weight is 35.59% (April 2026) and the index Herfindahl-Hirschman Index is 185 against a 5-year average of 142 -- record-level concentration, driven by a single AI-capex factor. MSCI EAFE spreads the same notional across far more names, sectors and geographies. The short leg therefore carries idiosyncratic single-factor exposure the long leg does not, which is precisely the kind of risk a structural spread is supposed to be paid to bear. (3) An FX-translation term that lands on one leg and never on the other. EFA is an unhedged, USD-denominated wrapper on developed-ex-US equities: its USD return is the local-currency return PLUS a currency-translation term. SPY has no such term at all. That asymmetry is definitional, not a forecast. What makes it a live premium rather than a rounding error right now is the dollar setting: DXY sits near 99.9 (1 Aug 2026), roughly 10% below its January 2025 peak above 109, with the Fed easing (effective funds 3.63%) and a documented, slow drift of official reserves out of USD (dollar reserve share down from ~71% in 2000, with ~30% of central banks expecting to add gold over the next 1-2 years). I am NOT forecasting the dollar and the direction of the FX term is not the argument -- the point is that a static EFA/SPY spread is deliberately holding an FX-translation risk premium that is currently active rather than dormant. long_leg='a' (long EFA, short SPY) is the direction all three arguments point; taking the other side would require arguing the multiple gap and the concentration are compensation the US leg deserves to be paid, which inverts (1) and (2). freq=M because none of this is a timing signal -- the weights are fixed, so rebalance frequency only controls drift and turnover on an always-on structural bet, and monthly matches the other static_spread_carry entries in this ledger. Not proposed: this is deliberately NOT the mirror of any already-verdicted spread. rp_static_spread_carry_EEM_EFA_a (emerging vs developed) and rp_static_spread_carry_IWM_SPY_a (small vs large) are different axes; no long-EFA/short-SPY spread exists in graveyard.csv or pipeline_ideas.csv. Honest framing, per DOCTRINE: every predictive strategy this lab has tested is DEAD against the pre-registered gates, and a cross-region equity spread has no exemption. A valuation gap is a LEVEL, not a return -- it can persist for a decade without ever converging, and the concentration and FX arguments are reasons to expect compensation, not evidence that compensation has been or will be paid. This is a candidate for the gate, not a claim that it passes one.

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_EEM_UUP_147_42
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- nothing below says trend-following, EM equity or the dollar has been working lately; every fact cited is a policy/plumbing condition or an index-composition fact as it stands today. THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES THE TWO LEGS OFFSET (what this primitive requires me to name): the dollar is a single common factor that enters BOTH legs with OPPOSITE sign, and it enters them for a documented reason rather than as an observed correlation. UUP is a direct long-dollar position. EEM's USD-reported return contains that same dollar term twice over -- once mechanically, as the local-currency-to-USD translation of its holdings, and once through the financial channel BIS Bulletin 114 sets out: a depreciating dollar repairs the balance sheets of dollar-indebted EM borrowers and of foreign investors holding EM assets, loosening EM financial conditions through the risk-taking channel of exchange rates, while an appreciating dollar tightens them. So whenever an EM trend is dollar-driven, a trend leg on UUP is long the very factor the EEM leg is short, and the candidate's net dollar exposure partly cancels while each leg keeps its own idiosyncratic driver -- for EEM the China/EM-earnings cycle and local policy easing (with the dollar weak, EM central banks can run their own cycles without FX pressure, per Janus Henderson's 2026 EM setup); for UUP the euro/yen policy-divergence term, since DXY is roughly 58% EUR and EM currencies including CNY are not in it at all. That is the offset claim, and it is a rate/funding-sensitivity argument about a shared factor, not an assertion that the two legs happen to be uncorrelated. WHY THIS SETUP IS LIVE RIGHT NOW, structurally: the dollar's support has been removed from both ends at once. Policy -- the Fed is easing (effective funds 3.63%), narrowing the rate differential that carried the dollar, with the US-Europe spread down to ~0.25pp. Plumbing -- QT has formally ended and the Fed has moved from passive runoff to active reserve management, rolling principal into and buying Treasury bills to lift reserves, which raises net liquidity; DXY has traded below 97 to a four-year low. Neither of those is a claim about returns: they are the conditions under which the shared dollar factor above is ACTIVE rather than dormant, which is the precondition for a two-leg hedge on that factor to be a coherent object at all. PARAMETERS, chosen from the mechanism's own timescales, not tuned. lookback_b=42 (~2 months) on the dollar leg: FX regimes turn on discrete policy/liquidity events (the QT end, a cut), so the dollar leg needs a window short enough to register a regime turn rather than average across it. lookback_a=147 (~7 months) on the EM leg: the financial channel transmits with a lag, through credit growth, local easing and earnings, so the EM leg should read a slower horizon. The mismatch is the point -- same factor, two different transmission speeds. freq=W because both lookbacks are multi-month; daily rebalancing would pay turnover on noise the signal cannot see. NOT A REPROPOSAL: no EEM/UUP pair exists in graveyard.csv or pipeline_ideas.csv. The two UUP hedges already tested (rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_TLT_UUP_189_63, _VNQ_UUP_126_63, both DEAD) pair the dollar with a duration-driven leg, where the shared factor is the real rate, not the dollar funding channel; EEM is the one UNIVERSE ticker whose exposure to the dollar is direct and definitional. STATED HONESTLY: the calibration-window correlation cap is a real hurdle for this specific proposal, not a formality -- a mechanism this strong could make the two sign series too ANTI-correlated to clear |corr| <= 0.3 on 2007-2017 data, in which case it is rejected mechanically and that is the guard working as designed. And per DOCTRINE: every predictive strategy this lab has tested is DEAD, trend included; a documented transmission channel is a reason to test, never evidence of an edge. This is a candidate for the gate, not a claim that it passes one.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_HYG_84
rationale: Structural setup, not a performance claim. HY index OAS entered August 2026 at 271-284bp -- the richest decile of its own history against a long-run median near 450bp -- with IG at ~81bp and the HY/IG ratio near 3.5x, i.e. at its long-run average, so the tightness is market-wide rather than one quality tier's distortion. On HYG's short spread duration (~3-4y) that configuration makes the asset's payoff structurally asymmetric right now rather than merely expensive: remaining compression toward any plausible floor is worth roughly a point of price, while a move back toward the historical median is several times that in the other direction. The asymmetry is not only arithmetic -- widening is already concentrated in the single-B/CCC tiers beneath a stable index level, the bifurcation pattern that also preceded the 2015-16 energy and early-2020 episodes. single_asset_trend is the vocabulary's mechanical way to hold a bounded-upside / unbounded-downside carry asset only while it is not repricing: the trailing-return sign accrues the ~6% index yield in quiet regimes and goes flat/short once a widening episode is underway. lookback=84 (~one quarter of trading days) because credit widening episodes historically develop over roughly a quarter -- long enough to ignore HYG's own NAV premium/discount noise, short enough to exit inside an episode rather than after it; W rebalance for the same reason, since a monthly clock can lag the exit by up to a month while a daily one churns a carry asset against its bid-ask. Explicitly NOT a claim that trend-following works -- this lab's own record says it does not; the claim is only about the current shape of this one asset's return distribution.
