name: rp_pair_zscore_LQD_TLT_45_2p0_3p5
rationale: Structural setup, not a performance claim. 2026 US IG gross issuance is forecast at a record $1.8-2.25 trillion, with roughly $300bn of it AI-infrastructure-related and deliberately LONG-DATED (data centers' multi-decade useful life), worth about $360bn in 10-year duration equivalents; hyperscaler supply alone is estimated at ~$400bn against $165bn in 2025. That is a large, recurring, calendar-driven flow shock hitting exactly the maturity bucket LQD holds (BBB-heavy, intermediate-to-long). The mechanism this proposes to harvest is the observable price signature of that flow: new-issue concessions on this paper are averaging ~12bp against a ~2.5bp broader-market average, while the same deals clear 4x or better oversubscribed -- i.e. secondary IG paper is repeatedly cheapened against duration for non-informational reasons and then re-bid as the order book absorbs the deal. A supply/liquidity shock that reverses once the flow clears is the one thing genuinely worth pointing a mean-reversion primitive at; an information shock is not. pair_zscore on log(LQD) - log(TLT) is the vocabulary's way to express it -- fade the spread when it dislocates ~2sd from its own recent mean, flat at the mean. TLT rather than IEF as the duration reference specifically because this supply wave is long-dated, so the dislocation should concentrate at the long end where TLT sits; the 1:1 log spread is NOT duration-neutral (LQD ~8.5y vs TLT ~16y), so residual long-end rate exposure rides along, which matters more than usual right now with the 2s10s out of its record inversion and steepening on term premium -- stated plainly rather than glossed, and a real reason this could fail on the calibration screen. z_window=45 (~two monthly new-issue calendars) so the reference mean spans a couple of supply cycles without drifting into the multi-year credit cycle; z_entry=2.0 so only genuine concessions trade; z_stop=3.5 rather than wider because beyond ~3.5sd the move is likelier a real credit or rate repricing -- IG spreads near historic tights (~81bp) have little cushion, and the maturity-wall/downgrade backdrop is exactly the tail where mean reversion stops working. D rebalance because the signal is a discrete state machine that holds until the spread crosses its mean, so a daily clock buys prompt entry/exit without implying daily turnover, whereas a weekly one can miss a snapback that resolves inside a week. LQD/TLT has not been proposed under any primitive; pair_zscore is among the least-used primitives in this ledger.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_low_vol_126_5
rationale: Cross-asset diversification by asset-class LABEL is structurally degrading right now, which is the setup this candidate is built for. Oxford Economics' 2026 call is that the stock-bond correlation returns to POSITIVE this year, driven by continued supply shocks, geopolitical risk and higher macro volatility from more activist fiscal policy pushing term premia higher -- explicitly framed as a problem for allocations that rely on long duration as equity ballast. CFR documents the same shift one level up: VIX and MOVE, which before ~2013 co-moved only in acute crises, now co-move as the norm, so an equity shock and a rates shock increasingly arrive together. March 2026 is the realized instance -- a correlation shock in which the traditional hedges failed simultaneously (gold about -18% intramonth, 10y Treasuries more than -4% over the same stretch), and the move was described as pervasive precisely because rates, FX and commodities were emerging from unusually low vol. The Fed holding at 3.50-3.75% with markets repricing from cuts toward possible hikes keeps that shared macro-vol driver live rather than resolved. MECHANISM: if a single macro-volatility factor is what moves every bucket together, then the asset-class label carries less cross-sectional information and each asset's OWN realized volatility carries more -- it is the direct measure of exposure to the factor that is actually doing the moving. Ranking the whole UNIVERSE by trailing realized vol and going long the 5 lowest / short the 5 highest is a label-blind expression of that ordering, dollar-neutral by construction against the common factor rather than hedged via an equity-vs-rates relationship the research above says is breaking. PARAMETERS: k=5 (of 15 tickers) deliberately broad -- the claim is about a factor ordering across the whole cross-section, not about a few extreme names, and every k proposed by this pipeline so far has been 1-4, so the broad end of the pre-registered range is untested. lookback=126 (~6 months) is long enough for a stable realized-vol estimate yet short enough to re-rank within the multi-month cadence at which the sources describe this regime moving; the two prior low_vol proposals sit at 63 and 252, so 126 fills the middle of the range. freq=W because realized-vol rankings are far more persistent than return rankings -- daily rebalancing would pay turnover for a signal that barely changes -- while monthly is slower than the regime shifts cited. HONEST PRIOR: this lab has killed cross-sectional momentum and every other predictive strategy tested, and low-vol is a well-known, heavily-mined anomaly; the argument here is not that low-vol is undiscovered, it is that the specific correlation regime makes a vol-ordered cross-section the structurally coherent construction to test now. It faces the same DSR/CPCV gate as everything else and should be expected to die there.

name: rp_curve_carry_168
rationale: The 2s10s slope is being pushed steeper right now by two structurally independent forces acting in the same direction: an ongoing easing cycle (~175bp delivered, effective funds ~3.63%) pins the front end down, while the long end has risen rather than fallen -- the 10y sits ~4.70% (near a 19-month high) on term-premium and inflation-risk-premium pressure, with year-ahead inflation expectations above 4% for a fifth month. That is a bear-steepening driven by policy mechanics plus a supply/term-premium repricing, not a bull-steepening, so the two drivers are not self-cancelling. curve_carry is the pre-registered primitive for a persistent directional drift in the slope, and its DV01-neutral TLT/IEF construction keeps the position hedged against the level move that is separately in play. lookback=168 trading days (~8 months) is chosen to match the span over which those cuts were actually delivered -- a policy-cycle-length window rather than a meeting-to-meeting one -- and freq=M matches that horizon with minimal turnover. name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_LQD_DBC_126_63
rationale: Regime argument for pairing a duration leg against an inflation-beta leg rather than the usual equity-vs-bond hedge. (1) IG credit spreads are at multi-decade tights (index OAS ~74bp, roughly the 1st percentile of a 20-year lookback; BBB OAS ~100bp near 25-year tights), so LQD's return variance right now is dominated by rate duration rather than by spread -- it acts as a long-duration leg with little spread left to tighten into. name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_momentum_168_5
rationale: The SF Fed's August 2026 Economic Letter reports that the stock-bond correlation has flipped and the stock-oil correlation changed accordingly, which it reads as the perceived source of macro risk shifting from demand shocks to supply shocks, with elevated oil prices and inflation now the prominent priced risk. That is a claim about the whole cross-section, not a two-leg pair: under a demand-driven regime a mixed asset-class universe collapses toward a single risk-on/risk-off factor, so relative ranks churn; under a persistent supply-shock factor real assets (DBC, USO, GLD, SLV) and nominal assets (TLT, IEF, LQD, HYG) separate durably, which is the dispersion a cross-sectional momentum rank needs to have anything to bite on. Corroborating structure: the curve has exited the longest inversion in the FRED series and re-steepened to roughly +35 to +52bp with the steepening attributed to term premium and fiscal supply rather than growth, and the IMF (Feb 2026) finds stock-bond diversification now offers less protection in selloffs -- both consistent with a nominal-vs-real split rather than a risk-on/risk-off one. A 168-day (~8 month) lookback spans the post-flip window without averaging deep into the prior demand-driven regime; k=5 of 15 tickers per side expresses an asset-class-bucket separation rather than name selection; monthly rebalance matches a slow structural factor. Not a performance claim -- no assertion is made about how cross-sectional momentum has recently performed; the four cross_sectional_rank momentum specs this pipeline has already tested are in graveyard.csv.

name: rp_curve_carry_210
rationale: The 2s10s curve has exited the deepest inversion in the modern series (a -108bp trough) and sits at roughly +35 to +52bp in mid-August 2026 (2y 4.15-4.18% on 13 Aug, 10y ~4.70%), and the driver is structural at the LONG end rather than cyclical at the front. The NY Fed's ACM 10-year term premium is positive for the first time since 2023 (~+0.51% June 2026, +0.83% in the 15 May daily snapshot) on three slow-moving forces: the cumulative duration returned to the market by QT since June 2022 (>$2tn), widened federal deficits expanding net Treasury supply, and an upward revision to r-star. Meanwhile the front end is pinned and contested, not trending: the 29 July 2026 FOMC HELD at 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 vote with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting toward a HIKE on persistent inflation, so 2y at ~4.15% sits above the policy rate rather than pricing a clean easing path. That asymmetry -- a persistent, multi-year supply/term-premium drift steepening the curve from the long end against a two-sided, meeting-to-meeting front end -- is exactly the condition under which curve_carry's mechanism (trend-follow the DGS10-DGS2 slope with a DV01-neutral TLT/IEF position) has a durable signal to track rather than whipsaw, and its DV01 construction is what isolates the slope from the level move the term-premium repricing also produces. Parameters: a 210-day (~10 month) slope lookback measures the change over roughly the length of the current re-steepening leg -- long enough to be dominated by the structural drift rather than by policy-meeting jitter (currently large and two-sided), short enough not to average back across the inversion-to-steepening turn the way the 252-day window does at this point in the cycle; it is also the one unsampled rung of the 21-day grid this pipeline has already tested (21/42/63/84/105/126/147/168/189/252). Weekly rebalance because a 10-month slope trend changes far too slowly to justify daily turnover, while monthly would hold a stale DV01 position through the 16 September FOMC and its updated projections; no weekly curve_carry beyond a 126-day lookback has been proposed. Bond volatility is dormant (MOVE 74.7), which is the reason to read the slope over quarters rather than weeks, not a claim about returns. Explicitly NOT a performance claim: nothing here asserts how curve or trend strategies have recently done -- the ten curve_carry specs this pipeline has already tested are in graveyard.csv and pipeline_ideas.csv.

name: rp_pair_zscore_IWM_SPY_105_2p5_5p0
rationale: MECHANISM: pair_zscore needs a spread whose DRIVER oscillates rather than drifts, and the small-cap-vs-large-cap relative is currently tied to the one part of the curve that is pinned and two-sided. The structural asymmetry is documented and large: roughly 32% of Russell 2000 debt is floating-rate against about 6% for the S&P 500 (WisdomTree's independent cut of the same gap puts it at ~40% of S&P 600 constituents carrying floating-rate debt versus ~10% of S&P 500 constituents), and small caps face a ~$368bn 2026 maturity wall rolling from 1-2% coupons into ~6.5%. That makes the IWM-vs-SPY log spread an unusually direct expression of the FRONT end of the curve -- SOFR is 3.64% and the funds target 3.50-3.75%. WHY THE DRIVER IS RANGE-BOUND RIGHT NOW, NOT TRENDING: the 29 July 2026 FOMC held on a 9-3 vote with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissenting toward a HIKE -- the first time since September 2016 that three policymakers dissented in a unified direction, and the most divided decision since 2016. A committee split between holding and hiking, with inflation above target for five years on one side and a July payrolls print of -23,000 on the other, is a policy rate that gets repriced back and forth on each data release rather than one following a delivered path. Repeated two-sided repricing of the front end mechanically drives repeated two-sided moves in a relative whose sensitivity to the front end is ~5x on one leg versus the other, which is the dislocate-and-close pattern a z-score fade is built for. Separately, the part of the curve that IS trending -- the long end, on term premium and fiscal supply -- hits both indices' discount rates in the same direction, so it largely differences out of the spread rather than imparting drift to it. PARAMETERS: z_window=105 (~5 months) spans roughly three FOMC cycles, so the z-score is normalized against the current hold-versus-hike regime rather than against the delivered-cuts period that preceded it; no pair_zscore proposal has used 105 (the ledger has 40/45/60/63/84/90/120). z_entry=2.5 is deliberately at the strict end of the pre-registered [1.5, 3.0] range -- every prior proposal here sits at 1.75-2.25 -- because this spread, unlike a hard-anchored one, does carry real multi-year drift from mega-cap concentration, and a low entry would repeatedly fight that drift; only genuinely large dislocations relative to the trailing window are worth fading. z_stop=5.0 is correspondingly wide so the position is exited on a regime break, not on ordinary noise past a tight entry. freq=W because policy expectations reprice on a meeting-and-release cadence, not intraday; daily would pay turnover on a signal that changes at data frequency. HONEST PRIOR: this lab has killed every predictive strategy tested, mean-reversion pairs included (family N, and eleven prior rp_pair_zscore specs). The level evidence also cuts against pure stationarity -- small caps sit far below and large caps far above their long-term trends, which is a divergence a rolling z-score partly absorbs into its own mean but does not erase. This is a claim about the CURRENT driver's two-sidedness, not a claim that the spread is cointegrated, and it should be expected to face the full DSR/CPCV gate on that basis. NOT a performance claim: nothing here asserts how small caps, large caps, or any mean-reversion strategy has recently performed.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_LQD_231
rationale: MECHANISM: LQD is normally a hybrid instrument -- a credit-spread carry component plus a duration component -- and the two historically partly OFFSET, since spreads tend to tighten in the same risk-on conditions that push Treasury yields up. That offset is what makes IG total returns choppy rather than directional, and choppy is the regime a trend signal loses in. Right now the offset is structurally exhausted at one end: US IG option-adjusted spreads are roughly +70-74bp against a long-run average near 132bp, the tightest in about 20 years, so the spread leg has very little room left to tighten and absorb a yield move, while it has the entire historical range available to widen. With the cushion gone, LQD's price becomes a near-pure long-duration expression (ICE BofA US Corporate index effective duration ~6.8y, weighted-average maturity 10.6y). WHY THE DURATION DRIVER IS A DRIFT AND NOT AN OSCILLATION RIGHT NOW: the long end is currently being set by a supply-and-buyer-composition process, not by the policy rate. Barclays puts private (price-sensitive) investors at ~73% of the Treasury market against ~50% a decade ago, so the marginal absorber of net issuance now demands term premium rather than holding for policy or reserve reasons; the 10y term premium has rebounded from 1.20% (11 Aug 2025) to 1.33% (10 Aug 2026) and the 30y has held above 5% for 41 consecutive sessions, the longest such streak since 2007, with the 10y at 4.70% and 30y at 5.26%. The corporate side pushes the same way: gross IG supply was $721bn in 1Q26 (+12% y/y) against full-year estimates of ~$2.25tn gross / ~$1.0tn net, which would exceed the $2.1tn gross record set in 2020. Buyer-composition shift and multi-year deficit/issuance paths are slow-moving stock variables -- they grind in one direction over quarters rather than repricing back and forth on each data release, which is the drift-type driver a trend signal is built for and the opposite of the policy-anchored front end. The asymmetry also matters for SIGN: at a ~70bp cushion a duration shock and a spread shock now add rather than cancel, so LQD's downside is the fatter side, and a signal that can go flat or short expresses that where an always-on long cannot. This proposal is a claim about what is currently DRIVING one specific instrument's price -- a slow structural supply process rather than an oscillating policy rate -- not a claim that trend following works, and it should face the full DSR/CPCV gate on exactly that basis. name: rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_TLT_a
rationale: MECHANISM. static_spread_carry is the pre-registered primitive for a fixed, always-on structural risk-premium bet, and the setup here is a single official-sector flow observed from both of its ends: reserve managers substituting away from long-dated dollar claims and into gold. Both ends are documented in level and flow data, never in returns. THE GOLD END: ECB data puts gold at 27% of global central bank reserve assets at end-2025, up from 20% a year earlier, while the US Treasury share fell to 22% from 25% -- the first time since 1996 that gold's share of foreign central bank reserves exceeds US government debt's. Official purchases have averaged roughly 1,000 tonnes a year for four consecutive years, about double the preceding decade's ~500t average; 45% of surveyed central banks say they intend to add over the coming year; and the buying is explicitly price-insensitive rather than opportunistic -- 289 tonnes were bought in Q2 2026 while the price was falling through the quarter. THE TREASURY END: the same substitution appears as a withdrawn official bid. Foreign holdings were 31% of federal debt at Dec 2025 and have been declining; foreign official Treasuries held in custody at the Fed are at their 2026 lows, down about $100bn since April; in Dec 2025 net purchases by private foreign investors were $55.7bn against $7.2bn by foreign official institutions. With QT simultaneously shrinking the Fed's own holdings, the marginal absorber of net issuance is now a price-sensitive private investor, who demands term premium to take the duration -- which is where the long end has gone: the 30y closed at 5.27% on 31 July 2026 and 5.26% on 14 August, the highest since 2007, the 13 August 30y auction cleared at 5.216%, and the 10y sits near 4.70%. The front end is pinned rather than trending: the FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on 29 July 2026 on a 9-3 vote, with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissenting FOR a hike. WHY THIS PRIMITIVE AND THIS PAIR. The claim is about a persistent multi-year reallocation between two reserve ASSETS, not about price action, so the honest expression is an always-on spread rather than a signal: nothing is forecast, nothing is timed, the position never changes sign. TLT rather than IEF is the leg that carries the mechanism -- the withdrawn official bid and the rebuilt term premium bite on long-dated duration, the 20y+ segment where the above-5%-since-2007 repricing is actually happening, whereas the 7-10y belly is dominated by the expected policy path, which is currently pinned by a committee split between holding and hiking. That distinction is load-bearing because rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_IEF_a (long gold / short belly, M) is already in this ledger: same gold leg, different rate leg, and the difference is exactly which end of the curve the cited mechanism operates on, not a re-parameterization. rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_UUP_a is also already logged and DEAD; that spec expresses the dollar side of the same story through the currency, a second-order channel, whereas the substitution documented above is directly between the two reserve assets this pair holds. GLD/TLT has never been proposed here in either direction. PARAMETERS. long_leg='a' (long GLD, short TLT) is the direction the mechanism implies -- toward the reserve asset gaining share, away from the one losing it. freq=W is deliberately the untested region of this primitive: all 14 prior static_spread_carry proposals in this ledger are M. Because the signal is constant by construction, frequency does not change WHAT is held, only how often engine.py's per-asset vol targeting refreshes the ratio BETWEEN the legs; with long-bond realized vol elevated at a 19-year yield high and repricing arriving in discrete auction and refunding events, a monthly refresh leaves that ratio up to a month stale exactly when the short leg's vol jumps, while weekly pays turnover only on vol drift, never on sign flips. HONEST PRIOR AND CAVEATS, stated before the test rather than after. This lab has killed every predictive strategy it has evaluated, always-on spreads included (rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_UUP_a, _LQD_IEF_a and _SLV_USO_a are all DEAD). Three specific things cut against this candidate. (1) The doctrine's OOS window starts in 2018, but the mechanism cited above is concentrated in its final years -- the official gold bid was far smaller before 2022 and the term premium was near zero through much of 2018-2021 -- so most of the evaluation window is a period this argument does not describe, and a verdict should not be read as flattering to it. (2) The short-TLT leg is negative carry: it pays away a coupon at a 19-year-high yield every day the thesis does not move, which gate 2's Calmar comparison will price directly. (3) Gold's higher realized vol is not a reason to expect a better Sharpe -- vol targeting is per asset, and the doctrine explicitly does not reward leverage. NOT a performance claim: nothing above asserts how gold, Treasuries, or any live strategy has recently performed. Every input is a reserve share, a holdings flow, a yield level, or a policy vote.

rationale: HYG and GLD are driven by structurally distinct flows, which is the specific reason the two trend legs should offset rather than duplicate each other. name: rp_static_spread_carry_IEF_DBC_a
rationale: MECHANISM: a two-sided ROLL/CARRY claim, not a directional or mean-reversion view -- which is what static_spread_carry is the pre-registered primitive for. Both legs are structural statements about the shape of a futures/yield curve right now, not claims about anything's recent performance. LONG LEG (IEF, 7-10y Treasuries): the belly of the Treasury curve has flipped from negative to POSITIVE roll-down carry. As of 2026-08-14 the 5y sits at 4.37% and the 10y at 4.70% -- roughly 33bp of positive slope across the exact maturity band IEF holds -- so a note held in IEF now ages DOWN a rising curve and picks up price as it rolls, the opposite of the 2022-2025 regime when the same segment sat under an inverted curve and rolled UP into higher yields. The 2s10s spread is positive (having exited its -108bp trough) though still narrow, with the front end inverted and the belly flat -- a late-cycle shape in which the 5-10y band is the specific part of the curve that earns roll, while the front end does not. SHORT LEG (DBC, broad front-loaded commodity futures): commodity futures sit in contango most of the time, and front-month concentration is the most expensive place on the curve to hold, with negative roll yield the single biggest long-run drag on futures-based commodity returns -- which is precisely why the newer broad-commodity products (COMT, CMDY, constant-maturity indices) exist to spread exposure along the curve, and DBC does not. That generic drag is unusually binding right now because DBC's largest sleeve is energy: the IEA's July 2026 Oil Market Report projects a surplus of just over 3.7 mb/d for 2026, a record annual average glut driven by non-OPEC+ supply growth (US, Brazil, Canada, Guyana, Argentina) against below-trend demand, and the WTI curve has accordingly held a contango structure for much of 2026. Oversupply IS contango, mechanically -- storage has to be paid for -- so the short leg is being paid to sit in the part of the curve that is structurally leaking roll. WHY THIS SHAPE: the two carry components are independent in origin (one is the term structure of interest rates, the other the term structure of physical commodity storage), so this is a spread between two separately-argued risk premia rather than a single bet dressed as two. Freq M, matching the 14 of 15 prior static_spread_carry proposals: the position is always-on and never changes sign, so monthly rebalancing pays the least turnover cost for the same exposure. HONEST CAVEATS: (1) DBC's index does apply an optimum-yield roll rule that mutes, but does not remove, front-month contango drag -- the leg is a weaker version of the pure claim USO would express; (2) IEF's roll-down carry is small in absolute terms (tens of bp) next to its duration risk, so realized returns will be dominated by rate level moves, not by the carry this rationale argues for -- the vol-targeted sizing partly but not fully addresses this; (3) neither leg's carry is observable in engine.load_prices()'s spot ETF closes, so the gate tests whether the claimed structure shows up in total returns, not the carry itself. Novel spec: IEF/DBC has never been proposed under any primitive.

name: rp_curve_carry_35
rationale: MECHANISM. curve_carry is the pre-registered primitive for a DV01-neutral TLT/IEF position whose SIGN trend-follows the real FRED curve slope (DGS10 - DGS2). The only free parameter is the lookback over which that slope change is measured, so the entire content of this proposal is an argument about WHICH HORIZON the slope's information currently arrives on. That argument is about the structure of the curve right now, not about anything's realized returns. WHAT THE CURVE LOOKS LIKE. As of the 2026-08-14 close: 1y 3.97%, 2y 4.17%, 5y 4.37%, 10y 4.68%, 30y 5.26% -- the 30y at its highest since 2007. T10Y2Y printed ~48bp on 2026-08-11 and sits near 48-51bp mid-August, positive after the 2022-2024 inversion (trough near -108bp). So the curve is upward-sloping but narrow at the 2s10s point while the long end carries a rebuilt term premium. WHY THE SLOPE'S VARIANCE IS ONE-SIDED RIGHT NOW. The front leg is administratively pinned: the FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29, its fifth consecutive hold, on a 9-3 vote with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan each dissenting FOR a 25bp hike -- the first time since September 2016 that three policymakers dissented in the same direction. The 2y at 4.17% and the 1y at 3.97% both sit ABOVE the 3.625% policy midpoint, i.e. the front end has already priced the hike risk that vote implies and is not free to wander between meetings. The long leg is not pinned: the 30y at a 19-year high is a term-premium and supply story that reprices in discrete, scheduled events (auctions, refunding, CPI prints, the 2026-09-16 SEP/dot-plot meeting). Net: the slope's day-to-day variance is dominated by one leg, and it arrives in steps rather than as diffusion. Bond volatility is dormant while this happens -- MOVE at 74.7, alongside HY OAS ~271-281bp and IG at 81bp, all level facts, none of them performance claims. WHY THAT ARGUES FOR A SHORT LOOKBACK. The standard reason a slope-trend lookback has to be long is to average out two legs jumping independently against each other. That reason is much weaker when one leg is held still by a committee on an extended hold and the other moves in low-vol drift punctuated by calendar events. WHY 35 SPECIFICALLY. The clock on which the information that actually reprices this slope arrives is the FOMC inter-meeting interval: 2026-07-29 to 2026-09-16 is 34 US trading days. A 35-day lookback is approximately one inter-meeting cycle -- the shortest window that spans a full policy-information cycle without straddling two of them. It is chosen from the Fed's calendar, not from the ledger: all 11 prior curve_carry proposals here sit on a 21-day grid (21, 42, 63 ... 252), and 35 falls in the untried 21-to-42 gap as a consequence of the calendar argument, not as the motivation for it. WHY freq=W. The signal is sign(slope_t - slope_(t-35)), which flips rarely, and the leg magnitudes are fixed by the frozen TLT/IEF duration constants -- so rebalance frequency controls only how often the vol-target sizing refreshes, never what is held. Weekly matches a ~7-week signal: monthly would leave the position up to a month behind a signal designed to turn within one inter-meeting cycle, while daily would pay turnover for refreshes a 35-day signal never asks for. HONEST PRIOR AND CAVEATS, stated before the test. (1) The dormant-vol argument cuts both ways: less noise per day, but also less signal amplitude to detect, and a short lookback on a smoothed macro series is exactly where trend-following most often finds noise rather than trend. (2) The doctrine's OOS window starts in 2018, and the specific configuration argued above -- five-meeting hold, front end priced above policy, 30y at a 19-year high, a committee with three hawkish dissents -- describes mid-2026 and essentially none of 2018-2024. Most of the evaluation window is a period this argument does not describe, so whatever verdict comes back should not be read as evidence for or against the argument itself. (3) DV01 neutrality rests on frozen duration point estimates (TLT 16.0y, IEF 7.5y) that drift with the curve, so the hedge is approximate; the calibration-window hedge-effectiveness guard tests whether it cancelled level risk in 2007-2017, not now. (4) This lab has killed every predictive strategy it has evaluated, curve-slope trend included; the honest prior on this candidate is DEAD. NOT a performance claim: every input above is a yield level, a policy vote, a volatility index level or a spread level -- nothing here asserts how any strategy, live or backtested, has recently performed.

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_EFA_UUP_252_63
rationale: MECHANISM. asset_class_trend_hedge is the pre-registered primitive for two independent trailing-return-sign legs, from two DIFFERENT asset classes, held as one candidate, and it requires the citation to name the SPECIFIC mechanism expected to make the two legs offset -- not merely that they have been uncorrelated. Here the offsetting mechanism is an accounting identity, not a correlation observation: EFA is an UNHEDGED foreign-equity ETF, so its USD total return decomposes exactly into (local-currency equity return) + (FX translation of the underlying currencies into USD). Roughly 70% of EAFE exposure is denominated in yen, euro, sterling or Swiss franc, and UUP tracks the US Dollar Index basket, whose weights are dominated by those same currencies (EUR ~57.6%, JPY ~13.6%, GBP ~11.9%, with CAD/SEK/CHF the remainder). The FX term inside EFA's USD return and the thing UUP prices are therefore the SAME underlying variable with opposite sign -- a shared factor by construction of the two products, which is why a trend leg on UUP is a hedge of a component EFA actually contains rather than a second bet that happens to zig when the first zags. ASSET-CLASS GUARD: EFA is equity, UUP is currency in tradefabe.pipeline.ASSET_CLASS -- different buckets, derived from the tickers, not asserted here. HOW LARGE THAT FX COMPONENT IS RIGHT NOW, structurally: it is currently the dominant term rather than a rounding error. In 2025 the dollar's move accounted for about 75% of the gap between MSCI EAFE and the S&P 500 and about 51% of the gap for MSCI ACWI ex-USA (a DECOMPOSITION of an index's return into its local and FX components -- stated here as evidence that the FX term is large, not as a claim that any strategy is working). Over the prior decade the identity ran the other way: MSCI EAFE Currency Hedged compounded ~11.5%/yr against ~8.4%/yr unhedged, i.e. the FX term subtracted roughly 3 points a year for ten years before mostly reversing in 2025. name: rp_pair_zscore_QQQ_SPY_42_2p5_5p0
rationale: MECHANISM. pair_zscore fades the z-scored log-spread log(QQQ) - log(SPY): long QQQ / short SPY when the spread is unusually low, the reverse when unusually high, flat near the mean. WHY NOW, structurally. That shared loading is not static, and it has just reached its highest level on record. The S&P 500's 12-month rolling correlation with the Nasdaq-100 hit an all-time high of 0.98 in March 2026, breaking out of the ~0.9 plateau it had held since roughly 2009. CME Group's June 2026 analysis attributes this specifically to index WEIGHTS rather than to any change in the underlying businesses: the S&P 500's information technology weight has gone from 6.7% to 39.6%, and the same research shows the mirror image -- the S&P 500's correlation to its own EQUAL-WEIGHTED version has fallen the other way, to around 0.8 since 2020. The cap-weighted benchmark has been pulled toward the Nasdaq-100 by concentration. Corroborating weights: information technology was 37.41% of SPY as of 1 July 2026, and technology plus communication services plus consumer discretionary is roughly 84% of QQQ against roughly 56% of SPY; the S&P 500's top ten holdings were 40% of index weight at 31 December 2025. Its single worst failure mode is therefore a spread whose two legs are diverging for a structural reason, where every 'extreme' reading is really the early part of a repricing. The state variable that governs that failure mode is exactly the shared-factor loading, and that loading is currently at an all-time high by construction. What is left in the QQQ/SPY spread after a 0.98 common factor is the ~14 Nasdaq-100 names outside the S&P 500 plus the sector-weight tilt (84% vs 56%) -- a genuinely small residual. This is the pre-condition under which a rolling z-score is measuring a dislocation rather than fighting a divergence. name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_IWM_TLT_105_189
rationale: MECHANISM. asset_class_trend_hedge holds two INDEPENDENT trend legs -- sign of IWM's own trailing 105-day return, sign of TLT's own trailing 189-day return -- in one candidate. It is only a hedge, rather than two bets on the same factor wearing one name, if the two legs' signals are driven by genuinely different things. The specific mechanism claimed here is that these two legs sit on OPPOSITE ENDS OF THE YIELD CURVE, and that those two ends are currently being set by different forces. WHY IWM IS A FRONT-END INSTRUMENT, structurally. This is a balance-sheet fact about the constituents, not a correlation read off the same prices the strategy would trade: roughly 40% of Russell 2000 companies' debt is FLOATING-rate, against under 10% for S&P 500 companies, and the index faces a reported ~$368bn maturity wall in 2026 with refinancing near 6.5% against the 1-2% coupons being rolled. Floating-rate debt reprices off the policy/SOFR complex, i.e. the 2-year sector and shorter. So the dominant rate channel into small-cap earnings is the FRONT end, which is currently pinned: the Fed is on hold at 3.50-3.75% after three consecutive 25bp cuts, and the 2-year at 4.15% (13 Aug 2026) sits roughly in line with that path. WHY TLT IS A LONG-END INSTRUMENT DRIVEN BY SOMETHING ELSE RIGHT NOW. TLT's 20+ year duration prices the term premium, and the current move in that premium is a supply/fiscal story rather than a policy-path story: the 10-year was 4.71% on 18 Aug 2026 with a one-year high of 4.75% set 31 Jul 2026, while investors are reported to be demanding higher term premiums across G10 bond markets on expanding deficits and record dollar-denominated fixed-income supply (US high-grade issuance alone set a third consecutive monthly record, $145.2bn by 17 Aug). The arithmetic of the two anchors is the point: 2s10s has re-steepened to roughly +55bp from a -108bp trough, so the two ends have been moving by materially different amounts -- which is the definition of a regime where a front-end-sensitive leg and a long-end-sensitive leg are not the same trade. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT PRIMITIVE FOR IT. This vocabulary's other primitives would either collapse the two legs into one spread (pair_zscore, static_spread_carry both force a 1:1 offset and a single position), or trade the curve directly with a duration-neutral rates-only book (curve_carry, already covered at 13 lookbacks). asset_class_trend_hedge is the only shape that holds the equity leg and the rates leg with their OWN independent signs and their own horizons, which is exactly what a 'these two ends are decoupled' claim implies. IWM/TLT has never been proposed here under any primitive, and IWM appears in only two prior rows. PARAMETERS, chosen from the mechanism rather than tuned. lookback_a = 105 (~5 months) for the equity leg: floating-rate financing costs reach reported earnings with a lag of roughly two quarterly cycles, so a ~5-month horizon spans one pass-through rather than a fraction of one. lookback_b = 189 (~9 months) for the rates leg: term premium is moved by quarterly refunding announcements and fiscal projections, which turn over far more slowly than the equity channel, and a deliberately LONGER window on that leg is what keeps the two legs' signals on different clocks instead of sampling one common shock twice. freq = M because both drivers are quarterly-to-annual; daily or weekly rebalancing of two slow sign signals mostly pays spread on noise. HONEST DISCLOSURES, stated before any result. (1) This lab's prior on trend is DEAD -- every trend family tested here has failed the pre-registered gates, and rp_single_asset_trend_IWM_168 and rp_single_asset_trend_TLT_126 are both already recorded DEAD individually. Combining two dead legs claims no lower bar; the only new content is the hedge claim, and it should be judged by the same gates. (2) The offsetting claim is checked mechanically against 2007-2017 calibration data (legs_pass_calibration_corr_cap, |corr| <= 0.3), and I have NOT run it -- if the two legs' trend signs turn out to have co-moved in that window, this proposal should be rejected on that check and that is the guard working, not a technicality. (3) The obvious way the mechanism fails: in a pure duration shock (2022-style), equities and long bonds fall together and both legs sit on the same factor after all. The claim above is that the CURRENT regime separates them, which is a statement about 2026, not about the whole 2018-onward OOS window; whatever the gate returns is evidence about the SHAPE across that window, not about today's setup. (4) The zombie-share and maturity-wall figures come from market commentary and should be read as order-of-magnitude, not audited. (5) NOTHING here is a claim about any strategy's realized performance: every input is a debt-structure share, a maturity total, a policy rate, a Treasury yield, or an issuance total.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_USO_UUP_a
rationale: MECHANISM: a two-sided CARRY claim -- long the commodity convenience-yield/backwardation premium, short a currency leg chosen because it partially offsets the long leg's spot beta -- which is what static_spread_carry is the pre-registered primitive for (an always-on structural risk-premium bet, never a directional or mean-reversion view). LONG LEG (USO, near-month WTI futures): the WTI curve is currently in steep backwardation driven by verifiable PHYSICAL scarcity, not by sentiment. The IEA's August 2026 Oil Market Report puts the 3Q26 global balance at a DEFICIT of 1.8 mb/d, more than double the ~800 kb/d it estimated a month earlier; global observed inventories fell 69 mb (2.2 mb/d) in July, dropping observed stocks below 7.9 bn bbl for the first time since April 2025, with the Strait of Hormuz still closed. Depleted inventory IS backwardation, mechanically: when there is no storage buffer, the convenience yield on a physical barrel spikes and deferred contracts must trade below near-dated ones. CME Group's own curve commentary confirms the shape has held since the Feb 28 outbreak of conflict and persisted past the Apr 7 ceasefire, with Dec-2026 WTI at times as much as $40 below May/June delivery. USO holds near-month WTI and rolls each expiry, so in this shape it rolls DOWN the curve into cheaper deferred contracts -- positive roll yield, the inverse of the contango drag that is USO's usual and well-documented structural handicap. This is the one primitive-expressible instrument in UNIVERSE that harvests that premium directly. SHORT LEG (UUP, long USDX futures): chosen as the funding leg specifically BECAUSE of the dollar-invoicing link, not despite it. Crude is priced in dollars, so a dollar-denominated oil price and the dollar index have a long-standing inverse relationship; shorting UUP therefore cancels part of USO's raw spot-oil beta and leaves a larger share of the position's return attributable to the roll/convenience-yield component the long leg is actually arguing for. The macro backdrop reinforces the leg rather than fighting it: the market has moved away from further Fed tightening (odds of a hike next month fell to ~31% from ~75% in late July, with the 2y at 4.15% as of Aug 13, 2026) and DXY is broadly forecast in a 95-102 range with a gentle downward drift into year-end, so the rate-differential carry that a long-dollar position collects is compressing rather than widening. WHY THIS SHAPE AND FREQ: the two carry components are independent in origin -- one is the term structure of physical commodity storage, the other a currency's rate differential -- so this is a spread between two separately-argued premia rather than one bet dressed as two. Freq M matches 15 of the 16 prior static_spread_carry proposals, and here it is also the mechanism's own clock: USO rolls its futures monthly, so a monthly rebalance is the natural cadence for a position whose thesis is that roll. HONEST CAVEATS: (1) the carry's SOURCE is explicitly expected to fade -- the IEA projects a return to surplus toward end-2026 and the CME curve itself implies spot in the mid-$70s by year end -- and an always-on position evaluated from OOS_START 2018 spans the 2020 super-contango, when exactly this leg bled catastrophically; the honest expectation is that full-window roll carry is negative and this fails the gates. (2) The inverse oil/dollar relationship is unstable and weakened materially after the US became a net crude exporter, so the spot-beta offset is partial at best and the position retains large directional oil risk. (3) Shorting UUP gives up its collateral T-bill yield, a real cost this rationale's carry argument does not recover. (4) Neither leg's carry is observable in engine.load_prices()'s spot ETF closes, so the gate tests whether the claimed structure shows up in total returns, not the carry itself. (5) DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THE MOTIVATION: sources encountered during this research also report USO's large 2026 gain. That is a performance claim and plays no part in this proposal -- selecting on a live instrument's recent returns is precisely the imported selection bias DOCTRINE.md's pre-registration discipline exists to prevent. The argument above rests only on inventory levels, curve shape and invoicing structure. NOVEL SPEC: USO/UUP has never been proposed under any primitive; the nearest prior rows are rp_static_spread_carry_USO_DBC_a (front-month vs optimized-roll basket) and rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_UUP_a (a monetary-hedge, not roll-carry, claim against the same funding leg).

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_126_4
rationale: Real-rate repricing is currently hitting this UNIVERSE's asset classes at visibly different SPEEDS, which is a cross-sectional dispersion setup rather than a directional one. The 10y TIPS real yield sits at 2.37% (July 2026), well above its 10-year average and higher over the trailing 12 months, while the 10y-2y curve has un-inverted to +0.51% (14 Aug 2026, ~58th percentile of its history). That is one common driver -- the real discount rate -- but its transmission channels run on very different clocks: FX and credit reprice within days via rate differentials and spread marks, whereas the real-asset channel runs through financing costs and cap rates over quarters. CBRE's H1 2026 US Cap Rate Survey has cap rates only now plateauing after roughly two years of repricing, with a further 5-15bp of movement still expected, and Cohen & Steers notes listed REITs reprice in real time while private marks lag by appraisal cycle. At the same time the stock-bond correlation has normalized (0.11 across 2025 to mid-2026, against 0.66 in 2022), so the cross-section again carries genuinely distinguishable factor loadings to rank, rather than collapsing to a single common beta the way it did in the 2022 inflation shock. A shared shock absorbed on asset-class-specific lags, inside a universe that is no longer one factor, is the structural condition under which medium-horizon RELATIVE moves overshoot and then converge -- which is what a cross-sectional reversal rank is built to express. lookback=126 is chosen to span the slow financing/cap-rate channel rather than a news-cycle bounce; k=4 of 15 tickers keeps both legs spread across asset classes instead of becoming a single-name bet; freq=M matches the quarterly-ish clock of the slow leg rather than churning against it. This is a mechanism claim only -- every cross-sectional rank tested in this lab so far is DEAD, and the pre-registered DSR/CPCV gates decide, not this rationale.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_SLV_189
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- nothing below says trend-following, precious metals or silver has been working lately; no price level, return figure or strategy performance claim is used as motivation, and this lab's own ledger already records rp_single_asset_trend_SLV_63 (W) as DEAD at OOS Sharpe -0.39 (2026-08-08). THE MECHANISM (why a TREND primitive at all, in a lab where every trend verdict is DEAD): the theory of storage says the inventory state, not the price, decides which time-series behaviour a commodity should exhibit. With ample above-ground stocks a price shock is absorbed by destocking and the price snaps back -- mean-reverting. As stocks approach a stockout boundary that buffer is gone, the local supply curve turns inelastic, and competitive-storage models (Deaton-Laroque 1992) predict positive serial dependence in the price path instead of fast reversion; Gorton-Hayashi-Rouwenhorst (2013) is the empirical statement of inventory-as-state-variable behind commodity risk premia. That is a claim about WHICH process should hold, derived from a measurable physical state, and it is the entire reason this primitive is chosen. WHY SILVER'S INVENTORY STATE IS UNUSUAL RIGHT NOW: the market is in its sixth consecutive annual physical deficit. Estimates of the 2026 gap itself disagree materially -- the Silver Institute's headline 2026 forecast is ~215 Moz while the World Silver Survey 2026 projects 46.3 Moz -- so I lean on the CUMULATIVE figure both agree on: roughly 762 Moz drawn from above-ground stocks since 2021. Visible vaults point the same way: LBMA London holdings ~870 Moz in Feb 2026 against 894.4 Moz at end-2025 and about 20% below the 2021 record, and COMEX registered stocks down more than 75% to ~79.9 Moz. The October 2025 silver lease-rate spike to ~39% annualised (since normalised to ~2-3%) is direct evidence the free float is thin enough to price. WHY THE SUPPLY SIDE CANNOT UNDO IT QUICKLY -- the inelasticity half of the argument: most mined silver is a BYPRODUCT of copper/lead/zinc/gold, so output responds to those metals' economics rather than silver's own price, and new primary capacity takes years; total 2026 supply is forecast DOWN ~2%. Demand-side substitution is real and already running -- solar thrifting cut per-panel silver use ~19%, taking PV demand from 186.6 Moz to ~151 Moz -- and the deficit still widens because supply falls faster. Both adjustment channels are therefore slow, which is exactly the condition under which the price path is a drawn-out repricing rather than an oscillation. PARAMETERS: lookback 189 trading days (~9 months) and freq M are set by the driver's own clock, not by search -- the physical balance is published annually and mine capacity moves on multi-year lead times, so the state variable updates far more slowly than a short-horizon signal could track, and monthly rebalancing keeps turnover matched to it. HAZARD I AM DECLARING EXPLICITLY: proposing a longer lookback on a ticker whose shorter lookback already died can look like parameter-shopping on a result. The horizon here is argued from the fundamental's update frequency and would have been argued the same way before that verdict existed; segregated n_tested plus DSR should price the extra look regardless. If the screen kills this, that is the screen doing its job.

Gorton, Hayashi & Rouwenhorst (2013), 'The Fundamentals of Commodity Futures Returns', Review of Finance 17(1):35-105 -- inventory as the state variable. THE TETHER (why these two tickers, and why it is mechanical rather than a correlation search): EEM and QQQ now sit on OPPOSITE ENDS OF THE SAME CASH FLOW. QQQ's dominant weights are the US hyperscalers funding AI infrastructure capex -- Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta are tracked at roughly $700B of 2026 data-centre capex, incremental spend of just over $300B versus 2025, with higher post-Q2-CY2026 estimates near $775-800B. EEM's dominant weights are the direct recipients of that spend: as of mid-August 2026 TSMC is 15.29% of EEM, Samsung Electronics 7.24% and SK hynix 5.08% -- about 27.6% of a nominally diversified 1,200-holding EM index concentrated in three foundry/memory suppliers, because MSCI classifies Korea as EM. J.P. Morgan Asset Management makes the transmission explicit: large amounts of AI capex flow to suppliers in Korea and Taiwan, so one index's largest cost line is the other index's largest revenue line. That is an accounting identity between the two legs' principal earnings drivers, not an observed co-movement. WHY THE TETHER IS TIGHTER RIGHT NOW THAN HISTORICALLY -- the part that makes this a CURRENT structural condition rather than a permanent one: both ends have concentrated INTO the same flow during 2026. EEM's TSMC weight has climbed through the year (a 13.3% snapshot earlier in 2026 against 15.29% now), and on the funder side AI capex has gone from 33% of hyperscaler cash flow from operations in 2023 to an estimated 93% in 2026. A larger share of both indices' earnings now runs through one flow than at any prior point, which is what makes a 1:1 log-spread a meaningful expression of the pair rather than two loosely-related equity betas. WHY DEVIATIONS SHOULD BE TRANSIENT (the mean-reversion half of the argument, stated as a mechanism): the capex-taker / capex-funder split means a single piece of news about the SIZE of the flow is a cost signal to one leg and a revenue signal to the other, so it moves the two legs in opposite directions on impact even though it does not change the total value of the chain -- the classic shape of a dislocation that closes as the flow is realized. The two ends also demonstrably reprice at different SPEEDS, which is a lag rather than a fundamental decoupling: 2026 EPS estimates have been revised up 89% for Asian semiconductor names against 22% for US and 17% for European ones since January, and capex guidance is known to move supplier names before any usage metric arrives, because chips are reserved and shells are built years before cloud revenue appears. Both legs are equity indices with comparable unconditional drift, so a rolling-window z-score is not fighting a structural drift wedge the way a spread between an equity leg and a zero-drift leg would. PARAMETERS, set by the driver's own clock rather than by search: z_window=63 trading days is exactly one quarter, the cadence at which hyperscaler capex guidance -- the shared driver -- is actually updated on earnings calls, so the trailing window spans one full guidance cycle and no more. freq=W because the dislocation being expressed is a multi-week repricing lag between the two ends of the chain, not a daily microstructure effect; a daily rebalance would pay turnover against a signal that cannot update faster than the quarterly driver. z_entry=2.25 is deliberately wider than a 2-sigma rule because the supply-chain link is partial (TSMC and the Korean memory names also carry China exposure, Taiwan geopolitical risk and a memory cycle QQQ does not), so a 2-sigma move is within the range this pair's own idiosyncratic wedge can produce; z_stop=4.5 exits rather than doubles down on a break, which is the correct default when the tether is partial. DECLARED HAZARDS: (1) the concentration that creates the tether is itself the risk -- 27.6% of EEM in three chipmakers means an EEM-specific memory-cycle or Taiwan-strait shock can hold the spread open far past any z-threshold, which is precisely why a stop is specified. (2) The AI capex flow could structurally break rather than oscillate -- J.P. Morgan flags whether $1.3T of hyperscaler capex since 2022 converts into profitable capacity as an open question -- and a break would decouple the legs permanently, not transiently. Both are reasons this may well be DEAD; the pre-registered DSR/CPCV gate decides, not this rationale.

name: rp_pair_zscore_GLD_USO_120_2p5_5p0
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- nothing below cites the recent performance of any strategy, fund or factor, and pair_zscore is not chosen because mean-reversion or pairs trading has 'been working'. Every pairs/cointegration study in this lab is DEAD, including thirteen pair_zscore rows already proposed through this same pipeline (rp_pair_zscore_GLD_SLV_60_2p0_4p0 and rp_pair_zscore_USO_DBC_40_2p25_4p5 are the nearest neighbours in commodity space); the prior here is DEAD and this rationale does not argue otherwise. THE CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION: the gold/oil ratio sits in the far right tail of its entire post-1970 distribution. Against a 1970-present average of roughly 15-20 barrels per ounce, mid-2026 readings are cited between ~55 and ~75 depending on the measurement window, a level whose only comparables are the April 2020 pandemic shock (WTI briefly negative, ratio 90-100) and the worst oil collapses of the 1980s and 2016. Both legs got there for identifiable, DIFFERENT reasons, which is what makes this a spread condition rather than one asset moving: gold ran ~60% in 2025 with more than fifty all-time highs, pierced $5,000 and set a high near $5,589 on 2026-01-28, while WTI gave back its war premium and trades in the mid-$80s with Brent around $91-92. THE MECHANISM I EXPECT TO CLOSE A DEVIATION, stated as economics rather than as an observed co-movement: GLD and USO are both dollar-denominated claims on physical real assets, and the ratio between them is the market's price for monetary safety expressed in units of energy. That price has a mean-reverting component because the oil leg has a physical anchor gold does not -- oil is consumed and must clear against production capacity each month, whereas gold's float is essentially all of it ever mined. As of August 2026 the oil curve is in clear backwardation, front-month WTI and Brent above deferred contracts, which is the market itself pricing NEAR-TERM PHYSICAL SCARCITY, and the scarcity is not merely a headline: independent estimates put truly deployable OPEC+ spare capacity at only ~1.5-2.5 mb/d concentrated in Saudi Arabia and the UAE against a much larger headline figure, drawing global spare capacity toward ~3.0 mb/d by end-2026. A tight physical market is the condition under which the denominator of this ratio has the most room to reassert itself. A MECHANICAL CARRY ASYMMETRY, DECLARED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AWAY: USO holds front-month WTI futures and rolls them, so while the curve stays backwardated it collects a positive roll return on every roll independent of what spot does -- it sells the higher near contract and buys the cheaper deferred one. That means the short-gold / long-oil state (which is the state a HIGH z-score triggers, and the ratio is currently high) carries a small structural tailwind the mean-reversion itself does not have to supply, and the long-gold / short-oil state pays it. This primitive is symmetric by construction and I am not claiming it is a carry strategy; I am declaring that its two states are not economically symmetric right now, and that the asymmetry currently favours the state the present dislocation would put it in. It reverses the moment the curve flips to contango, which is exactly the kind of thing the OOS window will or will not contain. PARAMETERS, set by the drivers' own clocks rather than searched: z_window=120 is the LONGEST window the pre-registered range allows and is capped there deliberately -- the dislocation has been building for roughly a year (gold's 2025 run plus oil's 2026 give-back), so a short trailing window would normalize the very extreme this candidate is about into its own rolling mean and see nothing. freq=W because both real drivers update on multi-week clocks: OPEC+ quota decisions are monthly, official-sector gold reserve data is monthly-to-quarterly, and USO's own roll is monthly; a daily rebalance would pay turnover against a signal that cannot update faster than that. z_entry=2.5 rather than a 2-sigma default because this spread's own unconditional wedge is wide -- a spread with a 90-100 print in living memory produces 2-sigma moves inside its normal behaviour -- so the threshold has to demand a dislocation large relative to the recent regime. z_stop=5.0 exits rather than doubles down, which is the correct default given hazard (1) below. DECLARED HAZARDS, and the first one is serious enough that it may be the whole story: (1) THE GOLD LEG MAY NOT MEAN-REVERT AT ALL. Official-sector demand is not a positioning flow that unwinds -- central banks added a net 337 tonnes in Q1 2026, the strongest Q1 on record, and 289 tonnes in Q2 2026, up 62% year-over-year and the strongest Q2 in the series, with 2026 full-year forecasts around 750-850 tonnes. Critically, that Q2 buying happened while prices were FALLING and while gold ETFs saw 45 tonnes of net outflows -- a price-insensitive reserve-diversification bid running opposite to the price-sensitive investor cohort. If the ratio's move is a structural monetary repricing of the numerator rather than a transient dislocation, there is no reversion to harvest and this candidate is simply DEAD; the stop is what bounds that, not the thesis. (2) The oil leg's backwardation is partly a geopolitical risk premium (repeated flow disruption since the 2026 US-Iran escalation, Hormuz risk), so a de-escalation could flatten the curve, remove the roll tailwind and push the ratio further out its tail at the same time -- the two hazards are correlated, not independent. (3) USO is a front-month futures vehicle, not spot crude: its tracking of the underlying commodity is imperfect by construction and its long-run drag in contango is well documented, so the 1:1 log-spread this primitive builds is a spread between a bullion trust and a rolling futures pool, not between two spot commodities. That is a real specification mismatch and it is stated here rather than discovered later. The pre-registered DSR/CPCV gate decides ALIVE/DEAD, not this rationale.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_USO_42
rationale: WTI's forward curve has been in extreme backwardation since Aug 2026, the opposite of the deep contango (~$20/bbl Aug26-vs-early-2030s) an earlier pipeline proposal on this same ticker (rp_single_asset_trend_USO_126, proposed 2026-08-07) built its trend thesis on -- that oversupply-driven regime has since been overturned by a live geopolitical supply shock, not by any performance claim about the strategy itself. Since the Iran-Israel-US war escalated on Feb 28 2026, Strait of Hormuz throughput -- the chokepoint for roughly a fifth of global oil supply -- has repeatedly whipsawed with the conflict's on/off phases: steep backwardation through the war's opening months, a brief flip back toward contango in late June as flows recovered and a US-Iran memorandum (signed 17 Jun 2026) lifted the US naval blockade, then a fresh escalation in early August when Washington reimposed the blockade after renewed attacks. Hormuz transits have since collapsed to roughly 1-5% of the pre-war ~97/day baseline (Lloyd's List Intelligence, 19 Aug 2026), and the WTI curve is back in backwardation -- a +$3.54 prompt spread per CME Group's analysis, severe enough that prices held firm even when the EIA's report for the week ending 14 Aug 2026 showed a surprise 4.4-million-barrel inventory BUILD. That decoupling is the mechanism: the physical-scarcity risk premium from a live, still-unresolved blockade is currently dominating the headline supply/demand print, not the other way around, and a naval blockade is a slow-moving state variable -- escalation/de-escalation phases lasting weeks to months, not a single-day event -- so a trailing-return trend signal is structurally suited to track which regime the market is currently pricing, unlike a static or mean-reverting construction. Lookback 42 (~2 months) is deliberately shorter than the existing USO proposal's 126-day window: it spans back to roughly the early-August blockade reimposition without also averaging in the late-June contango interlude the same war already produced once this year, so the signal reads the CURRENT escalation phase rather than blending two opposite regimes together. USO, not DBC, for the same reason the prior proposal gave: USO's return is dominated by front-month WTI roll mechanics that carry the curve's shape directly, while DBC's broad multi-commodity basket dilutes it. Stated plainly: this reuses the same primitive and ticker as an existing, still-unverdicted pipeline proposal, but the underlying economic driver has fully reversed since that proposal was written (supply-glut contango vs an active war/blockade backwardation), so this is a fresh structural thesis rather than a re-tuning of the old one -- and if the blockade resolves again as it briefly did in late June, this construction's own signal would flip with it rather than requiring a new proposal.

First, US high-yield credit is priced for perfection: OAS sat at 271bp on 2026-08-12 (Convex), in the richest decile of the last 25 years against a long-run median near 450bp, with intermediate Treasuries near 4.3% -- an acknowledged asymmetric setup ("far more room to widen than to compress") because spread duration near 3.2yr means a move back to a merely-average-tight 380bp erases roughly five months of carry. Credit priced for perfection plus a policy path with less room to ease than hoped is the setup under which a risk-off credit air-pocket and a dollar bid tend to arrive together: HYG (bucketed "rates" here) sells off on spread widening while UUP (bucketed "currency") catches a flight-to-safety bid, the offsetting pair this primitive is built to hold. lookback_a=63 (~1 quarter) matches how fast credit spreads actually move once they turn; lookback_b=126 (~6 months) matches the slower policy-repricing clock driving the dollar leg. freq=W avoids paying daily whipsaw cost on what is a quarters-long macro repricing, not a day-trade.

name: rp_pair_zscore_HYG_TLT_90_2p0_4p0
rationale: pair_zscore is tied for least-proposed primitive in pipeline_ideas.csv (17 uses, tied with curve_carry and cross_sectional_rank, vs 18-19 for the other three) as of 2026-08-22, so actively looked for a current structural setup to motivate it rather than defaulting to a more common primitive. STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM: nothing here argues mean-reversion or pairs trading has 'been working' -- every pairs/cointegration study in this lab (family N) and thirteen prior pair_zscore rows through this same pipeline are DEAD; the prior is DEAD and this does not argue otherwise. THE CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION is a live divergence between the two distinct risk premia HYG and TLT each price. Credit-risk compensation is at a multi-year extreme of cheapness: the ICE BofA US HY OAS sits at ~270-281bp as of mid-August 2026, in the richest (tightest) decile of its own history against a ~450bp long-run median, alongside a dormant MOVE index (74.7) and a re-steepened 2s10s (+35bp) -- a market pricing essentially no credit stress. Simultaneously, pure interest-rate/duration risk compensation is at the opposite extreme: the 30-year Treasury yield closed at 5.31% on 2026-08-17 and touched 5.33% on 2026-08-18, its highest level in 19 years, in a textbook BEAR STEEPENING (long rates rising while the front end stays anchored) that multiple analysts attribute mostly to a rising TERM PREMIUM and fiscal-supply pressure (Treasury expects to borrow $739bn in privately-held net marketable debt in the Jul-Sep quarter) rather than to growth or inflation optimism. THE MECHANISM I expect to produce mean-reversion in the HYG/TLT spread, stated as economics rather than an observed co-movement: HYG's total return is compensation for (short-to-intermediate duration + credit spread), while TLT's is compensation for (long duration alone, no credit spread). When term premium rises while credit stays calm -- the CURRENT regime -- TLT absorbs a duration hit that HYG's shorter duration and its (currently thin) spread carry partially buffer it from, pulling the spread in one direction; when a credit-stress episode hits instead while duration outperforms (flight-to-quality, the more common historical pairing), HYG's spread-widening dominates and the spread reverses hard the other way. Those two regimes recur and are not the same risk factor, which is the basis for expecting the spread between them (rather than either leg alone) to have a mean-reverting component across a full credit/duration cycle, distinct from either leg's own trend. PARAMETERS: z_window=90 (~4.5 months) is sized to span the 2026 bear-steepening episode building since the curve re-steepened without averaging over so long a window that the current historically-tight-credit/historically-cheap-duration combination gets diluted into an unremarkable reading. z_entry=2.0/z_stop=4.0 are the same moderate thresholds used by several prior pair_zscore proposals (not searched to fit this pair). freq=D because both legs are liquid, daily-priced instruments and the signal should react as the credit/duration divergence itself evolves, not lag it. DECLARED HAZARDS: (1) if the current combination is not a transient extreme but the start of a genuinely new, durable regime -- e.g. if fiscal term-premium pressure persists structurally for years rather than cycling back -- there may be no reversion to harvest and the candidate is simply DEAD; the z_stop bounds this, not the thesis. (2) HYG and TLT share a common rates-direction sensitivity (both are hurt by a straightforward parallel-shift rate rise even absent any credit event), so this is not a clean orthogonal pair -- the claimed divergence is specifically about the CREDIT-VS-TERM-PREMIUM composition of that sensitivity, not about the legs being uncorrelated. (3) HYG's own duration is far shorter than TLT's, so the 1:1 log-spread this primitive builds is not duration-neutral by construction (unlike curve_carry's explicit DV01-neutral TLT/IEF construction) -- that mismatch is real and stated here rather than discovered later. The pre-registered DSR/CPCV gate decides ALIVE/DEAD, not this rationale. DISTINCT FROM EVERY PRIOR PROPOSAL touching either ticker: rp_pair_zscore_HYG_LQD_90_2p0_4p0 (2026-08-07) pairs two credit instruments with no duration divergence; rp_pair_zscore_LQD_TLT_45_2p0_3p5 (2026-08-14) and rp_pair_zscore_HYG_IEF_120_1p75_5p0 (2026-08-13) each confound the credit/duration split differently (LQD carries both IG credit spread and long duration together; IEF is only 7-10y, not the long bond under the most acute term-premium pressure); this is the first pipeline proposal to pair the two cleanest available proxies for pure credit-spread compensation (HYG) against pure long-duration compensation (TLT).

name: rp_static_spread_carry_LQD_IEF_b
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM: nothing here asserts that LQD, IEF, credit spreads, or any live/paper strategy has recently performed well -- every input is an issuance-volume figure, a duration figure, or a fixed-income market-structure convention. THE MECHANISM: this is the same duration-clean LQD/IEF pair already tested once in this ledger (rp_static_spread_carry_LQD_IEF_a, DEAD, OOS Sharpe -0.077), but the OPPOSITE position expressing the OPPOSITE economic claim. That prior proposal harvested a static credit-risk PREMIUM (long LQD/short IEF, betting IG spread income compensates for default/downgrade/illiquidity risk, unconditionally, across the whole OOS window). This proposal is instead a static SUPPLY-PRESSURE bet: short LQD/long IEF (long_leg='b'), on the claim that a persistent, unprecedented wave of investment-grade bond SUPPLY -- driven specifically by AI-hyperscaler data-center capex -- structurally widens IG spreads (LQD underperforms duration-matched Treasuries) by requiring a larger new-issue concession to clear the market. That is a distinct, long-documented fixed-income mechanism (bond-supply/quantity effects on yields and spreads), separate from compensation for credit risk itself. THE CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION: US investment-grade gross issuance is forecast to reach a RECORD $1.8-2.25 trillion in 2026, exceeding even the 2020 post-COVID issuance wave, with the marginal driver being AI hyperscaler capex specifically rather than the broad market: the five major hyperscalers issued roughly $121bn in US corporate bonds in 2025 alone -- more than 4x their 2020-2024 annual average of ~$28bn -- and 2026 hyperscaler net supply is projected to rise a further 30-50% to $130-150bn, with total AI-related IG supply estimated near $300bn for 2026 (~$360bn in 10-year duration-equivalent terms, i.e. concentrated in longer tenors than typical issuance). This is a SUPPLY story, mechanically distinct from a demand/risk-appetite story: even with credit quality and default risk unchanged, a market absorbing an unprecedented volume of new, unusually long-duration paper from one concentrated sector needs deeper concessions to clear -- the same 'bond supply' channel through which heavy net issuance widens secondary-market spreads independent of fundamentals. WHY THE PAIR IS DURATION-CLEAN (an established mechanical property, not re-derived here): LQD's effective duration (~7.97yr) and IEF's (~7.2yr) are close enough that engine.py's per-leg 10% vol-target sizing on a 60-day trailing window scales both legs to approximately equal DV01, so the position is close to a pure credit-spread bet rather than a levered duration trade -- this proposal inherits that property from the prior LQD/IEF proposal rather than re-establishing it. WHY STATIC, NOT TREND: the claimed mechanism is a persistent, multi-year supply overhang (AI data-center capex build-outs are guided by the hyperscalers themselves through 2027+, not a single quarter's news), not something that should be timed off price action -- static_spread_carry's fixed, always-on construction is the correct primitive for a persistent structural imbalance, the same reasoning the prior LQD/IEF proposal used for its opposite thesis. HONEST DISCLOSURES, STATED FIRST RATHER THAN BURIED: (1) this ledger's own prior LQD/IEF static_spread_carry already died (OOS Sharpe -0.077), which is some evidence this pair's spread dynamics, in whichever direction, have not been profitably capturable at this primitive's granularity over 2018-present; I am not arguing that result was wrong, only that a materially different and more recent mechanism (this one barely existed before ~2023 and only became a large, quantifiable supply shock in 2025-2026) deserves its own independent pre-registered test rather than being inferred from the first verdict. (2) The AI-hyperscaler supply shock is a 2025-2026 phenomenon and describes essentially none of the 2018-2024 portion of the OOS window, so whatever verdict comes back is far more informative about this pair's general behavior than about the current setup specifically -- the same caveat this ledger applies to every dated catalyst tested against a multi-year backtest. (3) Heavy supply widening spreads is a real but usually modest and quickly-arbitraged effect under normal conditions -- this only clears gate 1 if the CURRENT wave is unusually large and persistent enough to matter net of costs, an empirical question this test settles, not this rationale. (4) IG spreads are currently near 25-year tights (~80bp OAS), so even a supply-driven widening starts from an unusually compressed base -- consistent with, not contrary to, the thesis, but stated explicitly since 'still historically tight even after some widening' is a plausible actual outcome. PARAMETERS: freq=M, matching the prior LQD/IEF proposal's own reasoning -- a fixed position's only turnover is the periodic vol-target rebalance, and monthly is this primitive's lowest-turnover option, which matters directly under gate 1's duty-cycle-matched null. DISTINCT FROM TODAY'S OTHER PROPOSALS: today's curve_carry, cross_sectional_rank, pair_zscore (HYG/TLT) and asset_class_trend_hedge (GLD/UUP) proposals touch Treasury term premium, broad cross-sectional rotation, HYG-vs-TLT credit/duration divergence, and gold/dollar debasement respectively -- none argues from corporate-bond PRIMARY MARKET supply, which is specific to this proposal; static_spread_carry itself was not used earlier today.

PARAMETER CHOICE: lookback=45 trading days (~9 weeks) is sized specifically to span from the 2026-06-19 trough through today, capturing precisely this steepening episode. name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_low_vol_45_3
rationale: cross_sectional_rank is the least-proposed primitive in pipeline_ideas.csv (17 uses vs 18-20 for the other five, prior to today's addition) as of 2026-08-22, and today's earlier cross_sectional_rank proposal already used the momentum metric -- this proposal uses low_vol instead, motivated by a DIFFERENT and more recent structural reading. STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM: nothing here argues any strategy has 'been working' -- every input is a volatility-index level or a documented market-structure mechanism. THE CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION is a live divergence between AGGREGATE and CROSS-SECTIONAL volatility, not a level of either alone: the CBOE VIX (index-level, 30-day implied vol on the S&P 500) touched 14.2 on 2026-08-17, its lowest print of 2026, while the VIXEQ (the CBOE's single-stock-average implied-vol index) remains only modestly below its own 31.56 long-run average -- i.e. individual names are still pricing meaningfully more uncertainty than the index-level number would suggest, because single-name moves are currently offsetting rather than compounding at the index level. THE MECHANISM this motivates, stated as economics: Baker, Bradley & Wurgler (2011, 'Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage: Understanding the Low-Volatility Anomaly', Financial Analysts Journal) document that benchmark-relative mandates structurally bid up higher-beta/higher-vol names disproportionately in calm, low-index-vol regimes (chasing relative return within a fixed tracking-error budget), while depressing demand for low-vol names despite their comparable or better risk-adjusted return -- an anomaly that is a cross-sectional dispersion effect, not an index-timing one, so it specifically requires the CURRENT condition of muted index vol coexisting with non-trivial single-name vol dispersion, rather than either extreme alone (a genuinely low-dispersion market or a genuinely high-index-vol one would not motivate this trade the same way).
