name: rp_static_spread_carry_HYG_LQD_b
rationale: MECHANISM: static_spread_carry is a fixed, always-on long-short -- a structural risk-premium bet, not a directional forecast or a bet on near-term spread movement. The economic content lives entirely in WHICH side is chosen long at proposal time. HYG (broad high-yield corporate bond ETF) and LQD (broad investment-grade corporate bond ETF) are this lab's only two corporate-credit instruments, and this ledger already holds the classic direction: rp_static_spread_carry_HYG_LQD_a (proposed 2026-08-04, long HYG/short LQD), which harvests the standard credit risk premium -- compensation for bearing default, downgrade and liquidity risk that IG debt does not carry. This proposal takes the OPPOSITE leg -- long LQD / short HYG (long_leg='b') -- which is NOT a bet that the classic premium reverses or that spreads widen from here (that would be a momentum/mean-reversion claim about the spread itself, the right shape for pair_zscore or single_asset_trend, not this primitive). It is a DIFFERENT, also well-documented structural premium: the quality / betting-against-beta anomaly. Frazzini & Pedersen (2014, 'Betting Against Beta', Journal of Financial Economics 111(1)) and Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen (2019, 'Quality Minus Junk', Review of Accounting Studies 24) show that leverage-constrained investors who cannot use leverage to hit a return target instead reach for risk by overweighting high-beta, high-leverage, lower-quality assets -- bidding those assets' risk-adjusted returns down and structurally UNDERPRICING safer, higher-quality assets relative to their own risk. Harvesting that mispricing means being long the safer/higher-quality asset and short the more-leveraged, more business-cycle-correlated one, funded by giving up some of the junk yield pickup -- exactly long_leg='b' on this pair, since LQD issuers are investment-grade (lower leverage, more diversified, higher and more stable credit quality) and HYG issuers are junk-rated (higher leverage, higher effective beta to the credit and business cycle). WHY THIS SPECIFIC PREMIUM LOOKS UNUSUALLY WELL-COMPENSATED RIGHT NOW, not merely in general (the BAB/QMJ anomaly is a structural, permanent claim, but the CURRENT leverage backdrop is what makes today a good time to add exposure to it, and is the actual research finding this run is contributing): US AI-hyperscaler-linked debt issuance has exploded in 2026 -- roughly $220bn issued year-to-date through 2026-08-10, versus only ~$12.5bn over the same stretch of 2025 -- and high-yield bonds specifically tied to AI infrastructure projects reached $26.6bn in just the first four months of 2026, already more than double all of 2025's full-year total (Morgan Stanley sees a further $40-50bn of near-term financing demand in the pipeline). Crucially, the market is NOT re-rating this uniformly: since June 2026, high-yield data-center spreads have WIDENED as investors turn more cautious on execution-intensive, tenant-concentrated AI infrastructure credits, while investment-grade hyperscaler spreads have TIGHTENED modestly on the back of those issuers' scale and stronger capital-market access (Man Group's H2 2026 Credit Outlook; Penn Mutual's 2026-08-06 'AI Infrastructure Bonds' spread note). That bifurcation is itself evidence the market is starting to discriminate along exactly the leverage/quality axis this trade is built to harvest -- named risks are concentrated tenant exposure, construction execution and chip-refresh-cycle risk, and reliance on assumed AI revenue growth to cover long-dated lease obligations (Reuters/Yahoo, 'US corporate AI debt surge tests investor limits as fatigue emerges'), all of which sit specifically on leveraged, junk-rated issuers financing speculative buildout -- the BAB/QMJ mechanism's textbook setup. HONESTY CAVEATS, stated plainly. (1) HYG is a broad, diversified high-yield index; AI-datacenter-linked issuers are still a minority of its holdings today, so this is a market-wide quality-tilt bet MOTIVATED BY, not narrowly concentrated in, AI-linked credit risk -- I am not claiming HYG is an AI-debt proxy. (2) Both directions of the same HYG/LQD pair now sit in this ledger's pre-registration record; that is mechanically fine (two distinct, independently pre-registered economic hypotheses, not a parameter sweep of one), but a skeptical reader should be able to tell this isn't 'the obvious side was taken, so try the other one' -- the citation anchor (BAB/QMJ, a named academic anomaly distinct from the plain credit premium) and the specific current bifurcation condition (dated to June 2026 onward, not available to the 2026-08-04 proposal) are what make this a separate, independently-motivated claim rather than a coin flip on sign. (3) Leverage/quality anomalies have historically been partially arbitraged in easy-credit regimes, and this lab has never tested BAB/QMJ in any form before, so there is no prior-art track record here to lean on either way. (4) This is still fundamentally a carry trade funded by giving up HYG's higher running yield, so its worst-case scenario is a long, low-volatility bleed rather than a sharp drawdown -- gate 3's pain test is the one to watch. freq M matches every other static_spread_carry candidate in this ledger: a fixed spread's only turnover is the periodic rebalance back to target weights, so monthly is the natural cadence, not a tuned choice.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_USO_DBC_b
rationale: MECHANISM: static_spread_carry is a fixed, always-on long-short -- a structural risk-premium bet on the LEVEL of a curve/roll differential, not a forecast of oil's price. This proposal is the OPPOSITE side of rp_static_spread_carry_USO_DBC_a (proposed 2026-08-04, long USO/short DBC), and that prior proposal's own stated risk is exactly the condition that has now materialized: it built long USO/short DBC on the WTI curve's steep FRONT-of-curve backwardation following the Feb 2026 Middle East supply shock (Dec 2026 WTI as much as $40 below May/June delivery at the time), and it named the failure mode explicitly -- 'when the front of the curve flips to steep contango, front-month rolling produces the most negative roll yield.' By mid-August 2026 that flip has happened: the WTI futures curve has moved into contango, forward months trading at a premium to the front month, reflecting improved/ample supply conditions relative to demand rather than the acute shortage that drove backwardation earlier in the year. The two UNIVERSE tickers separate roll-yield exposure to that curve shape by construction, not by correlation, for the identical reason the prior proposal invoked in the other direction: USO's benchmark methodology rolls the near-month WTI contract into the next month on a fixed near-term schedule and is therefore fully exposed to whatever the front-of-curve slope currently is, while DBC tracks the DBIQ Optimum Yield index, whose rule searches out to 13 months of contract maturities and selects the point on the curve with the most favorable implied roll -- built specifically to reduce (not eliminate) the roll cost when the curve is in contango, rather than concentrate on it. A fixed, always-on long DBC / short USO therefore harvests the negative roll-yield differential now facing a purely front-month-rolling instrument versus a curve-optimizing one, hedging out most broad commodity-price beta (both legs are heavily oil-linked; DBC's energy weight is large), with no directional forecast on the price of oil itself. HONESTY CAVEATS. (1) This is explicitly the mirror image of an already-pre-registered claim on the same pair -- that is not disqualifying (two independently-dated, opposite-regime hypotheses on one pair is mechanically fine, same as this ledger's HYG/LQD a/b pair), but a skeptical reader should note the two proposals share one economic story (front-of-curve roll differential) applied to opposite regimes at two different dates, not two unrelated mechanisms; the check is whether the regime genuinely flipped, which the contango-vs-backwardation search results cited below support. (2) DBC's Optimum Yield methodology reduces contango drag, it does not eliminate it -- DBC's own roll can still take a loss when the whole curve is offered at a premium, so this is a bet on a smaller loss for DBC than for USO, not a bet that DBC is carry-free. (3) DBC is a diversified 14-commodity basket (energy, metals, agriculture) with meaningful non-energy weight, so this spread is not a clean, single-factor front-of-curve isolate the way a WTI calendar-spread future would be; some of DBC's return comes from commodities with no relationship to the WTI curve at all, which dilutes but does not remove the intended roll-differential exposure. (4) No claim is made about how either leg or either direction of this pair has recently performed -- the argument here is the mechanical curve shape and each instrument's known, prospectus-level roll methodology, not a track record. freq M matches every other static_spread_carry candidate in this ledger and the natural cadence of a fixed spread's only turnover: periodic rebalance back to target weights.

name: rp_curve_carry_40
rationale: MECHANISM: curve_carry is a fixed, DV01-neutral TLT/IEF position whose direction trend-follows the realized FRED curve slope (DGS10-DGS2) -- it is not a directional bet on steepening or flattening, it re-derives direction from whatever the slope actually does. Fixed to TLT/IEF, with `lookback` (the trend window, i.e. the signal's reaction speed to a regime change) as the ONLY pre-registered free parameter -- so the economically-motivated choice available today is how fast this trend-follower should react, not which direction to bet. CURRENT LEVEL: as of mid-to-late August 2026 the 10Y-2Y spread sits modestly positive but narrow, roughly +0.45% to +0.6% (ycharts.com 10-2 Year Treasury Yield Spread tracker; primerates.com Treasury Yield Curve Today, dated 2026-08-20) -- a normal, upward-sloping curve, not a steep one. WHY THE REACTION-SPEED CHOICE MATTERS RIGHT NOW: the curve exited inversion earlier in 2026 on a narrative of anticipated Fed cuts, but the policy backdrop underneath that positive slope has since become genuinely two-sided, not a one-directional consensus. At its July 29, 2026 meeting the FOMC held the federal funds target range at 3.50%-3.75% for the fifth straight meeting since ending its Sept/Oct/Dec-2025 cutting cycle -- and three regional Fed presidents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) dissented in favor of a HIKE, the first time since September 2016 that three FOMC members have dissented in a single, unified direction, reflecting inflation that has now run above the Fed's 2% target for over five years (CNN, 'Fed holds interest rates steady after cliffhanger meeting, but three officials dissent', 2026-07-29; Axios, 'Fed leaves rates steady, with internal dissent', 2026-07-29; CNBC, 'Fed rate decision July 2026: Divided Fed holds interest rates steady'; J.P. Morgan Asset Management, 'FOMC Statement: July 2026'). The next FOMC meeting, September 15-16, 2026, carries a new Summary of Economic Projections and is described in current coverage as 'finely balanced' on whether a hike actually happens, contingent on Middle East developments and the next two CPI prints (Forbes, 'Fed Meeting Tracker 2026: How Interest Rate Shifts Shape Investor Strategy in August'). That combination -- a curve holding a positive-but-narrow slope while the committee that sets the short end just produced its most openly hawkish, unified dissent in a decade, heading into a live meeting where a hike is genuinely on the table -- is a real, dated shift in the uncertainty regime driving DGS10-DGS2, distinct from the earlier-2026 aggressive-cut narrative. WHY lookback=40 (~8 trading weeks, freq=W): a trend-follower needs a window long enough to filter single-CPI- print/single-day noise around individual data releases, but short enough that it is still meaningfully populated by post-dissent-regime curve data by the time the September 15-16 decision lands, and can update within weeks rather than months of whatever the new SEP delivers. The long lookbacks this ledger has already tried (147/168/189/210/252, all now DEAD in graveyard.csv) would still be dominated by the spring bull-steepening move and slow to register a reversal or acceleration triggered by the September meeting; the shortest ones already tried (21/35) risk chasing single-print noise rather than a genuine regime signal. 40 sits between those, is unused so far among this primitive's 18 prior proposals in this ledger, and is motivated by the ~2-month span from the July 29 dissent through the September 15-16 decision, not by picking an arbitrary unused integer. freq=W matches the majority of this primitive's own prior proposals and lets the position rebalance within the same window without chasing daily curve noise. HONESTY CAVEATS. (1) curve_carry's own calibration-window hedge-effectiveness guard (curve_carry_hedge_is_effective, checked mechanically before this can proceed) is unaffected by and independent of this rationale -- it tests whether the DV01 hedge actually cancelled DGS10-level risk in 2007-2017 data, not whether today's narrative is correct. (2) Five prior curve_carry candidates in this ledger already went DEAD against the doctrine gates; I am not claiming lookback=40 is likely to clear where those failed, only that it is a distinct, honestly-motivated hypothesis about reaction speed under a policy-uncertainty regime (the July 29 hawkish 3-dissent hold) that postdates every one of those five proposals. (3) Current commentary is genuinely split on WHY the curve holds a positive slope right now -- some framing it as a lingering bull-steepener (cut expectations), other analysis attributing it to fiscal/term-premium pressure on the long end -- and I take no side on which is correct; the disagreement itself is the evidence of two-sided uncertainty that motivates a moderately short (not extreme either way) reaction window, not a directional claim, since the primitive itself has no direction baked in. (4) No claim is made about how curve_carry or any of its lookback variants has recently performed live or in backtest -- this proposal is about the mechanism (policy-uncertainty regime -> appropriate trend-reaction speed), not a track record.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_momentum_45_3
rationale: MECHANISM: cross_sectional_rank is a fixed-metric long-top-K/short-bottom-K ranking across the full UNIVERSE (15 tickers spanning equity, rates, commodity, real_estate and currency buckets) -- its edge, if any, depends on the UNIVERSE currently having genuine cross-sectional dispersion in what drives each asset, not one shared macro factor moving everything together (in which case a long-short nets out the common factor and adds nothing). Metric/lookback/k are the only pre-registered free parameters, so the economically-motivated choices available today are WHICH metric captures the current dispersion regime and over WHAT window. CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION: single-stock implied correlation is unusually LOW right now and still below its long-term average even after a recent rise -- Cboe's 1-Month Implied Correlation Index (COR1M) stood at 7.88 on 2026-08-12 and the 3-Month (COR3M) at 9.71; COR1M and COR6M had risen 6.9% and 17.2% respectively in July 2026 but 'both indices were still below long-term averages' per Cboe's own July 2026 Index Insights note. Low implied correlation is the textbook signature of an idiosyncratic-catalyst-driven ('stock-picker's') market rather than a macro-driven one, where a single risk-on/risk-off factor dominates and cross-sectional ranking just re-expresses that one factor. SEPARATELY, market breadth/concentration is genuinely shifting, not just correlation: the equal-weight S&P 500 is outperforming the cap-weighted index by roughly 1.7-3 points in 2026 (CNBC, 2026-08-23: 'Equal-weight S&P 500 is leading the 2026 market and its flagship trade just hit $100 billion'), the Mag 7 mega-caps were flat in H1 2026 versus +9.3% for the S&P 500 overall, and commentary attributes the equal-weight index's outperformance to 'declining market concentration, a rotation toward small-caps, and a persistent value tilt' (Capital Group, 'Fresh breadth? A market where returns are no longer concentrated in one mega-cap-tech leadership group is structurally one where MORE of the UNIVERSE's own tickers can plausibly carry independent, own-asset trend information worth ranking, rather than every equity sleeve just tracking the same handful of names. name: rp_single_asset_trend_GLD_25
rationale: MECHANISM: single_asset_trend takes the sign of a ticker's own trailing return over a lookback window as its position -- a pure trend-following bet with no cross-asset reasoning. The only pre-registered free parameters are ticker and lookback, so the economically-motivated case available here is WHICH ticker's trend mechanism is well-matched to a currently identifiable price regime, and over WHAT window -- not any claim that trend-following in general, or this ticker specifically, has recently performed well. CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION: gold has moved through two DISTINCT, opposite-signed regimes within 2026, not one sustained move. Gold hit a record high of $5,595/oz in January 2026, then fell sharply to below $4,000 by June 2026 during the initial phase of the US-Israel-Iran war (outbreak 28 Feb 2026) -- a liquidity-crisis-driven selloff as investors and some central banks drew down gold holdings for cash amid broader market stress and the oil price spike, i.e. gold traded like a risk asset being liquidated, not like a safe haven. Since then gold has rebounded roughly 9% in August 2026 back to about $4,400/oz, which Reuters and multiple outlets specifically frame as gold 'regaining'/'reclaiming' its safe-haven status because peace talks to end the Iran war are faltering and the Strait of Hormuz closure persists (Day 175+ as of 22 Aug 2026, continued vessel attacks since 1 Aug, roughly 65 ships stranded after a collapsed transit understanding) -- the driver has flipped from liquidity panic to renewed geopolitical hedging demand tied explicitly to the conflict's continued, unresolved status rather than to an already-resolved one-off shock. A 126-day trailing window as of today (2026-08-23) reaches back to roughly late February 2026 -- squarely spanning BOTH the liquidity-crash regime (Jan-Jun) and the current safe-haven-recovery regime (Aug), so its trailing-return signal averages two opposite-signed price regimes together, structurally miscalibrated to detect either cleanly regardless of which (if either) carries real signal. A short lookback confined to roughly the August recovery leg is the parameter choice actually matched to the mechanism just described -- a regime that reasserted specifically in August, driven by war-persistence/failed-talks expectations, not a multi-month trend. PARAMETERS: lookback=25 trading days (~5 weeks), sized to span the August rebound (already roughly 3 weeks old as of 2026-08-23) with a small buffer, while staying short enough not to reach back into the pre-rebound trough/crash period. freq=W, matched to the roughly weekly cadence at which this event-driven regime (Hormuz transit status, peace-talk headlines) has been shifting. HONESTY CAVEATS: (1) This is a claim about which structural regime is currently operative for gold and why a short window is the mechanistically appropriate one to test it with -- it is explicitly NOT a claim that gold 'has been going up' as a reason to expect continuation, nor any claim about how any trend or other strategy has recently performed. (2) single_asset_trend on GLD at a longer lookback (126, M) has already been tested and is DEAD; this proposal is a different spec, not a re-test, but doctrine's no-lower-bar rule applies regardless -- a short-window trend signal on the same ticker carries the same base-rate caveats every trend primitive in this graveyard already carries (139 DEAD verdicts and counting as of 2026-07-29), and nothing here claims this draw is exempt from that base rate. name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_VNQ_TLT_189_63
rationale: MECHANISM: asset_class_trend_hedge holds two independent single_asset_trend legs (each leg's own trailing-return sign over its own lookback) in one candidate, and requires the two tickers to come from DIFFERENT ASSET_CLASS buckets (here: VNQ = real_estate, TLT = rates) -- a mechanical stand-in for 'these two legs have a real, checkable relationship', not a correlation search, and this is verified mechanically against 2007-2017 calibration data before the proposal can proceed regardless of how this citation reads. CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION: the 2s10s Treasury curve spent 2022-2024 in its longest inversion since the 1970s (26 months), began un-inverting in September 2024, and by Q4 2025 had settled into a sustained, positive slope across all major tenors after the Fed's late-2024 100bp cut and a further measured 2025 easing cycle. As of 20 Aug 2026 the 10s2s spread sits at roughly +46bps and the 10Y-3M gap at roughly +78bps -- both durably positive, read by commentators as a 'healthy expansion' signal rather than a recession warning. SPECIFIC MECHANISM CONNECTING THE TWO LEGS: REITs are widely documented as long-duration, rate-sensitive 'bond proxies' -- their valuations move with long-term rate direction via the cap-rate discount channel, with academic work (e.g. NYU Stern's 'Interest Rate Risk of Real Estate Investment Trusts' and EPRA's 'The Interest Rate Sensitivity of Public Real Estate') estimating REIT interest-rate betas directly against long Treasury proxies and finding effective duration driven by lease-renewal structure, the same underlying long-rate exposure TLT is built to trend-follow. A curve that has just completed a multi-quarter regime shift from inverted to a sustained positive slope is exactly the kind of environment in which VNQ's own trailing-return trend and TLT's own trailing-return trend would be expected to decorrelate from whatever static relationship they held during the older inverted regime, which is the calibration-window property this candidate is actually gated on. PARAMETERS: lookback_a=189 trading days (~9 months) on VNQ, long enough to filter REIT-specific noise (sector rotations, individual property-market headlines) and capture the multi-quarter re-coupling with the rate regime rather than any single data print; lookback_b=63 (~3 months) on TLT, shorter because Treasury long-end direction reprices faster on Fed communication and macro data than REIT valuations do -- an asymmetric long/short lookback pairing, the same shape as this ledger's one ALIVE pipeline candidate, rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_SPY_IEF_252_63. freq=W to avoid over-trading either leg's already-multi-month signal. HONESTY CAVEATS: (1) the REIT-rate literature is explicit that this sensitivity is TIME-VARYING and has switched sign historically (e.g. triple-net-lease REITs show high positive rate betas while hotel REITs have shown negative ones; VNQ is a broad blend), and 'there is no long-run predictive rule' governing the relationship -- this is a plausible-mechanism bet, not a proven constant. (2) VNQ+TLT specifically and this exact lookback pair have not been tested in this pipeline before (checked against pipeline_ideas.csv and graveyard.csv), but the same no-lower-bar rule applies as to every other candidate: 20/21 prior asset_class_trend_hedge proposals verdicted DEAD and one ALIVE (SPY/IEF), and nothing here claims this pair is exempt from that base rate. PARAMETER CHOICE: metric=momentum (not reversal) because all three moves above are explicitly ongoing, multi-week TRENDS, not one-off shocks that already mean-reverted; lookback=60 trading days (~3 calendar months) is chosen to span back before the 30 Jun 2026 inflection point in the 2yr/30yr divergence cited above, long enough to capture the building trend rather than just the latest week's headline print; k=3 (top-3/bottom-3 of 15 tickers) is a moderate-breadth choice matching that three distinct buckets are diverging right now, rather than a narrower top/bottom-1 that would just re-express a single pair. rationale: MECHANISM: static_spread_carry is a fixed, always-on long-short -- a structural risk-premium bet, not a directional call on the next few weeks. name: rp_pair_zscore_HYG_USO_60_2p0_4p0
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- nothing below asserts pair_zscore, credit, or oil trend strategies have recently performed well; every input is a market-structure or index-composition fact. MECHANISM: pair_zscore mean-reverts the z-scored log-spread between two tickers, so it needs a spread whose driver DISLOCATES then re-normalizes rather than one that drifts. HYG (high-yield credit) and USO (front-month WTI) sit on opposite ends of a real, named transmission channel: energy issuers are a large, persistent slice of the US HY market -- roughly 13% of the SPDR Bloomberg High Yield Bond ETF (JNK) by sector weight, with separate market commentary citing energy-linked HY exposure at up to ~1/5 of the broader HY universe -- and the academic literature (Bouri et al. and related event-study work on oil-price/credit-spread transmission in energy vs non-energy issuers) documents that a shock to spot oil repriced HY spreads specifically through the energy-issuer default-risk channel. CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION, WHY A DISLOCATE-AND-CLOSE SHAPE FITS NOW RATHER THAN A DRIFT: the WTI curve has been whipsawing on the still-unresolved Strait of Hormuz blockade's on/off phases -- steep backwardation through the war's opening months, a brief flip toward contango in late June 2026 when a US-Iran memorandum briefly lifted the naval blockade, then fresh escalation and renewed backwardation (+$3.54 prompt spread per CME Group's analysis) after the blockade was reimposed in early August -- with Hormuz transits collapsing to roughly 1-5% of the pre-war baseline (Lloyd's List Intelligence, 19 Aug 2026). Spot oil reprices on each escalation/de-escalation headline within a session; HYG, an ETF holding a diversified basket of already-issued bonds, cannot reprice energy-issuer default risk that fast -- dealer inventory, NAV-tracking lags and the fact that a single day's oil move does not immediately change any issuer's actual leverage all slow the credit repricing relative to the commodity. name: rp_static_spread_carry_VNQ_IEF_b

At this compression, the market is pricing close to zero incremental compensation for real-estate-specific risk over simply holding the duration-matched government bond -- the structural argument for OVER-weighting the real estate leg is currently at its weakest, and the safer, duration-matched leg (IEF, the conventional 10yr-equivalent proxy) is the side of this spread currently better compensated per unit of risk. name: rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_SLV_a
rationale: Structural, not a track-record claim -- no assertion is made about how GLD, SLV, or any live book has recently performed; the direction (long GLD / short SLV) is a standing structural-flow bet, not a forecast tuned to a recent chart. THE STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRY: gold and silver are exposed to fundamentally different demand bases, and one of those bases has undergone a real multi-year regime shift while the other has not. Central-bank official-sector gold buying has averaged ~1,000 tonnes/year over the past four years, double the ~500t/year decade-prior average (World Gold Council). 2026 continues this: 244t bought in Q1 2026 alone (Poland and China notable buyers), JPMorgan forecasts ~755t for the full year, and the WGC 2026 Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey (published 2026-06-16) found 45% of surveyed central banks plan to INCREASE gold holdings over the next 12 months while 74% expect the dollar's reserve share to keep declining over five years -- a policy-driven, multi-year reserve-diversification program, not a speculative trade. Silver has no equivalent -- it is not a reserve asset any central bank accumulates; its price is set by industrial demand (solar, electronics) and retail/speculative investment flow, both cyclical and reversible in a way official-sector reserve accumulation is not. WHY THIS FAVORS A STATIC, ALWAYS-ON TILT RATHER THAN A SIGNAL: static_spread_carry makes no claim about short-run direction or timing -- it is paid for bearing the asymmetry that GLD carries a standing, policy-backed buyer of last resort that SLV structurally lacks, the same shape as this lab's one surviving book (crypto funding carry: compensation for a real, persistent structural asymmetry, not a directional forecast). CROSS-CHECK, cited for context only (not as a performance claim driving the choice): the gold/silver price ratio sat at 61.7 on 2026-06-15, below the 50-year historical average of 65-70, and JPMorgan projects it normalizing toward 70 over H2 2026 and toward 75 in 2027 -- consistent with, not the basis for, the demand-asymmetry argument above. Neither this pair nor this direction has been proposed before: the one prior GLD/SLV pipeline proposal (rp_static_spread_carry_SLV_GLD_a, 2026-08-07) is the OPPOSITE leg (long SLV / short GLD); this is a new, distinct spec.

name: rp_pair_zscore_GLD_SLV_25_2p25_4p5
rationale: MECHANISM: pair_zscore mean-reverts the z-scored log-spread of GLD vs SLV -- long-the-spread (long GLD / short SLV) when the spread is unusually low, short-the-spread when unusually high, flat near the mean. It bets that once the spread's rolling z-score hits an extreme, the two legs' short-run divergence normalizes back toward the window's own recent equilibrium -- it does not require forecasting which metal outperforms over the long run, only that the spread oscillates around a level rather than moving in one direction without bound. STRUCTURAL CONDITION, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM: the gold/silver ratio underwent a genuine, dated regime shift and has since settled into a new, tighter band rather than continuing to trend. USAGOLD's daily precious-metals report for 2026-08-04 records the ratio 'compressing below 69' as silver surged 2.5% to $59; by 2026-08-25 the same source has it 'near 68.2,' essentially unchanged three weeks later, with gold at $4,627.36 and silver at $67.82. That is a level, not a trend: after an initial multi-week compression the ratio has been oscillating in a narrow sub-69 band for ~3 weeks rather than continuing to fall. The structural driver behind the initial move is the Silver Institute's 2026 World Silver Survey deficit figure (46.3M oz this year, ~762M oz cumulative since 2021, via goldsilver.com's 'Why Is Silver Outperforming Gold? A 6-Year Deficit') colliding with gold's own historic move -- gold is on pace for its strongest monthly gain since September 1999 (usagold.com, 2026-08-25 report). name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_QQQ_TLT_126_63
rationale: MECHANISM: asset_class_trend_hedge holds two independent trailing-return-sign legs across two DIFFERENT asset classes, and requires a citable channel for why they should offset -- not just historical decorrelation. CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION, NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM: 2026 is a genuine supply-shock year for the long end of the US corporate and Treasury-adjacent duration market, driven directly by the same AI-capex story concentrated in QQQ's own megacap holdings. Hyperscaler gross bond issuance already exceeds all of 2025 -- roughly $152B in the first four and a half months of 2026 against Street estimates of ~$300B in AI-related investment-grade supply for the full year, with about a third of ~$800B aggregate 2026 hyperscaler capex expected to be debt-financed (Goldman Sachs, Vanguard, Investing.com coverage, 2026). Critically this issuance is deliberately LONG-DATED -- most maturities five years and longer -- to lock in multiyear funding for AI infrastructure builds, which materially extends the duration profile competing for the same long-end buyer base TLT itself draws on. That supply pressure is visible in the long end directly: the 10-year Treasury yield reached 4.69% on 2026-08-20, and IG spreads on bonds maturing beyond 20 years widened to 118bp from a lower prior level as the market absorbed the wave (S&P warning of 'fatigue' with hyperscalers 'paying a higher premium compared with yields on risk-free bonds'). THE OFFSETTING CHANNEL: this is a single financing mechanism producing opposite-signed pressure on the two legs, not a coincidental correlation. When the AI-capex narrative strengthens (new hyperscaler guidance, accelerating GPU/datacenter builds), it does two things simultaneously through the SAME channel: it supports the earnings case dominating QQQ's own top-heavy composition (QQQ up), and it raises the debt-financed share and pace of that capex, adding to the long-duration supply TLT's own price must absorb (TLT down as yields rise). When the capex narrative cools (a guidance disappointment, a pause in debt-financed buildout), both reverse together: QQQ's growth premium compresses while long-end supply pressure eases and TLT rallies. This is NOT a claim that the strategy has performed well, nor that trend-following broadly works -- this lab has killed trend-following in every family tested so far, including on both TLT and QQQ individually -- only that this specific, live, event-dated supply/earnings dual-channel gives trailing-return sign on these two legs, over this window, something structural to track that it lacks in a generic 'growth stocks vs bonds' framing. PARAMETER CHOICE: lookback_a=126 (~6 months) on QQQ spans roughly two earnings cycles, the cadence at which hyperscaler capex guidance itself is actually revised upward or downward; lookback_b=63 (~3 months) on TLT is shorter because Treasury-market absorption of a given quarter's issuance calendar and auction results reprices faster than the earnings-driven equity leg. freq=W matches the pace new issuance and guidance headlines are actually arriving (multiple hyperscaler bond deals priced per month through 2026). name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_20_2
rationale: MECHANISM: cross_sectional_rank(metric=reversal) ranks the full UNIVERSE by trailing return over the lookback window and takes the OPPOSITE side -- long the K biggest recent losers, short the K biggest recent winners -- which is a direct bet on short-horizon overreaction correcting, not a claim about any live strategy's recent results. Nagel (2012, 'Evaporating Liquidity', NBER/RFS) shows this reversal return is best understood as compensation for liquidity provision: constrained intermediaries pull back exactly when volatility spikes, prices overshoot on the way, and the VIX is a far stronger, more direct predictor of reversal-strategy Sharpe than lagged market returns -- reversal profits and conditional Sharpe ratios rise sharply with the VIX because that is precisely when liquidity evaporates and overreaction is largest. CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM: as of 2026-08-27 the VIX sits at 14.56 (down 4.27% on the day), within a point of its 2026 YTD low, with the S&P 500 at record highs -- textbook low pre-event hedging and market complacency (Investing.com, 'S&P 500 at Record Highs, VIX Near 14: Why Jackson Hole Could Change Everything'). That calm sits directly against a genuine, dated two-sided catalyst landing inside this primitive's own rebalance clock: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote as chair, 2026-08-28 10:00am ET (today), with markets pricing roughly one-in-three odds of a September hike against a dovish alternative -- Goldman Sachs is on record (via BigGo Finance, 'Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole Debut: Goldman Sachs Warns of Amplified FX Volatility') that the keynote historically amplifies FX volatility sharply, and Investing.com/SpotGamma option-market coverage puts the plausible instantaneous move at 1-3% across USD, equity indices and commodities in minutes if Warsh surprises either way -- precisely BECAUSE implied vol is low and the market is not hedged for it. That is the Nagel mechanism in its purest form: a low-liquidity-buffer market catches a real, two-sided shock, dealers pull back into the print, cross-sectional prices overshoot on whichever names react hardest (rate-sensitive and FX-linked tickers most), and the reversal primitive is positioned to harvest the correction as liquidity providers step back in over the following sessions -- not to predict which direction Warsh surprises in, since the rank-based long-loser/short-winner construction is symmetric to that. PARAMETERS: lookback=20 is the floor of this primitive's pre-registered [20,252] range, chosen because Nagel's effect and the option-market framing above are both about a SHORT-horizon overreaction-then-correction around a single dated print, not a multi-month drift a longer lookback would blend away; freq=D matches that same short-horizon logic -- a weekly or monthly rebalance would miss the window entirely by marking after the liquidity-provision return has already been earned and reversed back out. k=2 is a deliberately narrower basket than this primitive's modal k=3-4 (pipeline_ideas.csv: existing reversal proposals use k=2,3,3,3,4,4), concentrating the bet on the names showing the most extreme trailing moves -- the ones actually doing the overreacting -- rather than diluting into a broader basket. PRIMITIVE-BREADTH NOTE: cross_sectional_rank is this pipeline's least-proposed primitive (26 of 165 prior rows vs 27-29 for the other five as of 2026-08-28), and within it, metric=reversal is itself the least-used metric (6 uses vs 7 for low_vol and 12 for momentum) -- raised here because today's actual research (the VIX-complacency-into-a-dated-event setup) specifically supports a reversal bet, not to force balance on its own. NOT A REPROPOSAL: grepped pipeline_ideas.csv for every cross_sectional_rank_reversal row (lookback/k pairs 21/3, 42/2, 20/4, 252/3, 126/4, 50/3 across M/W/D freqs) -- 20/2 does not appear, and grepping graveyard.csv for 'cross_sectional_rank_reversal' returns no rows at all, so none of this metric's proposals have reached a verdict yet either. HONESTY CAVEAT: this primitive has no dedicated calibration step of its own (unlike asset_class_trend_hedge or curve_carry), so nothing here mechanically confirms the liquidity-provision channel actually held in-sample before backtest; whether a 20-day, K=2 reversal book actually captures Jackson-Hole-scale overreaction versus just adding turnover and transaction-cost drag is exactly what the downstream DSR/CPCV screen decides, not this rationale.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_USO_90
rationale: MECHANISM: single_asset_trend's direction is mechanical (sign of USO's own trailing return), not chosen by me -- this is a structural-conditions claim about why a trend in crude is more likely to persist right now, not a forecast of which way it goes or a claim about any strategy's recent track record. THE STRUCTURAL SETUP. Two independent, currently-operating supply-side facts point the same direction. (1) Term structure: WTI moved into steep backwardation after the US-Israel-Iran conflict opened on 2026-02-28 and the effective Hormuz disruption that followed -- December-2026 contracts traded as much as $40 below May/June delivery at the peak -- but that premium has been unwinding since the 2026-04-07 ceasefire, and for much of 2026 the curve has reverted to contango, forward months priced above spot, which is the market's own forward-looking signal of weak near-term demand relative to supply, not a lagging indicator of price. (2) Physical balance: both major forecasters now project a large 2026 glut -- EIA's STEO puts the global surplus at 2.2 million b/d for 2026 (global liquids output ~106 mb/d against consumption ~104.1 mb/d), while IEA's August 2026 Oil Market Report puts it closer to 4 mb/d (~4% of world demand); both cite the same mechanism, OPEC+ unwinding its voluntary cuts (~1.2-1.4 mb/d of added OPEC+ supply into 2026) plus continued non-OPEC growth from the US, Canada, Brazil and Guyana. WHY THIS FAVORS TREND PERSISTENCE, mechanically, not directionally. A glut driven by a quota-and-capacity supply process and absorbed through inventory builds is a slow, multi-month repricing, not a single news shock -- WTI has been consolidating in the mid-$80s (stalling near $84.30) while the curve and the physical-balance forecasts both already point the same way, which is the setup a medium-horizon trend signal is built to catch: a persistent structural repricing rather than a one-day jump. LOOKBACK 90, ARGUED NOT TUNED. The IEA/EIA glut estimates are framed as full-year 2026 averages and the ceasefire that started the contango unwind is now almost 5 months old (2026-04-07 to 2026-08-28, ~100 trading days) -- 90 trading days (~1 quarter) is close to that unwind's own elapsed clock and short of a full year, long enough to filter the day-to-day headline noise this same ticker's single_asset_trend proposals at lookback 42 (2026-08-21) and lookback 126 (2026-08-07) sit on either side of, without being a re-proposal of either. freq W because a supply-and-inventory-driven repricing has no reason to be captured or acted on intraday; the position should turn over on the same order as the structural process generating it, not faster. WEAKNESSES, STATED BEFORE THE VERDICT, WORST FIRST. (1) Every trend-following strategy this lab has tested is DEAD -- tsmom, green_line_200d, family L's hourly trend, ~35 donchian_gen_* factory draws, and USO's own two prior single_asset_trend proposals carry the same prior. Changing the commodity and the reason for expecting persistence does not change the shape, and the entire burden is on the mechanism being different in kind, which it may not be. (2) Forecaster oversupply numbers disagree by nearly 2x between EIA and IEA (2.2 vs ~4 mb/d) and both are routinely revised; a 2007-2017 calibration window cannot see 2026-specific OPEC+ or shale-growth dynamics at all, so a calibration PASS here would necessarily rest on generic trend persistence in the window, not on this thesis, and only the 2018+ OOS gate can speak to the actual claim. (3) Geopolitical risk cuts the other way and is not mean-reverting on any fixed clock -- a renewed Hormuz disruption or a fresh regional escalation would flip the curve back to backwardation abruptly, which is exactly the kind of jump a 90-day trailing-return signal is slow to both catch and unwind from.

(2) By 2026-08-20 that decline had already been fully erased as yields rebounded (CNBC, 'Treasury yields rebound, wiping out the decline following Bessent's intervention'; Bloomberg, 'Bessent's plan at best circuit breaker for global bond slump'). (3) Bessent responded on 2026-08-21 by vowing to go even bigger. (4) By 2026-08-25 the 30yr had climbed back to 5.27% and reporting explicitly framed the prior intervention's effect as having 'lasted two days' (Universe News Network). (5) The week-of-8/24 Cboe Insights report -- already cited elsewhere in today's ledger for its MOVE/VXTLT data, cited here only for that same data, not reused as a second independent source -- shows the MOVE index and the VXTLT 20y-bond-vol index both turning back up over that same window, consistent with the stress still being live into this week rather than resolved by either intervention. WHY THIS FAVORS PERSISTENCE, MECHANICALLY: a move that a large, credible, repeatedly-announced official intervention cannot reverse for more than ~1-2 days is evidence the move is being driven by a slow-moving structural stock (accumulated fiscal deficits, net long-dated coupon supply, elevated term premium) rather than by a transient positioning imbalance that a buyback could plausibly absorb -- exactly the autocorrelated-repricing condition a trailing-sign trend rule needs, and a cleaner, more falsifiable version of that claim than an ex-ante supply argument alone, because it is based on the market's own revealed response to a real reversion attempt rather than on a forecast of one. PARAMETERS: lookback=60 (~1 quarter) is sized to span the run-up into and through this acute August episode (back to roughly early-to-mid June) without diluting it against the calmer stretch of H1 2026 further back; freq=W matches the roughly weekly cadence of the intervention/reversal pattern itself (each attempted circuit-breaker has been overturned within days, not hours), so a weekly rebalance tracks the episode's own clock rather than whipsawing on single-day intervention headlines a daily freq would chase. DISTINCTNESS: TLT has one prior single_asset_trend proposal in this ledger (rp_single_asset_trend_TLT_126, 2026-08-08, lookback 126/M) built on an ex-ante term-premium/quarterly-refunding-calendar argument dated before any buyback existed; IEF has a separate one (rp_single_asset_trend_IEF_147, 2026-08-19) built on a forward-guidance/communication-style argument for the belly of the curve. This proposal's mechanism -- revealed intervention failure over 2026-08-19/25, an event that postdates both prior proposals -- and its lookback (60) are both new; it does not dispute or lean on either prior verdict. HONESTY CAVEATS, worst first: (1) every trend variant tested in this lab is DEAD, including TLT and IEF themselves at other lookbacks, and changing the supporting evidence does not change the shape being tested or lower the bar. (2) The 'intervention failed twice' pattern is a sample size of two dated events, not a law -- a third, larger buyback operation (the doubled $4bn-plus program is scheduled to run 2026-09-09 through 2026-11-04) could yet succeed in reversing the move, which would argue against persistence going forward even though it has held so far. name: rp_static_spread_carry_DBC_QQQ_a
rationale: MECHANISM: static_spread_carry(ticker_a=DBC, ticker_b=QQQ, long_leg='a') is a fixed, always-on long DBC / short QQQ position -- a structural risk-premium bet on a persistent, dateable, non-price-based divergence between the two legs, not a forecast of either leg's near-term direction or a claim about any live strategy's recent results. STRUCTURAL CONDITION, NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM: the AI data-center buildout is currently producing two simultaneous, physically-linked but financially-decoupled effects, and this pair is built to harvest the gap between them rather than bet on either exposure alone. LEG 1 (DBC, long): copper -- one of DBC's industrial-metals weights alongside aluminum -- faces a widening physical deficit driven specifically by that buildout. Wood Mackenzie's 2026 forecast puts the deficit wider than 2025's already-record ~304,000 tonnes; other trackers estimate roughly 400,000 tonnes for 2026 as AI campuses (typically 50-150MW, at ~27-33 tonnes of copper per installed MW) draw down supply; and the IEA has flagged that existing and currently-planned mines can meet only about 70% of projected 2035 demand -- a structural, multi-year mine-supply rigidity, not a cyclical price spike. JPMorgan and UBS both revised 2026 copper price targets higher (toward $12,500-13,000/tonne) on the same mine-disruption-plus-AI-demand combination. LEG 2 (QQQ, short): the financial expression of the identical AI buildout is running well ahead of its monetization. The largest US hyperscalers are on pace for combined 2026 capex above $600bn (some sell-side estimates near $697bn for the top five, up ~$173bn since the start of the year alone) -- capex intensity near 23% of revenue, more than double pre-ChatGPT levels -- while 2026 research notes (Allianz; Guinness Global Investors) describe a widening gap between that infrastructure spend and actual enterprise monetization, with the Shiller CAPE having crossed 40 in 2025, a level reached only once before, immediately preceding the dot-com crash. QQQ is the vehicle carrying that capex-vs-monetization gap as embedded equity-multiple risk. The spread isolates the buildout's physical constraint (real, inelastic, supply-side) from its speculative equity-multiple expression (demand-side, monetization-dependent) -- both sides are dated, structural facts about the SAME underlying capital cycle, not a bet that commodities or tech have recently 'been working.' STATED RISK, not a caveat added after the fact: DBC is a diversified basket whose largest single block is still energy (Brent+WTI roughly 17%) with gold (~5.6%) and agriculture alongside copper/aluminum, so the pure copper deficit signal is diluted by unrelated curve moves in oil and softs; and QQQ could keep re-rating indefinitely if monetization catches up or if the market simply reads elevated capex as bullish forward revenue, in which case this spread loses on both legs simultaneously -- that is the hypothesis under test, not a hedge. Distinct from the existing DBC-legged static_spread_carry proposals in this ledger (USO/DBC roll-differential x2, GLD/DBC bullion-vs-futures roll differential, IEF/DBC belly-of-curve-vs-commodity-curve roll differential, SLV/DBC industrial-metals-vs-broad-commodity), none of which touch QQQ or the capex/monetization gap; and distinct from every existing QQQ pairing in this ledger (all pair_zscore or asset_class_trend_hedge, none a static structural carry bet).

MECHANISM, BALANCE-SHEET LEVEL: small-cap issuers carry a structurally different capital structure than mega-cap tech. Roughly a third of small-cap corporate debt is floating-rate and small-cap interest expense already consumes about 31% of EBITDA (RiverFront Investment Group, 'US Small-Cap... Lower Rates to the Rescue?', 2026), with a pandemic-era 'refinancing wall' of debt originally issued near 0-2% coming due in 2026 that must be rolled at the Fed's current 3.50-3.75% policy rate regardless of the cutting path (Yahoo Finance/247wallst, 'Will the Federal Reserve Crush the Small-Cap Stock Revival?', 2026-07-07). QQQ's mega-cap constituents are the mirror opposite by construction: they fund overwhelmingly from net cash balances or long-duration fixed-rate bonds locked in during the 2020-21 near-zero-rate window, so their financing costs are structurally insulated from near-term policy moves in a way small caps' floating-rate/short-duration liabilities are not. This is a mechanical, balance-sheet-composition argument about who pays more when short rates move, not a claim about which basket has recently outperformed.

MECHANISM, POLICY PATH: the Fed's own recent actions and internal split point toward continued near-term easing, which mechanically compresses small-cap financing costs disproportionately per the above. The FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% at its July 29, 2026 meeting but did so with a rare 9-3 dissent split, and July nonfarm payrolls -- published in early August -- fell by 23,000 against a forecast GAIN of 80,000, with a further 103,000 jobs erased from May/June revisions (Vantage Markets, 'US Dollar Index Falls to 98.55 as Yields Ease, Fed Splits', 2026-08-24). A committee this divided reacting to a labor-market print this weak is a structural signal about the near-term policy path, not a market-performance claim.

This is a snapshot valuation-gap fact, not a claim about which basket has been rising -- a wide, persistent discount alongside a structural financing-cost tailwind is the setup a genuine risk premium would produce, distinct from a momentum bet.

The lookback (110 trading days, ~5.5 months) is chosen to span the full 2026-03-18-to-today window over which the Fed's own forecast repriced -- not a round number, and not tuned to any known outcome for TLT itself. name: rp_single_asset_trend_VNQ_63

The case is that US listed real estate is currently mid-way through a MULTI-MONTH, gradual repricing process driven by an identifiable macro mechanism, which is exactly the Hong & Stein gradual-information-diffusion condition a trailing-sign rule is built to harvest -- not a one-shot news shock a trend rule cannot monetize. THE MECHANISM: REIT valuations are priced off the spread between dividend yield and the 10-year Treasury (the market's proxy cap rate), so REIT prices reprice gradually as that spread moves, not on any single print. TWO current, dated facts define the regime: (1) the Fed has cut three times since September 2025, taking the upper bound to 3.75% as of 2026-07-28 -- a multi-meeting, still-unfolding cutting cycle, not a completed one-off move; (2) the curve has been re-steepening at the same time -- the 10s2s spread widened from a 0.27% trough in June 2026 to roughly 0.39-0.45% now (late August 2026, sources differ slightly on the exact print but agree on direction and magnitude), while the 10-year itself has held in a 4.63-4.73% band. Multiple sources tied to this sector independently name the SAME two thresholds as the regime's hinge points: a sustained break above ~4.75% on the 10-year typically drives cap-rate expansion (REIT-negative, the same dynamic behind the 2022-2023 REIT drawdown), while a move back through ~4.25% restores VNQ's yield advantage over money-market cash and tends to pull allocator capital back into the sector -- i.e. the sector is currently sitting between two well-identified structural triggers, not drifting randomly, which is the condition under which a multi-week trailing-return rule has something non-random to track. WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM THE ONE PRIOR VNQ PROPOSAL: rp_single_asset_trend_VNQ_126 (2026-08-05, DEAD) cited a calendar-scheduled gradual-diffusion argument at a 6-month/monthly cadence; this proposal is grounded in the CURRENT rate-cut-cycle-plus-curve-steepening regime described above, not that prior thesis, and picks a materially different lookback/freq for a different reason: lookback=63 (~1 trading quarter) approximates the time since the curve's own June-2026 steepening turn, short enough to track the current regime rather than average across it and the 2025 hiking-era regime that preceded it; freq=W matches the FOMC's roughly 6-8-week meeting cadence (each cut is a discrete event the signal should be able to register within a few weeks, not average away at a monthly rebalance). NOT A REPROPOSAL: this exact name has never appeared in graveyard.csv or pipeline_ideas.csv. DECLARED HAZARD: VNQ is a diversified REIT basket spanning property types (industrial, data-center, residential, mortgage REITs) with heterogeneous rate sensitivity -- mortgage REITs in particular react to NIM (net interest margin) mechanics rather than cap-rate mechanics, which could add noise unrelated to the cap-rate thesis this proposal rests on. The pre-registered DSR/CPCV gate, not this rationale, decides ALIVE/DEAD.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_30_3
rationale: A concrete flow-fragility event just materialized in the last week of August 2026, and it is a structural/positioning argument, not a claim that reversal 'has been working': implied volatility across equities, rates and other asset classes spiked together after the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.33% intraweek -- its highest since 2007 -- forcing Treasury Secretary Bessent to intervene by doubling the size of the Treasury's long-bond buyback program to $4B per operation (CBOE Insights, 2026-08-24 weekly note). Citadel Securities' own flow analysis (published just before the spike) explicitly flagged that systematic deleveraging potential was 'elevated', with many CTA strategies 'approaching high exposure levels' and flow asymmetry 'skewed to the downside' -- i.e. the same momentum-chasing flows that pushed assets in one direction over the preceding weeks were positioned to amplify, not absorb, any reversal, and interest-rate vol (MOVE, VXTLT) was independently already climbing off its own multi-week lows into the event. This is the textbook precondition for a crowding-driven overshoot: a shock hits a market with one-sided, highly-levered positioning, produces an abrupt, flow-mechanical (not information-driven) price move, and a policy response (the buyback doubling) then removes the immediate trigger -- the setup in which a subsequent partial reversion is a structural, not a performance-chasing, expectation. cross_sectional_rank(metric='reversal') is the one primitive in this vocabulary built exactly for that shape: it ranks the full 15-ticker UNIVERSE -- spanning every asset class a multi-asset CTA book actually trades (equity, rates, commodity, real estate, currency) -- by trailing return and takes the opposite side of the most extreme recent movers, which is the right instrument for a crowding-driven, cross-asset overshoot rather than a single-pair or single-ticker mechanism. A 30-trading-day (~6 week) lookback is chosen to span the pre-spike low-vol grind that built the positioning through the spike itself, while still weighting the most recent extremes a reversal signal should fade; k=3 takes the top/bottom quintile of the 15-name universe, the same breadth already tested at other lookbacks (21, 126, 252) in this family. Weekly rebalancing matches the few-week decay this kind of flow-driven dislocation typically takes to resolve -- fast enough to catch the reversion, slow enough not to churn on daily noise while the shock is still working through the market. This exact (lookback=30, k=3) pair has not been proposed before (checked pipeline_ideas.csv), and 'reversal' is also this primitive's least-proposed metric to date (7 prior vs. 15 for momentum, 10 for low_vol), so this also broadens coverage of the pre-registered space rather than repeating the already-most-tested metric. These aren't two markets that happen to correlate; they are two prices set by the SAME driver (the sign of the US-vs-rest-of-DM policy gap) with OPPOSITE expected sign, exactly the offset asset_class_trend_hedge's own description requires, not an incidental correlation claim. A matched 126-trading-day (~6-month) lookback on both legs reflects that a single macro regime (the compressing policy differential) is the shared driver of both legs on the same horizon -- an asymmetric pairing would imply an unclaimed lead-lag relationship. Monthly rebalance matches a multi-month policy-repricing horizon rather than day-to-day FX/rates noise around individual data prints.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_VNQ_HYG_a

NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM: nothing here asserts that SPY, HYG, equities or credit have recently done well or badly -- the claim is about how richly credit RISK is currently PRICED, a spread level, not a return. THE CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION: as of August 2026 the ICE BofA US High Yield option-adjusted spread sits at roughly 2.73-2.81 percentage points, in the richest (tightest) decile of its full history against a long-run median near 450bps -- comparable in tightness only to brief windows like early 2024 and pre-2007/2020 complacency peaks. This compression is broad-based rather than a high-yield-specific distortion: investment-grade trades at 81bps and BBBs at 100bps, putting the HY/IG ratio near 3.5x, roughly its long-run average -- i.e. the whole credit-risk term structure is priced tight together, not high-yield alone decoupling from IG. MECHANISM: an OAS is compensation, over a duration-matched Treasury, for bearing default, downgrade and liquidity/tail risk on the issuer -- when that spread compresses to a historical extreme, the marginal compensation embedded in HYG for bearing those risks is close to its historical floor. SPY's equity risk premium is a economically DIFFERENT compensation (expected earnings growth plus dividend yield over the risk-free rate) that is not mechanically arbitraged by the same OAS-spread channel, so a credit cycle that has priced away most of its own risk premium says nothing about whether the equity premium has done the same. Financing a long-SPY position with a short-HYG leg is a bet that, structurally, SPY's un-compressed equity premium is the better-compensated place to hold risk right now than HYG's compressed credit premium -- a persistent positioning tilt, not a forecast that credit spreads must imminently widen. PARAMETERS: freq=M because an OAS is a slow-moving macro-cycle variable (default-rate expectations, issuance/demand technicals, Fed policy) that updates over weeks-to-months, not daily noise -- a finer freq would only pay turnover. HAZARD, stated honestly: tight spreads can stay tight for a long time ("priced for perfection" is a condition, not a trigger), and in a genuine risk-off shock SPY and HYG are both plausibly hit together -- this is a risk-premium tilt, not a hedge, and the pre-registered DSR/CPCV gate decides ALIVE/DEAD, not this rationale. name: rp_pair_zscore_SPY_TLT_65_2p0_4p5

MECHANISM: which sign the stock-bond correlation takes is not random -- it is set by the TYPE of shock driving markets. Demand shocks and flight-to-quality episodes produce the classic NEGATIVE correlation (bonds rally as stocks fall); monetary-policy shocks and inflation surprises instead produce POSITIVE correlation (both react to the same rate news in the same direction) -- a distinction Oxford Economics uses explicitly to argue correlation stays positive through 2026 because 'continued supply shocks, geopolitical risk, and higher macro volatility from activist fiscal policy' will keep monetary-policy-type shocks dominant rather than letting the 2026 dovish-Fed-cut repricing (itself a monetary shock) fade into a demand-shock regime. Corroborating, dated evidence that this is the CURRENT regime, not a 2026 forecast alone: stock-bond correlation was pushed to roughly 0.75 by 2022's rate shock and 'volatility has since receded while the correlation hasn't' -- i.e. the elevated co-movement has persisted for years past its original shock, and coverage as of June 2026 confirms stocks and bonds 'have been moving in tandem for much of the past several months,' prompting advisors to question whether TLT can still diversify a SPY position the way it used to (Nationwide Financial, June 2026). Weekly freq matches this primitive's own dominant precedent (21 of 32 prior pair_zscore proposals used W) and a catalyst cadence that is week-to-week, not intraday. HONEST CAVEAT: a positive-correlation regime is a reason to expect the SPY/TLT spread to behave differently than the classic 2007-2017 'flight to Treasuries' era few of this UNIVERSE's other pairs were built around -- it does NOT by itself guarantee the spread mean-reverts rather than drifts (a sustained fiscal or inflation shock could still push both legs' relative pricing in one direction for a long stretch), and this is a bet on relative spread behavior only, not a claim SPY or TLT outperforms; the pre-registered DSR/CPCV gate decides ALIVE/DEAD, not this rationale. name: rp_curve_carry_95
rationale: STRUCTURAL YIELD-CURVE CONDITION, NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM: the 2s10s spread came out of the longest sustained inversion in the FRED data series (July 2022 to late 2024, ~27 months) and has been RE-STEEPENING since, now positive (~0.51pp, ~58th percentile, +13.3% over the trailing 12 months) but still well short of a clean upward slope. The move is not a slow drift -- it is currently a BEAR steepener, i.e. driven by the long end selling off, not the front end rallying: in the week of Jul 27-31 2026 the 1y yield eased 4.14%->4.08% and the 2y eased 4.31%->4.28%, while the 30y SURGED 5.12%->5.27%. MECHANISM: the front end is pricing Fed cuts (the Jul 28-29 FOMC held 3.50-3.75% but Chair Powell told Jackson Hole "the time has come for policy to adjust" after July payrolls -- released Aug 7 -- showed nonfarm payrolls falling 23,000 with unemployment only ticking down to 4.1% via labor-force exits), while the long end is facing a SEPARATE, opposing pressure -- term-premium/fiscal-supply concerns that keep 10y+ yields elevated even as the policy rate falls. Two distinct drivers pulling DGS10-DGS2 the SAME direction (steeper) is a structurally different setup from either driver acting alone, and is exactly the condition curve_carry is built to trade: a DV01-neutral TLT/IEF position that trend-follows the real DGS10-DGS2 slope, so it earns on continued steepening from EITHER leg (front-end cuts or long-end term-premium repricing) without taking outright duration risk. lookback=95 (~4.5 months of trading days) spans back through the Jackson Hole/payrolls-driven acceleration without still being anchored to the pre-2024 inversion regime; W rebalance matches this primitive's established convention (22 of its 30 prior proposals used W) since curve-slope moves are gradual and a daily clock would just trade the DV01-neutral construction against its own hedge noise. curve_carry has the fewest total proposals of any primitive in this ledger (30, vs 32-37 for the other five) and this specific lookback has not been tried before. Explicitly not a claim that trend-following on the curve works -- this lab's own record on curve_carry so far is 8/8 DEAD -- only a claim that the CURRENT curve dynamic (two independent forces steepening it at once) is a cleaner-than-usual match for what this primitive mechanically tests.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_TLT_20

name: rp_curve_carry_32
rationale: STRUCTURAL SETUP, NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM: this is about the front-end-driven bear-steepening channel itself, not about how curve_carry or any related book has performed. FRONT-END REPRICING, EVENT BY EVENT. The July 28-29 2026 FOMC held the target range at 3.50-3.75% but recorded a genuine three-way hawkish dissent (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan voting for a hike) -- the first three-way dissent since September 2016. Two weeks later, the July payrolls report (released Aug 7) showed nonfarm payrolls falling 23,000 with unemployment ticking down only via labor-force exits, which briefly repriced the front end toward cuts. Then, at Jackson Hole on Aug 28, new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reversed that read: he gave an explicitly more hawkish inflation assessment than his own July post-meeting remarks, said this summer's encouraging prints don't show 'meaningful' improvement, and recommitted to the 2% PCE target as the Fed's main focus. Fed-funds-futures hike odds for the Sept 16 FOMC jumped from roughly 36% pre-Jackson-Hole to 60-68% within days (CME FedWatch per CNBC/Reuters reporting), while traders separately priced roughly 70% odds of at least one hike by December as Middle-East-driven oil prices keep headline inflation elevated. THE CURVE DATA. Over the same span the slope has been widening, not narrowing: 2s10s was ~35bp on 2026-07-10, ~37bp on 2026-07-17 (both pre-dissent), ~39bp on 2026-08-28 (the Jackson Hole print), and ~41bp on 2026-09-01 (10y 4.81% / 2y 4.40%) -- a modest but directionally consistent bear steepener running alongside this front-end repricing sequence. This is a claim about the SLOPE variable's recent path, not about any strategy's returns, and curve_carry's own direction is mechanical (sign of the trailing slope change), never chosen by me. WHY THIS CALLS FOR A SHORT LOOKBACK, DIFFERENT FROM THE EXISTING rp_curve_carry_126 PROPOSAL. rp_curve_carry_126 (pre-registered 2026-08-08) argued for a long, ~6-month window because its thesis was the SLOW channel: term premium as a stock that reprices over a full quarterly refunding cycle. This proposal is about the opposite, FAST channel: front-end policy expectations discovering a new, more hawkish reaction function under a new chair, moving in discrete jumps around scheduled FOMC meetings and data prints -- exactly the '~6-week FOMC cadence, ~32 trading days' the 126-day proposal itself named as the jumpy channel's clock, and singled out as too short a window for ITS OWN (term-premium) thesis. lookback=32 targets that cadence directly: long enough to span one full FOMC cycle end-to-end (the July 28-29 meeting sits roughly at the far edge of this window as of today), short enough that the signal is dominated by the event sequence just described rather than by the quarterly refunding/term-premium process the 126-day version already covers. freq=W, matching the primitive's dominant convention (25/33 prior curve_carry proposals) and appropriate for a ~32-day-window signal: fast enough to catch a sign flip within days without paying daily two-leg turnover on a position that should flip only a handful of times a year. WEAKNESSES, WORST FIRST, STATED BEFORE ANY VERDICT. (1) Every trend-following strategy this lab has tested on PRICE data is DEAD (tsmom, green_line, family L, the donchian_gen_* factory sweep) -- this only changes the INPUT to yield-curve data, not the sign-of-trailing-change SHAPE, and the burden is entirely on the input differing in kind, which is unproven. (2) The move described (35bp -> 41bp) is small in absolute terms and could reverse on a single dovish print between now and the Sept 16 FOMC -- a short lookback is more exposed to that kind of single-print whipsaw than the 126-day version. name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_VNQ_LQD_65_21
rationale: TWO INDEPENDENT, CURRENT CATALYSTS -- NOT A CORRELATION SEARCH, NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM: asset_class_trend_hedge needs each leg's OWN trailing-return sign to be driven by its own live mechanism, not a shared story dressed up as two tickers. VNQ (real_estate) and LQD (rates, per this primitive's ASSET_CLASS map) satisfy the mechanical different-asset-class requirement. LEG A, VNQ -- THE CAP-RATE/REFINANCING CHANNEL: REIT valuations are mechanically set by cap rate = risk-free rate + spread, and REIT balance sheets carry real, near-term refinancing exposure to the level of long rates, not just a directional preference for low rates. The US 10-year Treasury yield closed at ~4.80-4.81% on 2026-09-01, its highest level since January 2025 (TradingEconomics, US 10-Year Government Bond Yield, accessed 2026-09-02), driven by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's 2026-08-28 Jackson Hole remarks sharpening the inflation warning and reviving hike odds for the September 16 FOMC from roughly 36% pre-speech to 60-70% within days (CNBC, 'Kevin Warsh sharpens inflation warning at Jackson Hole, signaling possible rate hike', 2026-08-28; Forbes, 'Forecast: Fed To Hike Interest Rates After Warsh's Jackson Hole Talk', 2026-08-28). That is a direct, mechanical repricing of REIT discount rates and refinancing costs today, not a forecast about where VNQ 'has been going.' LEG B, LQD -- THE CREDIT-MARKET SUPPLY-TECHNICAL CHANNEL, DELIBERATELY NOT JUST DURATION: if this leg were only 'LQD is long-duration so it falls when rates rise,' it would be the same mechanism as VNQ's and would fail this primitive's own different-mechanism requirement. The distinct, current catalyst is a SUPPLY/TECHNICAL one: US investment-grade issuance for September 2026 is expected in a $175-250bn range (investmentgrade.com, '2026 Investment Grade Bond Statistics'), landing on top of spreads already sitting near their tightest levels since before the financial crisis -- option-adjusted spreads around 77-81bp over Treasuries (Breckinridge Capital Advisors, Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 Corporate Bond Market Outlook notes). A heavy new-issue calendar hitting historically rich secondary spreads is a classic indigestion/concession setup -- dealers and real-money accounts absorbing large primary supply typically demand concessions that pressure secondary-market prices independent of the rate level itself. That is a corporate-bond-market plumbing mechanism, not a real-estate operating-economics one, even though both legs sit under the same 'hawkish-for-longer' macro umbrella. TODAY'S CONFIRMING SIGNAL: broad risk-off on 2026-09-02, with the VIX up over 9% intraday alongside the 10-year holding its cycle-high yield and the Dollar Index at 99.65 (Bloomberg, 'Stock Market Today: Dow, S&P Live Updates for September 2', 2026-09-01; Charles Schwab, 'Crude, Yields Flex Muscle, Bruising Stocks Early') -- the same hawkish-repricing backdrop both legs' catalysts sit inside, active as of today rather than a stale multi-week-old read. PARAMETERS: lookback_a=65 (~3 months) spans the full arc from the July 28-29 FOMC dissent through the Jackson Hole repricing to today, matching VNQ's catalyst's own timescale. lookback_b=21 (~1 month) is deliberately short and specific to LQD's catalyst, which is a September-issuance-calendar phenomenon, not a multi-quarter one -- a 65-day window on the credit leg would mostly average in August's much quieter supply backdrop and dilute the signal this leg is actually about. freq=W matches this primitive's typical cadence elsewhere in the ledger and avoids paying daily two-leg turnover on a combination that should only flip a handful of times over the relevant horizon. WEAKNESSES, WORST FIRST: (1) VNQ and LQD as a PAIR have already been tested in this ledger, via pair_zscore(VNQ, LQD, 84, 2.0, 4.0) -- DEAD in graveyard.csv (DSR/CPCV fail). That was a mean-reversion bet on a public-vs-private real-estate valuation gap closing, a genuinely different mechanism from this trend-following, independent-legs proposal, but it is the closest prior evidence in this ledger and is stated up front rather than omitted. (2) Both legs share obvious, unavoidable common exposure to the general level of long-term interest rates -- this primitive's own calibration-window guard (|corr| of the two legs' trend signals capped at 0.3 over 2007-2017) exists exactly to catch a hedge that is really one duration bet wearing two tickers, and given how correlated 'both hurt by higher-for-longer' sounds, there is a real chance this combination fails that mechanical check regardless of the separate-mechanism argument above -- the check decides this, not the rationale. (3) The 77-81bp IG OAS figure is the same data point already cited in this ledger's earlier (DEAD) VNQ/LQD pair_zscore proposal; only the September issuance-calendar catalyst and the trend-not-reversion framing are new here. (4) Every price-trend-based primitive tested in this lab so far is DEAD (tsmom, green_line, family L, donchian_gen_*, and most prior asset_class_trend_hedge rows) -- the burden is entirely on these two specific, current catalysts mattering enough to produce genuine multi-week trend persistence, which is unproven and decided only by the OOS gate.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_25_3
rationale: STRUCTURAL MICROSTRUCTURE EVENT, NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM: cross_sectional_rank's reversal metric (score = -(trailing return)) only needs today's cross-asset move to be a genuine, dated OVERREACTION/liquidity-driven dispersion event that the short-horizon contrarian literature (Jegadeesh 1990, 'Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns'; Lehmann 1990, 'Fads, Martingales, and Market Efficiency') documents partially unwinding over the following days-to-weeks -- this is not a claim that reversal 'has been working,' and this proposal takes no view on which specific tickers end up long or short; the metric's own sign does that mechanically from the data. THE REGIME TRANSITION, DATED. The VIX printed its 2026 LOW of 14.2 on 2026-08-17 (CNBC, 'VIX: Wall Street's fear gauge hits 2026 low -- here's why'), a multi-week complacency stretch. That regime broke abruptly at the start of September: US equities opened the month with a broad, cross-asset sell-off as renewed Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz hostilities sent oil sharply higher and reignited a GLOBAL bond sell-off, pushing Treasury yields to fresh multi-month highs (Motley Fool, 'Stock Market Midday, Sept. 1: Stocks Slide on Global Bond Sell-Off', 2026-09-01); the US VIX was up further intraday on 2026-09-02 on top of that already-elevated base (Charles Schwab, 'Crude, Yields Flex Muscle, Bruising Stocks Early', 2026-09-01/09-02 -- the same VIX-spike read already cited in today's rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_VNQ_LQD_65_21 proposal in this ledger). THE DISPERSION, NOT JUST THE LEVEL: tech and other rate-sensitive growth names led the market lower while energy was the lone bright spot as crude spiked (Motley Fool, ibid) -- a textbook FORCED/liquidity-driven dispersion shock (a discrete geopolitical trigger hitting a market positioned for calm) rather than a slow fundamental re-rating, which is exactly the shape of move short-horizon reversal is built to harvest, not multi-month trend. A SEPARATE, INDEPENDENT CONFIRMING STRAND: Japan's 10-year JGB yield hit 3% for the first time in three decades over the same Sept 1-2 window, on fiscal worries, a weak yen, and BOJ rate-hike prospects, with Treasury Secretary Bessent reportedly saying BOJ Governor Ueda would 'do the right thing' to prop up the yen (TradingEconomics, 'Japanese Shares Mixed on Hawkish BOJ Signals', 2026-09-02 coverage) -- a second, geographically distinct source of the same 'quiet-regime cracking at once, on a discrete trigger' pattern, not one shock read twice. WHY REVERSAL, NOT MOMENTUM/TREND, AND WHY NOW: every trend/momentum primitive tested in this lab is DEAD (tsmom, green_line, family L, donchian_gen_*, and the momentum-metric cross_sectional_rank rows already in graveyard.csv), and this proposal does not relitigate that -- it is a genuinely different, shorter-horizon mechanism (post-shock overreaction unwind) that this ledger has barely tested: of the 9 prior cross_sectional_rank proposals using the reversal metric, none has yet reached a graveyard.csv verdict, versus many already-DEAD momentum and low_vol rows -- reversal is this primitive's least-explored corner by verdict count, not just by proposal count (16 momentum / 11 low_vol / 9 reversal proposed to date). PARAMETER CHOICE: lookback=25 (~5 trading weeks) is sized to span back through the Aug 17 VIX-low complacency stretch and capture the full Sept 1-2 regime break within the window, short enough that the signal is dominated by this specific shock rather than diluted by a longer, unrelated past regime -- a new point in the pre-registered range, distinct from the 9 lookbacks already proposed (20, 21, 30, 42, 50, 126, 252). k=3 (top-3/bottom-3 of 15) matches this primitive's most common convention elsewhere in the ledger rather than an untested extreme. freq=W matches this metric's dominant convention (4 of 9 prior reversal proposals) and suits a signal meant to capture a days-to-weeks unwind without paying daily two-sided turnover on a shock that should resolve within the window, not every session. DECLARED HAZARDS, WORST FIRST: (1) the shock could simply be the start of a durable regime change (a genuine hawkish Fed/BOJ tightening cycle plus a live Hormuz war) rather than an overreaction that reverts -- if so this reversal bet is wrong in the same direction a trend bet would be right, and only the OOS gate decides which. (2) A 25-day lookback spanning both the calm pre-shock stretch and the shock itself may dilute the signal relative to a purely post-shock window; this tradeoff (enough history for a stable cross-sectional rank vs. isolating the event) is unresolved by me and left to the calibration/OOS gate. (3) This whole primitive family (cross-sectional rank/momentum) is already DEAD in this lab under the momentum metric -- the burden is entirely on the reversal metric's different, shorter-horizon mechanism actually differing in kind, which is unproven and decided only by DSR/CPCV, not by this rationale.
