name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_IWM_LQD_30_60
rationale: STRUCTURAL SETUP, NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM: this is about a specific rate-sensitivity channel that is currently live for small-cap equities, not about how any book or strategy has traded. THE MECHANISM LINKING THE TWO LEGS. IWM (Russell 2000) and LQD (investment-grade corporate bonds) are both structurally short duration/rates, but through different, nameable channels: LQD mechanically loses value as yields rise (straightforward bond-duration effect on a long-duration IG book). IWM is exposed through a refinancing-cost channel that is unusually acute right now -- Russell 2000 constituents carry about 32% floating-rate debt versus roughly 6% for the S&P 500, face a reported $368B 2026 debt maturity wall of low-rate-era issuance rolling over near 6.5% against 1-2% legacy coupons, and an estimated 41-46% of index constituents cannot cover interest expense from operating income ('zombie' share) -- so a rates-up surprise raises IWM's discount-rate AND its debt-service burden simultaneously, a double channel LQD doesn't share, while the direction both react to is the same one. One analysis of this exposure states the condition plainly: the debt wall is survivable only 'as long as the Fed is cutting and the 10-year is drifting lower... if either of those assumptions breaks, the math gets ugly quickly.' THAT ASSUMPTION IS CURRENTLY BREAKING, EVENT BY EVENT, NOT AS A TRADING-PERFORMANCE CLAIM. The Jul 28-29 FOMC held rates but recorded a three-way hawkish dissent (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan voting for a hike) -- first three-way dissent since Sept 2016. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh then hardened that read at Jackson Hole (Aug 28): a more hawkish inflation assessment than his own July remarks, explicitly no 'meaningful' improvement in recent prints, recommitting to the 2% PCE target. CME FedWatch-tracked odds of a Sept 16 hike jumped from roughly 36% pre-Jackson-Hole to the 55-66% range within days (CNBC/Reuters reporting), and the 10-year has NOT drifted lower -- it sits at 4.81% on 2026-09-01 versus 2y at 4.40% (2s10s ~41bp, wider than the ~35-37bp seen in mid-July, a modest bear-steepener). The dollar index is likewise firmer (~99.5-99.7, a two-week high) on the same hawkish repricing. Every piece of that chain -- the dissent, the payrolls-driven wobble on Aug 7 that briefly reversed and then got overridden by Jackson Hole, the FedWatch jump, the curve not cooperating -- is a structural/rates-path fact, not a claim about what any strategy has earned. WHY lookback_a (IWM) = 30, SHORTER than lookback_b (LQD) = 60: the refinancing-cost channel is driven by fast-moving, event-clustered repricing (three FOMC-adjacent events in six weeks), so a short trailing window is needed to catch IWM's reaction to the current cluster without averaging it into the unrelated small-cap rally earlier this year (Russell 2000 hit record highs in H1 2026 on an unrelated soft-landing/Fed-cutting narrative per financialcontent.com reporting -- exactly the regime this setup argues is now reversing). LQD's duration effect is a smoother, more continuous function of the level and trend of yields, so a longer window (60d) spanning the full post-Jul-28 repricing arc is the more appropriate matched horizon for that leg. IWM and LQD have not been proposed together in this pipeline before (checked against pipeline_ideas.csv and graveyard.csv: no IWM_LQD or LQD_IWM row exists in either), though the individual rate-sensitivity legs discussed here appear independently: graveyard.csv already carries HYG_IWM (rp_pair_zscore_HYG_IWM_90_2p25_4p5, DEAD) citing the same debt-wall dynamic from a mean-reversion angle, and IWM_TLT / IWM_UUP asset_class_trend_hedge variants exist with different partner legs and different lookbacks -- this proposal is a distinct partner leg (LQD, not TLT/UUP) chosen because IG credit duration is the cleanest single-mechanism match to the rates-up thesis without HYG's own credit-spread-compression noise (HY OAS is separately sitting at ~275-281bp, in the richest decile of its own history, per Convex/CME-adjacent reporting -- a live risk-premium fact about HYG specifically that would confound rather than clarify a pure rates-duration hedge).

rationale: PRIMITIVE CHOICE: breadth check as of this run -- single_asset_trend 40, cross_sectional_rank 38, static_spread_carry 37, asset_class_trend_hedge 36, pair_zscore 36, curve_carry 35 uses in pipeline_ideas.csv (all six within a narrow 35-40 band, so no primitive is heavily under-represented right now); asset_class_trend_hedge is picked here because it is the mechanism that fits today's actual research finding, not to correct an imbalance. MECHANISM: asset_class_trend_hedge holds two INDEPENDENT single_asset_trend legs (own trailing-return sign, own lookback) in one candidate; it only earns its place as a hedge, rather than two bets on one factor wearing one name, if each leg has its own live, nameable catalyst. ticker_a=EEM (equity) and ticker_b=UUP (currency) satisfy the mechanical different-asset-class requirement. THE MECHANISM LINKING THE TWO LEGS, NOT A CORRELATION SEARCH: UUP is a direct long-dollar position. EEM's USD-reported return embeds the dollar structurally and doubly -- EM sovereigns/corporates carry meaningful dollar-denominated debt whose real service burden rises exactly when the dollar strengthens, and dollar strength tightens the global dollar-funding conditions EM issuers depend on (Rey (2013) 'global financial cycle'; Bruno & Shin (2015) cross-border dollar-funding channel). A genuine, sustained move in the dollar should therefore show up with OPPOSITE sign in UUP's own trend and EEM's own trend -- the offsetting relationship this primitive requires, driven by a named channel, not an observed correlation. CURRENT STRUCTURAL EVENT, DATED, NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM ABOUT EEM, UUP, OR ANY LIVE STRATEGY: this exact pair was proposed once before in this ledger, on 2026-08-14 (rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_EEM_UUP_147_42), but the dollar-driver regime it described has since flipped. EM equities' 2025-2026 run (EEM +52.6% trailing 12-month return per an April 2026 Yahoo Finance snapshot) was built substantially on a WEAK dollar -- the dollar's sharpest annual decline in eight years during 2025 per market commentary -- which eased EM dollar-debt service and pulled in foreign flows. That weak-dollar tailwind has been reversing since Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Aug 28 2026 Jackson Hole speech: the 2-year Treasury yield jumped over 12bp intraday to 4.356% on his hawkish remarks, September-hike odds priced into fed funds futures rose from about 56% to 60.4% per CME FedWatch (CNBC, Aug 31 2026), and the Dollar Index (DXY) has since climbed back above the mid-99 handle to around 99.7, its firmest level in weeks (FXStreet, Sep 1-2 2026). This is a genuine reversal in the SIGN of the dollar's own trend, not merely a continuation of an existing move -- exactly the kind of regime inflection a trend-following signal on each leg separately should register once it has had a few weeks to diffuse through EEM's price (Hong & Stein (1999) gradual-information-diffusion), rather than something a single correlation snapshot would show. LOOKBACK CHOICE: lookback_b=30 (UUP) is short enough to pick up the dollar's own trend flip, which is under two weeks old as of this proposal, without waiting for it to round-trip through a much longer window; lookback_a=40 (EEM) is somewhat longer, reflecting that the equity leg's repricing should lag the FX/rates leg by design under the transmission channel above. Both stay inside the primitive's pre-registered [20, 252] range, and this (lookback_a, lookback_b) combination has not been proposed for EEM/UUP before -- only 147/42, predating this regime shift, exists in the ledger.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_HYG_IEF_b
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM: static_spread_carry is a fixed, always-on long-short with no timing/mean-reversion mechanism, so this only needs the CURRENT relative pricing of credit risk versus duration-safe Treasury exposure to reflect a genuine, persisting regime rather than a one-print blip -- same shape as this lab's surviving crypto-funding-carry primitive, a structural risk premium, not a forecast. THE DATA, DATED AND UNUSED IN THIS LEDGER BEFORE TODAY: CME FedWatch puts the probability of a 25bp hike at the Sept 16, 2026 FOMC meeting at 66% as of 2026-08-31 (Forbes, 'CME FedWatch Provides A 66% Chance Fed Will Hike Rates In September') -- a reversal to a RESUMED tightening posture, not a pause, driven by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's own public characterization of PCE inflation as 'concerning' at 3.7% y/y (4.1% over the trailing 6 months annualized), both well above the 2% target. AT THE SAME TIME: investment-grade corporate spreads entered 2026 at ~77bp OAS over Treasuries (ICE BofA US Corporate Index, via Schwab's '2026 Corporate Credit Outlook' and American Century's 'What Might 2026 Hold for U.S. Corporate Bonds?'), a level not sustained since the pre-2008-crisis era, even as gross IG issuance is projected to top $2T in 2026 (up from $1.7T in 2025; Q1 2026 alone was the largest quarterly total since Q2 2020), a record technical supply overhang financing AI-infrastructure capex. THE MECHANISM FOR THE SPREAD, NOT JUST EACH LEG SEPARATELY: a resumed hiking cycle raises the risk-free discount rate and historically coincides with credit-spread widening as financing costs rise faster than default-risk repricing catches up, while record supply adds a technical overhang on top of a starting spread already near a two-decade tight -- an asymmetric setup where credit has structurally more room to cheapen than to compress further. HYG (high-yield, the most spread-sensitive slice of UNIVERSE's credit exposure) as the short leg against IEF (intermediate Treasury duration, no credit exposure) as the long leg isolates that credit-vs-duration-safety spread specifically, without taking the outright rates-direction view a TLT leg would add. Never proposed for this ticker pair before -- HYG/LQD (both credit) and HYG/TLT (credit vs. long duration) are already mined in this ledger; HYG/IEF (credit vs. intermediate, less rate-volatile duration) is not.
